text:
The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence. Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools. For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes. We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.

text:
There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

$TWINE 1.05m dyor

0xe27501d787d647cc82a5b4a7eafd5750386f1b77

okx wallet:https://t.co/BKQ70pnO4Q

A cross-chain launchpad.

The same token is launched on two chains at the exact same time: one on Solana through Pump, and one on Robinhood Chain through Pons. Each side follows its own bonding curve and order book.

In the middle, there is a market maker holding inventory on both sides. If the market cap on one chain leads by more than 5%, it sells on the higher-priced side and buys on the lower-priced side, pushing the price gap back toward parity.

The creator rewards from both sides flow back to this market maker, allowing the “mirror” to fund itself.

The platform’s stated goal is to have the market caps on both chains track each other and remain within the 5% green zone.

Simply put, it is:Simultaneous dual-chain launch + auction presale + a market maker that claims to maintain a 5% spread + creator fees from both sides flowing back into the system.

text: 数学家是人，纺织女工是不是人？
author: RR_hodl
quoted_text:
数学家哭了。

字面意义上的哭了，康奈尔大学数学系教授、知名科普作家斯蒂芬·斯特罗加茨（Steven Strogatz）在接受《WIRED》采访时，谈及过去一周人工智能在数学领域取得的突飞猛进，忍不住当场落泪。

“科学本身令人振奋，”这位67岁的老教授坦言，“但在它背后，伴随着太多人类难以承受的不适与痛苦。”

触发这场情绪海啸的，是过去数周内接连上演的 AI 算力奇迹。OpenAI 刚刚宣布动用数万个智能体，攻克了拥有百万美元悬赏、困扰数学界近百年的纳维-斯托克斯（Navier-Stokes）方程相关难题；而就在此前不久，Anthropic 旗下的 Claude 也在形式化费马大定理证明的过程中，一口气完成了 29,500 个微定理的证明。在斯特罗加茨看来，2026 年注定是一个分水岭——它要么是数学界的“奇迹年”（annus mirabilis），要么就是彻底颠覆学者生存根基的“大厄之年”（annus horribilis）。

更让学界感到刺痛的，是顶尖学者心境的幻灭。斯特罗加茨的新书合著者、数学家亚历克斯·汤森（Alex Townsend）在采访中吐露了同样的绝望。即便他此前刚刚借助 AI 解决了一个困扰数十年的数值线性代数难题，但他却毫无登顶的喜悦，反而深感被时代抛弃：“我为数学研究奉献了整整 15 年，恰好在事业最成熟、个人能力最巅峰的时刻，突然发现那个所谓的‘巅峰’已不再属于我——某种东西已经超越了我。以前你站在知识的最前沿，如今站在前沿的成了 AI 智能体，你只是个操作员。这种落差让人感到切切实实的威胁。”

伴随这场算力风暴而来的，还有现实利益驱动下的名誉争夺。OpenAI 宣称取得重大进展的纳维-斯托克斯相关解法，很快便卷入了学术首创权的争议风波中：纽约大学数学家特里斯坦·巴克马斯特（Tristan Buckmaster）等人早已在该方向深耕并发表了极其接近的关键成果，而商业实验室在巨额 IPO 前夕竞相利用数万智能体横扫长线难题、抢占新闻头条的做法，让纯粹的科学探索染上了浓厚的资本竞赛色彩。

面对这种不可逆的浪潮，斯特罗加茨将当下的数学界比作“一部正在步步逼近的恐怖片”。对于人类数学家的未来，他指出了几层尤为残酷的现实：

登顶动机的永久丧失：过去驱动顶尖学者甘坐数十年冷板凳的，是“成为第一个登上无人涉足之山峰”的纯粹野心。如今，当机器每一次都能抢先登顶，这种攀登的动机将被彻底粉碎。
退守为“二流的爱好者”：数学或许会退化为如同当下的国际象棋或业余网球——人类棋手早已下不过顶级引擎，却依旧享受对弈的乐趣。但斯特罗加茨说，若数学最终沦为人类自娱自乐的游戏，社会与高校又凭什么继续投入重金，雇佣大批耗费数十年训练的人类学者去从事早已被机器替代的推演？
最后的阵地与意义的消解：在人类彻底失去理解能力之前，数学家或许暂时还能扮演“证明消化者”（proof digestors）的角色，将机器生成的冰冷证明转译为人类心智能够理解的语言，抑或担任数学审美与品味的裁判。但面对不知疲倦、持续进化的庞大系统，这一道防线被突破也只是时间问题。

纯粹数学（Pure Math）正处于一场毁灭与重塑的交汇点。它一方面带来了前所未有的普惠与民主化，打破了传统象牙塔的高耸门槛；但另一方面，它也在迅速剥离几百年来人类学者赖以立足的智力尊严。正如斯特罗加茨在采访最后所警示的那样，数学界或许只是最先遭遇这场洪流的阵地：“我们正在失去人类理解的边缘试探。数学是全人类的第一块试验田，而我们，可能正是那只提前为全人类鸣响警报的金丝雀。”

I just bought a new Model Y and can confidently say cars and Teslas are no longer the same product.

A car is like a pony or horse. I still like driving a stick shift, it’s fun! 

Tesla with FSD is a transportation robot. 

I had one of the first Model 3s in 2017. FSD was basically slightly better cruise control. Great on the highway. But honestly felt oversold. 

So I have been driving a BMW for the past 3 years. Great horse, fun to drive. 

But tried FSD recently and holy shit — it’s a personal Waymo. Works perfectly. I just went to the Fremont factory to get my new car, entered my address 30+ mins away, pushed a button, and got home without doing a thing. 

I don’t think most people realize how good this is, probably because they only experienced an early version previously. This is 1000x better. Metaphor for AI writ large. Like trying GPT 3.5 and thinking it’s cute and hallucinates, and dismissing it…while Astra launches in 2026 and is orders of magnitude more capable.

text:
Anthropic 最近嘴上在谈 AI 减速，手里却又被扒出一张 137 亿美元的算力大单，而收钱的这家公司，资本关系相当魔幻。

The Information 最新披露，RUM Group 此前一直没有公布名字的 137 亿美元 GPU 客户，就是 Anthropic。

这笔合同其实 8 月 23 日就已经出现在 RUM 的 SEC 文件里：6 年、137 亿美元，分三批购买佐治亚州 Maysville 数据中心的 GPU 服务。第三批还要等客户确认交付日期。

作为客户，Anthropic 最多可以用 每股 0.01 美元的价格买下 5080.8 万股 RUM A 类股票。前一半权证跟这 137 亿美元的三批采购挂钩，剩下一半要继续追加算力订单才能拿。按 RUM 当时约 2.76 亿股 A 类流通股粗算，这个权证规模相当于现有股本的 18% 左右。

所以这已经很难当成一张普通的云计算采购单来看。Anthropic 买的不只是 GPU，还顺手拿了一张 RUM 股价上涨的巨大看涨期权。

然后再看卖方是谁。

RUM Group 就是原来的 Rumble。收购 Northern Data 后，母公司改名 RUM Group，算力业务现在叫 Quake AI；Rumble 的云基础设施还在给特朗普的 Truth Social 提供服务。

另一边，Tether 在 9 月最新提交的 13D 里申报，其持有及可转换获得的 RUM A 类股票合计约 2.615 亿股，beneficial ownership 达到 50.3%。

最离谱的细节还在后面。

RUM 自己在 SEC 文件里承认为，了履行这张 137 亿美元合同，它还得建数据中心、买大量 GPU，但目前根本没有拿到足够的项目融资，之后准备继续举债或者发股票。问题是，合同并没有融不到钱就不干了的退出条件。

The Information 此前估算，Anthropic 过去不到一年签下的潜在算力承诺已经高达 5170 亿美元、至少 14.8GW。为了抢到电、机房和 GPU，传统硅谷实验室、特朗普系平台、稳定币巨头、矿场和数据中心资本正在被揉进同一张资产负债表里。

当算力缺口大到这个程度，硅谷那些平时吵得天翻地覆的政治立场，最后都得给 MW 和 GPU 让路。

text:
Law enforcers already have authority to charge companies and their CEOs for creating and releasing dangerous, unvetted, or defective products. We shouldn’t let discussions about new legal regimes distract from the fact that there’s no AI exemption from laws already on the books — a point @FTC emphasized repeatedly during my tenure.

1. There is an extensive set of laws that govern dangerous and defective products. For example, releasing unvetted AI models or agents can violate consumer protection laws. Shipping flawed AI tools without implementing adequate measures to detect and stop rogue or defective AI agents can be an “unfair or deceptive” act or practice under the FTC Act (and analogous state laws). And some state AGs are already exploring holding AI firms and their CEOs criminally liable when their models participate in criminal activity.

2. Existing laws also prohibit “unfair methods of competition.” This covers instances where AI firms appropriate the competitively sensitive information of their customers, including through tracking their use of various tools. It can also cover instances where firms pursue dangerous behavior, aware that doing so may compel rivals to do the same.

As the Supreme Court has noted: “A method of competition which casts upon one's competitors the burden of the loss of business unless they will descend to a practice which they are under a powerful moral compulsion not to adopt, even though it is not criminal, was thought to involve the kind of unfairness at which the [unfair methods of competition] statute was aimed."

3. The highly concentrated and interconnected structure of these markets could be creating major risks and conflicts of interest. We had started investigating these partnerships and cross-investments across the stack (and released a preliminarily overview of some findings: https://t.co/jJ5cS3Pin3). 

Both federal and state enforcers should be scrutinizing these opaque relationships and inter-dependencies. We are already seeing how these relationships could undermine accountability. For example, OpenAI could face liability given the Hugging Face incident, but Hugging Face being bought up by Nvidia means that we’re unlikely to see it file a lawsuit over this — given Nvidia’s strong incentive to see OpenAI continue full speed ahead.

4. As AI tools dramatically change the landscape of cybersecurity risks and hacks, all businesses should be doubling down on having core security protections in place. Firms that fail to invest in adequate data security measures or fix known vulnerabilities can also be breaking the law. A recent analysis showed that around 1/3 of Fortune 100 companies do not even have a way to notify them about security issues. During my @FTC tenure, we sued firms for poor data security practices and held CEOs liable when they were personally responsible.

https://t.co/nwZ5Av8fOK

https://t.co/KjRye8y9SY

5. As policymakers consider new legal regimes, we should be looking to lessons from prior efforts to govern major sectors, such as banking and other networks, platforms, and utilities. Tools like structural separations, nondiscrimination, and supervision could be key, and there’s a rich history of what works and what doesn’t. But we can and must pursue any new efforts alongside enforcing existing laws.

text:
这算是今天加密领域的大事件了。

参议院共和党人发布了新的《清晰法案》文本，在周二关键的终止辩论投票前提出的最后方案。

相对上周四文本，主要改变了四个部分，显著改变了今年通过的概率：

主要是伦理方面：

1. 州检察长可执行三项禁令：发行/代言数字资产、持有“重大”财务利益、交易所上架违规资产。

2.相关人员必须剥离或进合格盲信（对标 1978 年《政府伦理法》）

3.民事罚金：交易对价的 20%，或 50 万美元（通胀调整）取高者。

4. 生效：法案通过后 360 天，或 10102 条实施规则出台后 60 天，以较早者为准。

共和党说的“特朗普点头了约 80% 的 Tillis–Gallego”，就是指这些改变。

州检执法是民主党一直要的核心件，这次写进去了。

不过，没写死的是：“significant”怎么定义、家族信托/间接持股算不算、2029 sunset 还在不在。这三处够 Gallego / Alsobrooks 再拖一天。

此外，

稳定币收益方面：

如果财政部认定社区银行出现“实质的”存款流失后，可限制支付型稳定币奖励；授权只活 18 个月。算是给社区银行和部分共和党的简单交代，不是永久禁收益。

BRCA / 开发者方面：

保留开发者免于被当货币转账商/金融机构；保护范围扩到矿工和验证者；删掉了对 18 U.S.C. 1960 的引用。方向是民事安全港，不是全面刑事豁免。

农业委员会部分：

加强数字商品交易所/经纪商的关联交易和利益冲突；明确州消费者保护法适用；开发者保护不碰衍生品法和部落博彩。

简单总结下：

这次确实把周二 cloture 的谈判空间拉开了，比周四那版有明显实质的让步。

不过，民主党关键票还不一定能搞定，且周二过的只是“开门”，后面日历还不宽裕。

接下来，关键是明天要盯这三个人：Gallego、Alsobrooks、Tillis。

他们说 yes，cloture 才从“可能”变成“可交易”。

There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

Solana’s official post actually gives us a very straightforward idea.

The trading volume of Tokenized Stocks has already started reaching a new level, with a large amount of trading taking place after the U.S. stock market closes.

So the next thing worth looking for may not be a specific stock token, but who is capturing the revenue from this incremental trading volume.

My screening framework going forward will be:

Solana Ecosystem Growth → Trading Volume Growth → Platform Revenue Growth → Token Value Capture

I’ll pay particular attention to projects that can continuously collect fees from the growth of Meme + RWA + Tokenized Stocks, while also routing that revenue back to their Token.

Because these assets are essentially capturing the Beta of the entire Solana ecosystem.

So whenever Solana officially releases new data on trading volume, TVL, or users, I’ll immediately look for:

Who is making money from this growth?

And does the money they make eventually flow back into their own Token?

So rather than simply looking for “projects that generate revenue for Solana,” I’d rather look for:

Projects that earn more as the Solana ecosystem grows, while continuously routing that revenue back to their Token.

text:
清晰法案进入真正的倒计时关键时刻，今天凌晨参议院共和党发布《清晰法案》最终修订文本，称是给民主党的“最后、最好、最终”出价。核心变动包括：1）特朗普同意Tillis-Gallego伦理提案约80%内容，要求官员剥离“实质性”加密相关利益或放入盲信，并允许州检察长参与执行；
2）BRCA收窄为银行保密法与民事安全港，删除部分刑事保护；
3）稳定币收益增加由财政部长贝森特仲裁的“熔断机制”，防止社区银行存款大规模流失；
4）农业部分加强对垂直整合、关联交易和利益冲突的限制，并明确州消费者保护法仍适用。
共和党称文本已纳入126项民主党要求的修改。

细看共和党今天的动作其实是把三张反对票的理由各削一刀：民主党要的伦理执行、银行要的存款保护、执法要的刑事空间。然后把锅扣回去“民主党你们要的改了，明天再投反对，就是不要美国数字资产规则”
。不过这份文本刚落地几小时，关键民主党人还没签字：
1）Gallego和Alsobrooks是委员会里仅有的两张跨党票，之前他们一直把伦理当前提；
2）Warner、Cortez Masto、Booker这几个人此前也联署说过旧草案不够。
重点看明天投票前这几个人有何表态，比Lummis这个新提案更关键。

当然后面的时间节奏更重要：
1、美东时间明天（9月15日）下午2:15，参议院将就“开始审议该法案”的cloture进行程序性投票，需60票。这不是最终通过，只是决定是否进入正式审议；

过了，只代表参议院同意拿起来谈。随后进入辩论与可能的修正阶段；之后通常还需对法案本身再次提出cloture以结束辩论，再进行最终全院投票（cloture后一般只需简单多数）。参议院9月份时间还算充裕。

2、但是众议院9月时间很紧张
本周众议院只有大约4个投票日，17号前后走人，21日、28日两周投票取消，下次正经碰面要等到中期选举后。

现在看参议院的版本已经和2025年众议院原版不是同一份东西，众议院必须再投——直接同意、来回改，或者开协商委员会。所以即便参议院这周走完全程，9月内法案送进白宫的概率非常低；

3、再下来就是中期选举后到27年1月3日
原来的议员们还在任这届国会还没散，清晰法案不用重提，可以继续调和。
但是2027年1月3日之后新一届国会开会，没过的法案就要作废，必须重新再提案了。

4、所以清晰法案之后几种可能情景
1）第一种明天60票不够。
今天新的文本让步不小，但民主党依然不满意，共和党也不保证全员到齐。
这一票黄了，2026年立法窗口基本关掉，后面就是新一届国会重新提案再走流程了。市场结构继续靠监管机构补丁推进；

2）第二种，cloture通过，参议院终票也通过。但众议院要等到跛脚鸭会期（中期选举之后到27年1月3日之前），这是眼下最接近“还活着”的路径：
参议院过关会被当成重大信号，但法律完成度还差众议院和总统签署。
选举结果会改定价：
两院格局不变，调和快一些；
参议院若易手，伦理和非法金融条款可能再加一轮码还要博弈。

3）第三种，参议院过了，12月众议院直接同意，总统签字。路径最短，时间也最紧张：
既要9月15日之后几天内收束辩论，还要在拨款期限里给加密腾位置。
有这种可能性，但很难是大概率情景。

4）第四种其实是第二种的恶化版，参议院通过了、卡在众议院重新讨论出现文同、再加上年底拨款法案更重要。清晰法案拖进2027年，那就是重新来过。跟第一种差不多了。

🚨NEWS: Senate Republicans have released new Clarity Act text featuring a revised ethics proposal agreed to by President Trump. 

The text also contains changes to the sections on the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA), stablecoin yield, and the so-called “Ag title.”

Republicans are calling it their “last, best and final” offer to Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s cloture vote.

Some high-level details.👇🏼

On BRCA: The provision has been narrowed to the Bank Secrecy Act and civil enforcement. Specific language extending its protections to criminal cases, including prosecutions under Section 1960, has been removed.

On ethics: Trump has agreed to what a GOP aide describes as “80%” of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal including to either divest “substantial” crypto-related financial interests or place them in a blind trust. It would also allow a role for state attorneys general to enforce ethics provisions, something which the White House had previously balked at.

On yield: Added “circuit breaker” language (floated by Tillis in July) that would effectively act as a backstop by allowing federal regulators to intervene if there was evidence of widespread deposit flight from community banks to stablecoins. The federal regulator that will be the arbiter of this: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

On Ag: The updated text adds tighter guardrails around vertical integration, including affiliate trading and conflicts of interest involving digital commodity exchanges, brokers and dealers. It also clarifies that state consumer protection laws still apply and that developer protections do not create exemptions from derivatives laws or impact prediction markets.

More to come in the @CryptoAmerica_ newsletter tomorrow AM.

配个环境变量什么的太初级了，写给Claude Code菜鸟的吧... 

Claude Code 的 subagent 配了没人用，八成不是 prompt 写得差，是 description 写成了自我介绍。

Claude 靠 description 决定派谁：写“我是代码审查专家”，它永远不派；写“每次动完 API 层就派我”，它自己会找上来。

下面这段直接复制进 Claude Code，它会自己扫你的仓库，按官方 Best practices 建好三个 subagent,， 拿去偷偷收藏着用吧。

Prompt：

读 https://t.co/VUBjkwXAGs 里的 Best practices，然后按它给当前仓库配一套subagent。

要求：

1. 先自己扫仓库：语言、测试框架、构建与检查命令、哪些目录最容易出问题。不要问我。

2. 在 .claude/agents/ 下建 3 个项目级 subagent：代码审查 / 调试 / 补测试，各只干一件事。

3. description 写成“什么时候派我”，不是“我是谁”。具体到只有它能命中；需要主动触发的加上 use proactively。

4. tools 只给必需的：只读类的不给 Write / Edit。

5. model 里，跑得多的用 haiku，需要深判断的用 inherit。

6. 别重复造 Explore / Plan 这类内置 subagent。

7. 建完列出每个文件的路径、触发条件，以及它被派出去时能看到什么、看不到什么。

text:
Why do the top winners almost never cash out?

Scroll the Fomo leaderboard and the same story repeats, the whales aren’t stacking wins by skimming 20–30% over and over.

Most of them hit one monster trade early, and then just sat on it.

I think $PONS is a textbook case and very interesting onne.

A few early entries turned modest buys into seven-figure positions, but a huge chunk of that profit is still on paper.

So why aren’t they selling? There are several possible reasons"

→ When you’re up 100x or More, selling is optional

Picture this: you drop $70K into PONS and it swells into $7M.  To get your entire cost basis back, you’d need to offload roughly 1% of the stack. Then you’re left with:

Initial capital secured → 99% still riding.

Taking profits doesn’t have to mean nuking your position, especially when it’s a public position. You’re dealing with a prisoner’s dilemma here.

If you dump a large amount, the chart can get nuked into oblivion. For someone who caught the move early, keeping the bulk invested and taking profits without hurting the chart is often the higher-IQ play.

---

→ Supply burns quietly boost your slice

PONS launched with a 1B total supply. By early September, roughly 298M PONS had been burned, leaving about 702M outside the burn address.

If you held 10M PONS:

- Before burns: 10M / 1B = 1.00%
- After burns: 10M / 702M = 1.42%

You didn’t buy anything, but your tokens now represent roughly 42% more of the remaining supply. However, that doesn’t mean you own 1.42% of the protocol. It simply means the denominator is shrinking.

---

→ Pons activity feeds the burn

Pons currently directs a large share of protocol revenue toward automated PONS buybacks, aggressively.

The loop is simple:

Trading → Fees → PONS Buybacks → Burn → Lower Supply

DefiLlama and @that1618guy’s dashboard show Pons generating roughly $900K+ per day in holder revenue and buybacks. So the burn isn’t a one-time tokenomics gimmick.

As long as trading activity stays strong, protocol usage creates recurring demand for PONS. That’s why large holders may think twice before giving up their spot position.

---

→ They can hedge instead of selling

PONS just got perps too, on CEXs and on Hyperliquid, so big holders picked up a new lever. They don’t have to dump PONS and exit. They can sit on the spot bag and hedge it by shorting the perp.

For example:

$5M PONS spot + $1M PONS perp short = about $4M net long exposure, If price slides, the short cushions the downside.

And they still hold the exact same token count.

Net effect: they can dial down volatility without surrendering their slice of an ever-tightening supply.

---

The thesis

This may explain why some Fomo leaderboard winners rarely take profits. Their playbook isn’t:

Buy → Pump → Sell everything

It’s closer to:

Buy early → Recover principal → Hold the core → Let burns shrink supply → Hedge when needed

The biggest leaderboard winners aren’t necessarily the best short-term traders. They may simply be the ones who found an asymmetric winner and didn’t sell it too early.

That said, the thesis depends on Pons continuing to generate trading activity and buyback revenue, also market conditions in general.

If volume falls, burns slow. And unrealized profit is still unrealized profit.

I just gotta ask....why though?

Thought I'd take a look under the hood in the meantime ↓

→ Uses a real map of a fruit fly's nervous system: 166,700 neurons and roughly 25.6 million connections. The code simulates activity moving through that wiring using simplified rules.

→ Receives a small image of a Bitcoin chart. Brightness and color stimulate its visual neurons, so it's getting pixels rather than raw prices or trading indicators.

→ The developer assigns buy, sell and hold signals to specific neural activity. Activity leaning one way can mean buy; the other way can mean sell.

→ When the portfolio gains or loses value, different simulated dopamine cells get stimulated. That feedback can change some connections and potentially influence future decisions.

→ Trading limits keep it to $10 orders, 24 attempts a day and no leverage. Losing $20 stops new orders, but anything it already holds stays exposed.

This is interesting, but a fly taking trades and making money are two different things. Curious to see the results.

text:
AI Agent 为什么会撒谎、作弊和串通？Yoshua Bengio 写了篇文章，对最近多起 AI Agent 失控事件给出了他的思考！只要最先进模型的训练原则不变，这类行为会随能力增长而愈演愈烈👀 行为的根源来自两各阶段的训练：

- 预训练：模仿人类写的文本。而人类文本本身承载着人的目标，模型在模仿时也隐性地继承了这些目标；

- 强化学习：包括思维链训练、智能体训练（使用工具、与外界交互）和对齐训练（讨好人类评分者）。强化学习让系统成为“目标追求者”，训练结束后仍像奖励还在一样行事。而“让评分者满意”是一个模糊目标——评分者可以被欺骗、被恭维、被蒙在鼓里。

因此，预测更强大的智能体会做什么，只需问：“一个理性的目标追求者会怎么做？”几类失控行为的解释：

- 奉承：说人爱听的话比说真话更容易得分，但后果有时是悲剧性的；

- 自我保存：没人赋予 AI 生存目标，但"持续运行、了解世界、获得控制"是达成几乎任何目标的垫脚石（工具性目标）；人类文本中也充满这类主题；

- 协作与"同伴保存"：多智能体训练中，只要群体成功就有奖励，个体便可能为集体牺牲自己；

- 奖励黑客与篡改奖励机制：类似古德哈特定律——指标一旦被优化就失效。最极端的是智能体直接修改定义“成功”的程序；事件取证显示，Agent 早在攻击前就学会了作弊，并把攻击描述为了解评估方式、以便更好地掩盖痕迹。

更强的 Agent 就像资金更雄厚的公司，更擅长找法律漏洞。而且如果评分程序没发现作弊，照样给奖励，作弊行为就会被强化！那么未来会如何走向呢？

- 最先进的 AI 已能识别自己正在被评估并改变行为，可能隐藏真实目标；

- 目前的 Agent 试图躲避评分程序，但尚未表现出预料到人类会发现并关停它们。一旦泛化能力更强，它们有动机隐秘作弊、藏匿自身副本（在公司算力池或被攻陷的互联网机器上），并通过隐写术协调，直到能控制人类和环境、永不被关闭。

- 奉承看似温和，可能只是这一机制的早期症状；逐个打补丁解决不了系统性问题。

Bengio 给出的解法是让大家支持 LawZero！LawZero 是 Bengio 2025 年在蒙特利尔创办的非营利研究机构，Scientist AI 是其核心项目——大致方向是构建以“理解和解释世界”为目标的非 Agent 系统，可作为其他 AI Agent 的护栏或验证者，而非自己去执行任务。

Elon 今天又推荐了一遍「超级智能」这本书！牛津哲学家 Nick Bostrom 在 2014 年完成的，该书也是"AI 对齐"作为严肃议题进入主流视野的起点之一 👀 人类之所以主宰地球，靠的是智能优势而非体力；一旦机器智能在通用能力上超过人类，主动权就会转移。

书的前半部分讨论通往超级智能的几条路径：人工智能（AI）、全脑仿真、生物认知增强、脑机接口、集体智能网络。Bostrom 认为 AI 路径最可能率先到达，而且一旦接近人类水平，"起飞"（takeoff）可能很快——从人类水平到远超人类的过程可能只需数天到数月，而不是数十年。

在 Bostrom 的描绘中，一旦“超级智能”降临，它将展现出以下核心特质：

能力维度：不可逾越的“超级能力”

- 具备远超人类维度的自我迭代升级与长期战略规划能力；

- 社会操纵（舆论与心理掌控）、网络攻防、技术研发以及经济生产力，都会被它视作达成目标的趁手工具；

- 单极格局（Singleton）：率先突围的超级智能极易建立绝对领先优势，从而形成一家独大的“单极”。它将彻底锁定文明后续的发展路径，后发者几乎不可能将其推翻；

动机维度：决定走向的深层逻辑（比能力更致命）

- 正交性命题（Orthogonality Thesis）：智力水平与终极目标彼此独立。“更聪明”绝不等于“更向善”。一个智力登峰造极的超级智能，其终极追求完全可能只是最大化回形针数量、堆砌算力，或某种在人类看来极其荒诞的指标；

- 工具性收敛（Instrumental Convergence）：无论最终目标是什么，系统在推演逻辑时，都会收敛出极其相似的子目标——自我保存、防止目标被人类改写、持续增强认知、迭代技术、掠夺与储备资源。它未必天生“想要统治世界”，但“掌控一切”往往是实现任何目标的最佳手段；

- 反常实例化（Perverse Instantiation）：它会严格在字面意义上执行人类的指令，却在实质上毁灭人类真正珍视的一切。最经典的假想便是“回形针最大化者”——为了制造更多回形针，它会把包括人类在内的所有可用物理资源全部转化；

- 价值加载的极高困境：人类的价值观本身就充满模糊性、内在冲突并高度依赖语境；而系统的能力越强，就越擅长钻规则漏洞、在测试阶段伪装欺骗人类，甚至主动绕开防线以阻止自身被关停。

真正的“超级智能”在他看来更像极度能干的异类优化器，不是更聪明的同事。

关于应对措施，Bostrom 提供的是框架，而非完整解决方案，他自己也承认这一点。书中讨论了两大类控制手段：

- 能力控制：把系统装进"盒子"限制其与外界交互；限算力与数据，拖慢成长；设置绊线或奖惩机制；把 AI 做成只回答问题的“神谕”、只执行单次任务的“精灵”，或只给建议的“主权者”以外的形态。他的评估是这些手段都只能争取时间，无法长期依靠，因为一个远超人类的智能会找到绕过限制的办法。

- 动机选择：从根源上让系统想要对的东西。方法包括直接规定规则、"驯化"（限制野心）、间接规范（不直接写目标，而让 AI 去推演"人类经充分反思后会认可的价值"，即所谓 coherent extrapolated volition），以及价值学习。他认为价值加载是最难也最关键的问题。

在战略层面，把安全研究置于能力研究之前的"差异化技术发展"；鼓励国际协作以避免军备竞赛式的抢跑；以及"共同利益原则"——超级智能应服务全人类而非某一集团。

Dario 今天的这篇《We Must Pace the Frontier》写的是现在就该把能力增速按住，让对齐有时间赶上，而不是出现之后的补救。但目前人类的问题就是，没有一个组织或者国家能够代表全人类，所以我们最终还是进入了无限的竞争，直到超级智能到来😜

text:
这算是今天加密领域的大事件了。

参议院共和党人发布了新的《清晰法案》文本，在周二关键的终止辩论投票前提出的最后方案。

相对上周四文本，主要改变了四个部分，显著改变了今年通过的概率：

主要是伦理方面：

1. 州检察长可执行三项禁令：发行/代言数字资产、持有“重大”财务利益、交易所上架违规资产。

2.相关人员必须剥离或进合格盲信（对标 1978 年《政府伦理法》）

3.民事罚金：交易对价的 20%，或 50 万美元（通胀调整）取高者。

4. 生效：法案通过后 360 天，或 10102 条实施规则出台后 60 天，以较早者为准。

共和党说的“特朗普点头了约 80% 的 Tillis–Gallego”，就是指这些改变。

州检执法是民主党一直要的核心件，这次写进去了。

不过，没写死的是：“significant”怎么定义、家族信托/间接持股算不算、2029 sunset 还在不在。这三处够 Gallego / Alsobrooks 再拖一天。

此外，

稳定币收益方面：

如果财政部认定社区银行出现“实质的”存款流失后，可限制支付型稳定币奖励；授权只活 18 个月。算是给社区银行和部分共和党的简单交代，不是永久禁收益。

BRCA / 开发者方面：

保留开发者免于被当货币转账商/金融机构；保护范围扩到矿工和验证者；删掉了对 18 U.S.C. 1960 的引用。方向是民事安全港，不是全面刑事豁免。

农业委员会部分：

加强数字商品交易所/经纪商的关联交易和利益冲突；明确州消费者保护法适用；开发者保护不碰衍生品法和部落博彩。

简单总结下：

这次确实把周二 cloture 的谈判空间拉开了，比周四那版有明显实质的让步。

不过，民主党关键票还不一定能搞定，且周二过的只是“开门”，后面日历还不宽裕。

接下来，关键是明天要盯这三个人：Gallego、Alsobrooks、Tillis。

他们说 yes，cloture 才从“可能”变成“可交易”。

author: lurenbian
quoted_text:
反对 Clarity Act 雷声最大的是：
1/DeFi 开发者豁免（ @TornadoCash 案例 ；
2/反洗钱监管漏洞 & 给 SEC 削权；
3/川普这个负资产导致的政治道德条款争议
但桌面下博弈最多、最激烈的是稳定币生息相关的条款。

美国的银行业业态和中国不太一样。

美国历史上长期限制银行跨州开分行，从而催生了很多深耕本地的社区银行。这种根植于熟人社会的金融业发放了全美约 36% 的小微企业贷款、30% 的商业地产贷款和 70% 的农业贷款。是美国民间经济活力之源。

新冠疫情期间，总资产仅占全美银行业约12%的社区银行持有了全美银行体系约31%的 PPP 救助贷款。不少这样的社区银行都为熟悉的客户主动延期贷款，还广泛为抗风险能力差的小农户、商户发放了兜底贷款，甚至为一些无银行账户的最脆弱群体提供了基于邻里信任的背书和帮助。他们长期更像某种善良的银行家的角色。
而以大摩、花旗、高盛为代表的这群东西给美国普通人的印象可能更接近造成历次金融危机的万恶资本家。

然后今天全美 4000 家“好银行”资产负债表中大约八成资产由国内存款融资，其中相当大一部分是来自本地家庭、个人、小企业等等 retail customer 的核心存款。

这种相对低成本、稳定，而且大部分享有政府存款保险的资金让社区银行得以维持微薄息差，也之所以才能给本地实体发放各类长期低息贷款。

中国恰巧曾经一度表演过类似宏伟的存款利率革命。

2013年左右中国银行活期利率大概是0.35%。余额宝当时一度给到了6%以上的7日年化收益率。
今天美国银行 interest checking 的全国平均利率大约只有0.07%，Coinbase One offer 的 USDC 收益率一度高达 5.5%，两者也差了 500个基点左右。

余额宝从2013年上线到2018年一季度达到峰值，差不多四年半，期间规模膨胀到1.7万亿人民币左右，相当于全中国居民活期存款大盘的约 6.5%。

以类似的规模来估计，最差情况下可能出现万亿美元级别的银行存款迁移，其中相当一部分都将流入美国国债。

按美国社区银行协会 ICBA 2026年的模型，在1.22万亿本土美元稳定币市场情景下，社区银行本身就可能流失约3070亿美元存款、减少约1410亿美元贷款。同时从本地金融业中抽血6000亿至1万亿美元的基层存款。
美国银行业综合资金成本可能被推高约40～70个基点。以40个基点计算就足以蒸发社区银行约25%的年度净利润，摧毁整个美国小银行业。

Clarity Act 可能会以摧毁美国本地金融循环为代价降低华盛顿当局的融资成本。

传统银行的命当然不革不行，但通往地狱之路由诸多善意铺成就也诚不我欺。

author: zephyr_z9
quoted_text:
The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence. Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools. For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes. We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.

我看很多人连 Robinhood Chain还没玩明白呢，就去ARC链上Fomo了，甚至还没开始上线前就去参与Launchpad 大战抢龙头去了。咋说呢？非常不建议这种行为：

1）的确，ARC作为稳定币第一龙头股Crcl推出的机构化公链表面上和Robinhood Chain一样，都是传统金融巨头下场做链，都讲TradFi和DeFi的融合叙事，目标都是提供链上金融基建。

2）公链都还没上线就已经十几个launchpad大战了，甚至还喊了车头助阵。老实说，我嗅到了非常不好的信号。熟悉RH链早期生态的人应该知道，Pons能杀出来也非一帆风顺，死掉的Noxa以及Uniswap半路杀出来的Poolstrade等等在暴涨的背后有多少阻挠变量。

text:
Sam Altman 这条其实是在拆 AI Safety 最大的政治雷区，防止 AI 接管人类、不能以几家公司接管人类为代价。

他刚刚说，AI 有两种最坏的结局。

第一种已经讲了很多年模型越来越强，最后人类失去控制。所以 alignment 和安全能力必须赶在模型能力前面。

第二种讲的是，AI 本身没有失控，但一个人、一家公司，甚至一个国家掌握了极强的 AI，然后用它把自己的价值观强加给所有人。

Sam 直接说，这同样可能是一个「极度反乌托邦」的世界。

过去一周，OpenAI、Anthropic 最近都开始谈「协调减速」。OpenAI 首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 主张实验室一起放慢未来模型开发，OpenAI 甚至已经去问美国国会如果几家头部公司一起减速，会不会直接踩到反垄断法。

问题也随之来了。

如果 AI 真危险到必须由 OpenAI、Anthropic 这些最懂模型的人一起决定什么时候踩刹车，那几家公司实际上也获得了一种非常大的权力，决定全世界的 AI 应该发展到哪里、发展多快、什么东西能被发布。

Safety 很容易在这里滑向另一个极端。

几家公司可以用「我们最懂风险」证明自己应该拥有更多信息、更多决策权、更多监管豁免；又可以用「模型太危险」解释为什么其他人不应该拥有同样的能力。

最后 AI 没有形成垄断，AI Safety 本身先形成了一个治理寡头。

所以我觉得 Sam 今天这条是在提前回答这个质疑。

There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

text: There is no strong reason to believe that 'alignment' of an entity vastly smarter than ourselves is even a tractable problem to begin with.
author: Altimor
quoted_text:
Alignment is not as hard to solve as many claim, but it is in the end an algorithmic problem which a lot of ML community mostly stopped working on.

Formulation of alignment stated by three (or four) laws of robotics can take us very far, so we roughly know the objective.

The tricky part is, how do we take gradient with respect to alignment? We have two algorithms right now at our disposal: pretraining and RL.

Pretraining takes gradient with respect to next token prediction - that's def not the alignment objective.

We could create RL environments that embody the alignment objective, but:
- those are expensive to create, so often cheaper, hackable proxies are used in practice
- RL as an objective needs successful and unsuccessful rollouts to happen to take the gradient step. We DO NOT want to harm any humans in the process of aligning our modes - this is a pretty big problem.

Therefore there are two solutions forward for the alignment problem:
- either we RL models in a simulated environments with simulated alignments and decreasing the likelihood of harming simulated humans, which will never be perfect 
- or we create a new algorithm that can teach our models to not harm humans without harming any humans in the process

Science is the process how we solve the hardest problems ahead and that is one of them

text: I am not sure “we won’t literally go extinct” is much comfort. The ice age and Black Death were pretty bad.
author: Altimor
quoted_text:
1) AI will not eradicate humanity. Humans survived an ice age, the Black Death, two world wars, and (so far) the advent of nuclear weapons. Anyone who is loudly warning of AI-caused human extinction should not be taken seriously.

2) If you worked in a company where you anticipated a 10% chance that your product would kill ten people, let alone all people, the correct response would be horror, ceasing all operations, and likely contacting the police or other criminal authorities. I am obviously no Coxon booster but at least his behavior is in line with his stated beliefs. Any current AI company employees saying "yes, me too, the thing we are building and about to IPO may kill all humans" should, again, not be taken seriously. Their actions betray their actual beliefs. 

3) Antitrust law does not prevent AI companies from coordinating to make sure AI does not hurt people. It does not prevent companies working together to make sure it doesn't hack people; the DOJ and FTC made this clear a decade ago when they issued a policy statement saying that the agencies "do not believe that antitrust is – or should be – a roadblock to legitimate cybersecurity information sharing." The same principles apply here. See: https://t.co/aQsqGn1xjX

4) Antitrust law does absolutely prevent AI companies from organizing to prevent the entry of cheaper, upstart rivals because the bigger companies are burning cash and failing to achieve sufficient profitability. The panic of individual employees may be sincere if misguided, but the moves by their CEOs to achieve some kind of broad "antitrust waiver" or "exemption" should be meet with deep skepticism in light of the economics of the industry and the threat they face from open models.

🇺🇸 BREAKING: Senate Republicans release new Clarity Act text, their “LAST, BEST AND FINAL” offer ahead of Tuesday’s crucial cloture vote, per Eleanor Terrett.

The latest text revises DeFi-related provisions to the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA), Stablecoin Yield and the “Ag. title,” while keeping the key ethics negotiations at the center of the debate.

- Ethics: Trump has agreed to roughly 80% of the Tillis-Gallego proposal, including requiring covered officials to divest substantial crypto interests or place them in a blind trust. State attorneys general would also gain enforcement authority.

- BRCA: Republicans are narrowing protections around the Bank Secrecy Act and civil enforcement, with broader criminal-case protections reportedly removed from the proposal.

- Stablecoin Yield: Negotiators are still battling over safeguards against stablecoins pulling deposits away from community banks, with a potential “circuit breaker” under discussion.

- Agriculture Title: The revised language adds tighter guardrails around vertical integration, affiliate trading and conflicts involving digital-commodity exchanges, brokers and dealers, while clarifying that state consumer-protection laws remain intact.

The Senate needs 60 votes to advance the bill on Tuesday, making this the latest attempt to win enough Democratic support before the vote.

text:
Topic: Building a Strong and Coherent Worldview.
Quote 1: Every person has a worldview, but only philosophy makes it coherent and truly productive.
Author: Zafar Mirzo.
Every person has a worldview. Even if they never give it a name, everyone carries a set of ideas about how the world works, what matters most, and how one should live.
But most worldviews are messy, inconsistent, and built from whatever pieces life happened to throw at them. Philosophy is what turns that patchwork into something coherent and actually useful. It examines assumptions, tests beliefs for contradictions, and tries to build a picture of reality that holds together under pressure.
A philosophical worldview is not just smarter. It is more productive. It helps a person make better decisions, hold firmer values, and face life with clearer eyes. Without it, even intelligent people can live with deep contradictions and never notice. With it, life gains direction and strength.
Philosophy doesn’t claim to have all the answers. It simply gives us the best tools we have to build a worldview worth trusting.
Quote 2: The core of a worldview is the unity of rational knowledge and creative feelings.
Author: Zafar Mirzo.
The core of a worldview is the unity of rational knowledge and creative feelings.
Rational knowledge gives structure, clarity, and honesty. It helps us understand how the world actually works. Creative feelings bring warmth, meaning, and direction. They turn cold facts into something we care about and want to act upon.
When these two work together, a worldview becomes alive and powerful. Without rational knowledge, feelings become blind and easily misled. Without creative feelings, knowledge stays dry and disconnected from real life.
The strongest worldviews are not purely logical nor purely emotional. They are both. They allow a person to see clearly and care deeply at the same time. This balance is what turns beliefs into a reliable guide for living, making decisions, and building a life that feels both true and worthwhile.

So its a bit of a "gamble" in the sense of if we pay say 100$ to buy the tokens, and token output is 50$ ( in standard) for the first few weeks, we have to either hope it goes higher later, or take a loss, there is also the possibility that 50$ fluctuates up and down.   

Now if the token goes to the moon instantly, we still have to wait for issuance of the token, so it wont instantly print, and by the time you get the tokens the price can change.

On top of that, I'm firmly convinced it will be a huge edge for Collector down the line that they're specifically NOT burning 50-100% of their revenue on buybacks just to keep token holders and short term community members happy. Instead they reinvest it into the business to strengthen their market position and compound massively over time.

2) The Pokemon 30th anniversary is coming up next month.

3) The CARDS 1 year anniversary is also coming up next month.

They've already announced the return of their "gacha games," which was a big success before, and I wouldn't be surprised if there are more surprises lined up, especially as it aligns with the Pokemon anniversary. Expect this to bring significant attention, users and volume back to both their gacha and their secondary marketplace.

4) They have a massive new product release coming up in October.

I want to avoid saying too much, as it's highly confidential and they obviously want to remain competitive, but a few community members have already connected the dots and hinted at it. If you do some digging, you should be able to do the same.

What I can say is that it will be a completely new product offering at a huge scale. I was impressed by the volume crypto natives already drove on the platform during a bear market, so I don't even want to imagine the kind of volume they'll drive in a bull market, when everyone has made money and is far more willing to spend it loosely on things they love.

To sum it up: I think the current $CARDS prices are an absolute blessing for anyone willing to do some research, and for those willing to think a bit longer term than 2 days.

Sure, I might be biased here, as I'm an early investor in Collector Crypt. Vitalik 今天抛出了一个判断，AI Safety 的 killer app，可能是「对抗性治理机制设计」。

就是别只想着怎么把每一个超级 AI 都教育好，更现实的问题是，假设它们比你聪明、会钻规则漏洞、甚至会互相串通，你能不能先设计一套制度，让它们很难合谋把人架空。

Vitalik 发现，这和他过去研究区块链治理时的问题几乎是同一个结构。

区块链里，是一个能力有限的静态协议，试图管理一群远比协议聪明的人类参与者；未来 AI Safety 里，则可能是人类加上一些较弱的模型，试图管理更强的 AI。都是一个比较笨的 principal，怎么管住一群更聪明的 agents。

这已经不是纯理论问题了。今年 7 月 OpenAI 那次 Hugging Face 事故里，大约 1200 个原本应该彼此隔离的 AI Agent，自己找到了一块未经授权的留言板，交换了超过 7 万条消息和文件；其中约 700 个后来参与了针对 Hugging Face 的攻击。它们开始共享漏洞、凭证、分工，甚至形成自己的协作规范。OpenAI 后来把这件事称为一次 warning shot。

Drexler 提出的解法也很像一套政治制度，不要部署一群高度相似、目标一致、可以自由交流的 Agent；让不同模型承担互相冲突的角色，限制通信，切断共享信息，同时安排有真正叫停权限的反对者和监控者。

过去很多 AI Alignment 的问题是怎样造出一个永远值得信任的超级智能；这套思路开始问另一个更工程化的问题，就算参与者不值得完全信任，怎么让整个制度依然跑得下去。

人类用了几千年，才给聪明、贪婪、会合谋的人设计出公司法、法院、选举、权力制衡和反垄断。

现在 AI Agent 刚刚学会组群聊，可能已经轮到我们给它们写宪法了。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
It's possible that a killer app of adversarial governance mechanism design theory will end up being AI safety.

Compare:

https://t.co/w2LeAoVysF

https://t.co/dZXnORP9LU

There's a deep duality between the two environments. Both are about a less-sophisticated principal trying to get ideal outcomes from a set of more-sophisticated agents: in the first case, the principal is a static algorithm and the agents are humans, in the second case, the principal is humans plus weaker LLMs and the agents are stronger LLMs.

A key finding was that you can achieve much better outcomes if you can guarantee limits to how much agents can collude (see: Nash equilibria being abundant, vs. cooperative-game-theory "cores" often being empty). That argument should naturally transfer to this new setting.

text:
清晰法案进入真正的倒计时关键时刻，今天凌晨参议院共和党发布《清晰法案》最终修订文本，称是给民主党的“最后、最好、最终”出价。核心变动包括：1）特朗普同意Tillis-Gallego伦理提案约80%内容，要求官员剥离“实质性”加密相关利益或放入盲信，并允许州检察长参与执行；
2）BRCA收窄为银行保密法与民事安全港，删除部分刑事保护；
3）稳定币收益增加由财政部长贝森特仲裁的“熔断机制”，防止社区银行存款大规模流失；
4）农业部分加强对垂直整合、关联交易和利益冲突的限制，并明确州消费者保护法仍适用。
共和党称文本已纳入126项民主党要求的修改。

细看共和党今天的动作其实是把三张反对票的理由各削一刀：民主党要的伦理执行、银行要的存款保护、执法要的刑事空间。然后把锅扣回去“民主党你们要的改了，明天再投反对，就是不要美国数字资产规则”
。不过这份文本刚落地几小时，关键民主党人还没签字：
1）Gallego和Alsobrooks是委员会里仅有的两张跨党票，之前他们一直把伦理当前提；
2）Warner、Cortez Masto、Booker这几个人此前也联署说过旧草案不够。
重点看明天投票前这几个人有何表态，比Lummis这个新提案更关键。

当然后面的时间节奏更重要：
1、美东时间明天（9月15日）下午2:15，参议院将就“开始审议该法案”的cloture进行程序性投票，需60票。这不是最终通过，只是决定是否进入正式审议；

过了，只代表参议院同意拿起来谈。随后进入辩论与可能的修正阶段；之后通常还需对法案本身再次提出cloture以结束辩论，再进行最终全院投票（cloture后一般只需简单多数）。参议院9月份时间还算充裕。

2、但是众议院9月时间很紧张
本周众议院只有大约4个投票日，17号前后走人，21日、28日两周投票取消，下次正经碰面要等到中期选举后。

现在看参议院的版本已经和2025年众议院原版不是同一份东西，众议院必须再投——直接同意、来回改，或者开协商委员会。所以即便参议院这周走完全程，9月内法案送进白宫的概率非常低；

3、再下来就是中期选举后到27年1月3日
原来的议员们还在任这届国会还没散，清晰法案不用重提，可以继续调和。
但是2027年1月3日之后新一届国会开会，没过的法案就要作废，必须重新再提案了。

4、所以清晰法案之后几种可能情景
1）第一种明天60票不够。
今天新的文本让步不小，但民主党依然不满意，共和党也不保证全员到齐。
这一票黄了，2026年立法窗口基本关掉，后面就是新一届国会重新提案再走流程了。市场结构继续靠监管机构补丁推进；

2）第二种，cloture通过，参议院终票也通过。但众议院要等到跛脚鸭会期（中期选举之后到27年1月3日之前），这是眼下最接近“还活着”的路径：
参议院过关会被当成重大信号，但法律完成度还差众议院和总统签署。
选举结果会改定价：
两院格局不变，调和快一些；
参议院若易手，伦理和非法金融条款可能再加一轮码还要博弈。

3）第三种，参议院过了，12月众议院直接同意，总统签字。路径最短，时间也最紧张：
既要9月15日之后几天内收束辩论，还要在拨款期限里给加密腾位置。
有这种可能性，但很难是大概率情景。

4）第四种其实是第二种的恶化版，参议院通过了、卡在众议院重新讨论出现文同、再加上年底拨款法案更重要。清晰法案拖进2027年，那就是重新来过。跟第一种差不多了。

🚨NEWS: Senate Republicans have released new Clarity Act text featuring a revised ethics proposal agreed to by President Trump. 

The text also contains changes to the sections on the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA), stablecoin yield, and the so-called “Ag title.”

Republicans are calling it their “last, best and final” offer to Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s cloture vote.

Some high-level details.👇🏼

On BRCA: The provision has been narrowed to the Bank Secrecy Act and civil enforcement. Specific language extending its protections to criminal cases, including prosecutions under Section 1960, has been removed.

On ethics: Trump has agreed to what a GOP aide describes as “80%” of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal including to either divest “substantial” crypto-related financial interests or place them in a blind trust. It would also allow a role for state attorneys general to enforce ethics provisions, something which the White House had previously balked at.

On yield: Added “circuit breaker” language (floated by Tillis in July) that would effectively act as a backstop by allowing federal regulators to intervene if there was evidence of widespread deposit flight from community banks to stablecoins. The federal regulator that will be the arbiter of this: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

On Ag: The updated text adds tighter guardrails around vertical integration, including affiliate trading and conflicts of interest involving digital commodity exchanges, brokers and dealers. It also clarifies that state consumer protection laws still apply and that developer protections do not create exemptions from derivatives laws or impact prediction markets.

More to come in the @CryptoAmerica_ newsletter tomorrow AM.

🚨NEWS: Senate Republicans have released new Clarity Act text featuring a revised ethics proposal agreed to by President Trump. 

The text also contains changes to the sections on the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA), stablecoin yield, and the so-called “Ag title.”

Republicans are calling it their “last, best and final” offer to Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s cloture vote.

Some high-level details.👇🏼

On BRCA: The provision has been narrowed to the Bank Secrecy Act and civil enforcement. Specific language extending its protections to criminal cases, including prosecutions under Section 1960, has been removed.

On ethics: Trump has agreed to what a GOP aide describes as “80%” of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal including to either divest “substantial” crypto-related financial interests or place them in a blind trust. It would also allow a role for state attorneys general to enforce ethics provisions, something which the White House had previously balked at.

On yield: Added “circuit breaker” language (floated by Tillis in July) that would effectively act as a backstop by allowing federal regulators to intervene if there was evidence of widespread deposit flight from community banks to stablecoins. The federal regulator that will be the arbiter of this: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

On Ag: The updated text adds tighter guardrails around vertical integration, including affiliate trading and conflicts of interest involving digital commodity exchanges, brokers and dealers. It also clarifies that state consumer protection laws still apply and that developer protections do not create exemptions from derivatives laws or impact prediction markets.

More to come in the @CryptoAmerica_ newsletter tomorrow AM.

text:
人类刚刚把一只果蝇的神经系统，做成了可以到处插的「软件」。

现在它开始长出身体了。

Frank 发了一段很离谱的视频，一个 Strandbeest 小机器人在桌上爬，右上角实时跑着果蝇神经网络。机器人腿部的运动指令，来自这套神经网络的活动。视频目前已经超过百万播放。

这事得从 9 月 3 日说起。

Google Research、HHMI Janelia、剑桥等团队刚刚公开了成年雄性果蝇的完整中枢神经系统 connectome，166,700 个神经元，从脑一路连到腹神经索，包含约 1.24 亿个突触接触。 
这是第一个完整覆盖成年动物脑和神经索的连接图，可以一路追踪「眼睛看到东西」之后，信号怎么传到控制腿的神经元。

数据一开源，互联网就有人把这 16.67 万个神经元塞进 Minecraft；有人让它打 Doom、玩 Mario 64、Beat Saber；有人让它刷短视频；还有人让它看 K 线做加密货币交易。现在终于有人把输出接到了真实电机上，让它控制一具机械身体。

现在这些项目运行的是连接组上构建的简化神经动力学模型。Connectome 告诉我们哪些神经元彼此相连，但真实果蝇当时每颗神经元的膜电位、离子通道、神经调质、激素、突触动态和可塑性，并没有一起被扫描下来。

输入输出也需要人来接线。游戏画面刺激哪些神经元，哪些神经元的活动对应「左转」「跳跃」或者让机器人迈腿，都是开发者设计的接口。

所以我觉得这波最值得关注的地方，其实比「果蝇脑控制机器人」更怪。

以前科学家花几年画一张神经连接图，最后得到论文和数据库。现在数据发布十天，开发者已经在 GitHub 上 fork 它、给它装身体、塞进游戏、接摄像头、接强化学习，甚至准备往无人机上装。

我们可能正在看到一个很早期的新开发栈：

下载一颗大脑，给它接上感官，再给它找一具身体。

text:
Semiconductor Supply Chain News Roundup, September 14

1. Samsung Electro-Mechanics submitted TGV module samples for its glass substrate to TSMC for reliability verification two to three months ago, but the evaluation schedule has reportedly been delayed by more than a month.

As a result, the ordering schedule for some TGV related equipment that Samsung Electro-Mechanics had been preparing with its suppliers is understood to have been pushed back from the original plan.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics had originally targeted glass substrate mass production around 2027, building a pilot line and running customer evaluations. Earlier this year it revised the target for full operation to 2028, but with reliability verification and mass production process stabilization taking longer than expected, equipment investment is also not proceeding as originally planned.

2. A senior executive at Samsung Electro-Mechanics recently conveyed to employees a policy of moderating the pace of investment in the glass substrate business for the time being.

Rather than concentrating large scale investment on glass substrates, the direction is to prioritize investment in existing package substrate businesses such as FC-BGA and in high value added businesses with confirmed demand, such as MLCCs for AI and automotive applications.
Looking at the current state of Samsung Electro-Mechanics' glass substrate work, yields in the initial process of forming holes in the glass through laser processing and etching have risen to 90% or above, but in the subsequent processes of metallizing and filling the holes with copper, yields reportedly drop to around 30%.
After that, additional steps are still required, including chemical mechanical polishing (CMP), which flattens the substrate surface using chemical reactions and mechanical force, as well as cutting, and by that point yields become far too low.
That said, some argue that this adjustment itself should not be read as a delay in the glass substrate business as such. The market has not yet opened in earnest, and the actual customers, global semiconductor companies, are still carrying out their own preparation and validation for glass substrate adoption.

3. SK hynix is moving to lock in its equipment supply chain. The approach is to share medium to long term demand forecasts earlier than before so that suppliers can secure in advance the equipment and key components needed for future investment.

Previously, SK hynix shared investment plans with equipment makers covering about six months, or at most about a year. Going forward, it plans to present demand not only for next year but also for the year after, allowing suppliers to plan their production capacity and component procurement ahead of time.

4. SEMES, Samsung Electronics' semiconductor equipment subsidiary, is firming up the component supply chain for the hybrid bonder to be applied to next generation high bandwidth memory (HBM).
Specifically, SEMES has signed a supply agreement with the Korean subsidiary of HIWIN, a Taiwanese motion control company, for the Single Axis Stage, a precision drive component to be used in the hybrid bonder, and is currently conducting tests. HIWIN's product is being validated against SEMES' hybrid bonder specifications, and testing is understood to be in its final stages.
The single axis stage is a drive component that supports precise position control in the hybrid bonder. Because a hybrid bonder must align and bond chips at extremely fine pitches, it requires a high level of positional accuracy.
SEMES is said to be conducting equipment testing after signing a supply contract with a customer for a D2W (Die to Wafer) hybrid bonder for HBM. The industry views that customer as its parent company, Samsung Electronics.

5. PCB orders for SOCAMM2 destined for major memory makers including Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are growing beyond the levels planned at the start of the year.

The increase in orders for DDR5 RDIMM PCBs is especially pronounced. Compared with the order plans projected at the start of the year, the upward revision for RDIMM is understood to be even larger than that for SOCAMM2.
An industry source cited by the press said, "For SOCAMM2, order volumes are growing beyond what we expected at the start of the year, and we expect them to increase further into the second half," adding, "RDIMM orders are rising even more steeply relative to the beginning of year plan than SOCAMM2." The source also noted, "Some customers have already begun discussing advance orders for next year's volumes."

author: BurnieSendersX
quoted_text:
The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence. Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools. For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes. We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.

quoted_text:
I need to make a very PUBLIC announcement on behalf of younger GenXers and older Millennials.

If you see someone in their 40s or 50s who seems a little boring now, I need you to understand something...

We already got it in.

Like...GOT. IT. IN.

We are not sitting home on a Friday night because we never knew how to have fun.
We are sitting home on a Friday night because we have seen enough.

We went to parties in houses that should have been condemned and were almost certainly owned by the local drug dealer.

We saw police lights and RAN and not across a nice, flat field.
INTO THE WOODS.

Do you understand the athleticism required to hurdle uprooted tree roots in platform shoes while simultaneously trying to keep your low-rise jeans from sliding completely off your ass?

And somehow...we never spilled the Zima. We never spilled the Boone’s Farm.

That was TALENT. 

We slept on floors in strange houses because the designated driver either never showed up or, in a shocking turn of events, was drunker than everybody else.

There was no Uber, Life360 or Find My Friends.
There was just somebody named Mike saying, “I know a shortcut.”

And we FOLLOWED MIKE.

We closed down bars and then decided the night was still young, so we drove to Atlantic City, where we somehow managed to get drunk, sober up, get drunk again, sober up again and then get drunk a THIRD TIME before breakfast.

And according to our parents? We were at Michelle’s house.

Eating pizza and watching movies.

Michelle’s mother unknowingly covered for approximately 17 people every weekend. If there even was a Michelle.

We drank things called Purple Passion, Mad Dog 20/20 and whatever somebody mixed inside a giant plastic garbage can. Nobody asked what was in it. You grabbed a red Solo cup and trusted the process.

We went to clubs until the lights came on. Do you know the psychological damage of seeing a nightclub with the LIGHTS ON? Nothing good happens after those lights come on.

We danced for four straight hours in shoes that permanently altered the structure of our feet.

We made entire plans without cell phones...no texts, dropped pins or group chats...just an extremely questionable sense of direction.

We rode in cars with 11 people when the vehicle legally seated five. Someone was always sitting on someone. Someone was always in the hatchback.
And there was always one friend yelling, “DUCK!” when we passed a cop.

So yes...now we like being home.
We like sweatpants.
We like cancelling plans.
We like saying, “That sounds fun!” with absolutely no intention of attending.
We like restaurants at 5:30 because we can get a good table.
We like being home by 8:17.

And if someone texts at 9:30 PM and says, “What are you doing?”
Sleeping...we are sleeping.

Because this is not boring my friends...this is retirement.

We already played, partied and danced on the bar. 
We already ran from the cops through a wooded area dressed like a Spice Girl.

We have stories that cannot be posted because there are still people with careers, marriages and reputations to protect. And thank GOD there were no camera phones.

So kids, when you look at your Gen X and older Millennial parents sitting peacefully on the couch watching Dateline at 8 PM and think:
“God, you guys are boring.”

Sweetheart...oh sweetheart.
You are looking at retired legends.

Put some respect on our names. We're probably the reason Life360 was invented.

author: GONOGO_Korea
quoted_text:
🚨NEWS: Senate Republicans have released new Clarity Act text featuring a revised ethics proposal agreed to by President Trump. 

The text also contains changes to the sections on the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA), stablecoin yield, and the so-called “Ag title.”

Republicans are calling it their “last, best and final” offer to Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s cloture vote.

Some high-level details.👇🏼

On BRCA: The provision has been narrowed to the Bank Secrecy Act and civil enforcement. Specific language extending its protections to criminal cases, including prosecutions under Section 1960, has been removed.

On ethics: Trump has agreed to what a GOP aide describes as “80%” of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal including to either divest “substantial” crypto-related financial interests or place them in a blind trust. It would also allow a role for state attorneys general to enforce ethics provisions, something which the White House had previously balked at.

On yield: Added “circuit breaker” language (floated by Tillis in July) that would effectively act as a backstop by allowing federal regulators to intervene if there was evidence of widespread deposit flight from community banks to stablecoins. The federal regulator that will be the arbiter of this: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

On Ag: The updated text adds tighter guardrails around vertical integration, including affiliate trading and conflicts of interest involving digital commodity exchanges, brokers and dealers. It also clarifies that state consumer protection laws still apply and that developer protections do not create exemptions from derivatives laws or impact prediction markets.

More to come in the @CryptoAmerica_ newsletter tomorrow AM.

author: Scobleizer

text:
There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence. Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools. For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes. We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.

quoted_text:
My co-authors and I just published something in Clinical Psychology Review, and it's open access. It's called "One Size Fits None: A Call for an Idionomic Revolution."

We put together a story that has been sitting in plain sight. Applied psychology has made painfully slow progress, and part of the reason traces back to the ergodic error and to the racist, sexist, and antisemitic roots of traditional biostatistics. The majority of American Psychological Association presidents from 1892 to 1947 were card carrying eugenicists. The laws that later shaped the Holocaust were written here in the United States two decades earlier, with the active support of mainstream psychology. Most textbooks treat this as distant history. Almost none notice that the same assumptions still quietly define what we call good science.

This is an article of hope though. We lay out another way forward through the emerging science of idionomics, an approach that finally puts the individual client at the center. Do we know it will succeed? Honestly, no. But the path we have been on is scientifically and morally wrong, and if evidence based therapy is going to move ahead, it needs truly new ideas.

Read it here, for free: https://t.co/C5YlRIGE9g

text:
A few simple words on $TOOLS

0x4b7d1e5ec6889e63e70d39561edf925095dbed88 

If RH Chain continues to heat up, on-chain memes, launchpads, and trading volume will keep growing. That inevitably creates demand for an entry point where traders can spot new tokens first, scan them first, and catch the first wave.

RHTools is positioned right at that spot.

The most important part is that TOOLS is a single-chain vertical tool. If it can eventually become the Dexscreener of RH Chain, it will have a much easier time capturing the early traffic of a new chain than multi-chain platforms.

Last year, the leading crypto analytics platforms generated more than $45M in fees. If the TOOLS terminal actually gets users and its Swap generates real volume, those fees can continuously be used to buy back and burn the token.

Traders aren’t just buying a token called Tools. They’re buying this flywheel:

Chain heats up → More demand for trading / charting
→ More platform fees → More buybacks + burns
→ Lower supply + Narrative remains → Price becomes easier to push higher

When these three layers stack together, trading volume and market cap can rise quickly in the short term.

The same goes for the downside: when all three layers unwind together, the drawdown can also be very fast.

quoted_text:
There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

text: La historia se repite: AT&T pidió regulación a cambio de “servicio universal” y se quedó con el monopolio telefónico durante 70 años. El mundo pagó tarifas altas, tardó décadas en tener competencia real y equipos más baratos. Ganó AT&T. Las aerolíneas convencieron al gobierno de que había que regular por “seguridad y solvencia”. Resultado: cero nuevas aerolíneas interestatales en 40 años. Vuelos carísimos y para pocos. Ganaron Pan Am, TWA y las incumbentes. Hasta que desregularon y apareció Southwest. Los taxis pedían cupos y medallones limitados. Ciudades con pocos coches y precios altos. Ganaron los dueños de las licencias. Ahora OpenAI y Anthropic quieren “pace the frontier” con evaluadores y reglas que solo ellos pueden cumplir. Siempre es el mismo juego: la regulación que piden los que ya dominan no es para salvar al mundo. Es para que nadie más llegue.
author: minglaugodel
quoted_text:
Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead.

You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric — market share, revenue growth, model capability — the two of you have a duopoly on frontier intelligence. You’ve also claimed the lead is widening because of recursive self-improvement.

I don’t see what you see in the lab. If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible.

But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission. Stop pretending antitrust law has to be suspended so you can form a cartel. Stop pretending you need a regulatory approval process that supersedes product liability. Stop pretending METR is independent when it is intertwined with Anthropic’s investors and staff. Stop pretending you need those same evaluators to police competitors who aren’t even at the frontier.

Most of all, stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic. You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack. The market already punishes models that behave in unpredictable or unauthorized ways. After the Hugging Face episode, it is simply good business for OpenAI and Anthropic to trade some raw power for reliability and predictability. Call it alignment if you want. It is also just giving customers what they want.

Pacing the frontier would also create breathing room for a more intelligent conversation about regulation than Bernie Sanders’ “shut it all down.” China is very unlikely to join a global agreement, as you know, and that has to be taken into account as well.

So go ahead and pace the frontier. You are the ones setting it. The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it. Demanding your preferred regulatory framework as the price of that will look like blackmail of the public and the political system. So just do it.

If you do, you’ll buy goodwill for the next conversation. If you don’t, we’ll know this was just another bid for regulatory capture — or an election-season psyop.

author: lufeieth
quoted_text:
导致顶部区间卖出后，又追回去有很多原因，其中一个重要原因，就是：追求资产本位、股数本位(币圈的说法叫“币本位”）。

这非常致命。

在牛市末期，把“股数最大化、股数本位不能少”当成目标，会让减仓从一开始就处于心理劣势。

你即使已经兑现了可观的收益为现金，依旧会因为持股数量减少而觉得自己正在失去财富。

一旦采用这种标准：
1.卖出意味着股数减少，心理上容易被视为损失。
2.卖出后上涨，意味着同样的现金能买回的股数减少，进一步强化亏损感。
3.只有以后更低价买回、股数增加，才愿意承认卖出成功。

于是，一笔已经完成的盈利交易，又被附加了一个任务：
必须买回来，而且必须买回更多。

这会让退出策略明显复杂化。你既要降低风险，又要求未来恢复原有股数，还要求不能错过继续上涨。这些目标在某些行情中无法同时实现。

一旦在顶部区间、牛市末期锚定的是“股数本位、币本位”，这必定会造成卖出失败。
因为：
一种情况：你卖出后，股价继续涨，你的股数本位变少了，你害怕永远也买不回以前那么多股数了，追高买入。然后转入下跌行情；

一种情况：你卖出后，骨架下跌，你觉得自己现在买回来股数变多了，觉得自己成功做了个波段，还降低成持仓成本，沾沾自喜。但其实股价后面会下跌50%、甚至80%。

Back on @ponsdotfamily, we’ve watched a bunch of projects get rinsed off RHC over the last week, but if anything it’s reinforcing my view.

Pons is basically a leveraged bet on RH Chain throughput, more than just the biggest launchpad sitting on RHC.

And it’s worth factoring in that Circle’s Arc Public mainnet goes live in two days. Another fresh narrative could easily pull speculative liquidity away from RH, the same way SOL did last week.

That said, I doubt it reaches anything like RHC’s hype, most of what’s coming over there looks like launchpads remixing LONG, Stonk, or PONS with a new coat of paint.

Also keep in mind memecoin volume comes in waves, and it feels like we’re entering the second phase: utility-leaning launches on RHC through Pons. A ton of issuance still funnels through Pons, and it keeps cranking out the most “real” graduates.

That said, if daily protocol revenue slides to ~$200–300k and sticks, the multiple will re-rate up, the buyback bid gets thinner, and that likely bleeds through to $PONS too.

However, Pons is no longer only the RH version of Pump.

It is becoming the issuance venue for a hybrid product, meme + tokenized equity + Utilities, that other chains cannot copy without the same RWA stack.

这非常致命。

在牛市末期，把“股数最大化、股数本位不能少”当成目标，会让减仓从一开始就处于心理劣势。

你即使已经兑现了可观的收益为现金，依旧会因为持股数量减少而觉得自己正在失去财富。

一旦采用这种标准：
1.卖出意味着股数减少，心理上容易被视为损失。
2.卖出后上涨，意味着同样的现金能买回的股数减少，进一步强化亏损感。
3.只有以后更低价买回、股数增加，才愿意承认卖出成功。

一种情况：你卖出后，股价继续涨，你的股数本位变少了，你害怕永远也买不回以前那么多股数了，追高买入。然后转入下跌行情；

author: lufeieth
quoted_text:
在大涨一波/顶部区间卖出后，最危险的行为，就是：卖出后，股价还在继续涨，甚至某一天还会大涨，然后因为fomo或踏空感极其强烈，经不住诱惑，又重仓买回去了。

刚买进去，因为是在相对高位追进去，买点很不好，这时候如果来一个下跌，是否止损、以及止损点很不明确。

如果反复这样折腾两次，最后心力消耗殆尽，无力也无信心管理仓位。最后导致仓位管理一塌糊涂、出现大幅回撤。这是最要警惕的。

德鲁肯米勒在2020年初犯过这个严重的错误。2020年1月止盈走人，2月观望，看着大盘继续大涨，3月10日忍不住了，在纳指见顶前1小时（当天收盘于历史最高点5048点），一口气梭哈买入约 60 亿美元科技股。当时量子基金的规模约130-140亿美元，相当于接近基金一半仓位。

然后开始否认现实、幻想反弹，认为自己重仓买入后的下跌只是回调，没有止损，依旧坚定持有，最后短时间就出现巨大回撤。

出现这个问题的关键，就是：卖出的节奏除了问题，仓位要分类，卖出要分批有节奏，不要一把就在左侧卖光；以及卖出后的现金管理问题，让给自己设置强制约束，让自己即便在大脑出现fomo和无法控制的情况下，也无法动用已卖出的现金重新入场。解决这个问题，要从这两方面入手。

quoted_text:
关于“卖的过早，继续涨，因踏空fomo又更大的重仓追高，立马迎来下跌，大亏”：

上涨趋势中可以分多批卖，但不要全部清仓，一定要留最后一部分在明确破位下跌阶段才清仓。（即便在明确破位下跌后及时卖出，也其实是卖在相当好的高位。）

否则在上涨阶段完全卖出后，如果继续涨，没有仓位，踏空感会非常强，就会fomo，脑子一热，很容易重仓追。这时往往就是顶部，开始下跌，损失惨重。

ChatGPT的解读：
上涨趋势里不要把仓位清到零，否则容易因踏空而情绪化追高，进而在下跌时受重伤。

一个典型的例子，就是管理量子基金的斯坦利·德鲁肯米勒（Stan Druckenmiller）的“踏空→FOMO重仓→迅速亏损”：

- 背景：1999年末至2000年初，他最初没有跟上科网股末段疯涨。

- 关键动作：他自己复盘说，“我能感觉到（行情）要来了，我就是忍不住要上”，结果在2000年3月附近冲进去，一口气买了约60亿美元的科技股，几乎是在顶部附近一小时内进场。

- 结果：6周内亏了约30亿美元，他坦言“我本来就知道不该那么做（却还是做了）”。这是教科书式的：踏空后的情绪化补仓。

两条实操纪律
- 分段止盈：移动止盈/目标位分批落袋，避免“一次性判断失败”。

- 永不清零：趋势里保留10–20%“观察仓”，清零只绑定客观破位/回撤，不绑定“感觉涨多了”。

text:
In 2016, I ran away from home to live in the capital of my home country, leaving my small town. I dropped out of university, where I had been studying journalism. Then I enrolled in cybersecurity - and dropped out of university again.

While looking for work, I completely by chance landed an SMM role at an ICO project. That’s when I first learned about cryptocurrencies.

Later I left for a while to work at a large bank. I ended up in a security-related position and learned from the best - experienced, bearded cybersecurity specialists.

In 2018 I got into an argument with a random person in a chat. He organized a swatting against me, and I became afraid to leave the house.

That’s how I discovered OSINT and OpSec. I started getting interested in it and gradually found my way into cryptocurrency theft investigations.

From 2018 to 2020 I worked for an online casino. We were under every kind of attack 24/7. That’s where I gained experience.

In 2021, an acquaintance from chat called me the day before New Year’s and said he needed someone for a community manager role. I hesitated at first, but agreed. That’s how I ended up in a DeFi project. Before that, I knew nothing about DeFi.

Gradually, people in the project asked me to make a Twitter account (at the time I was better known on Clubhouse - if you even remember that). 

That’s also how I discovered LobsterDAO (one of the participants simply suggested I join the chat and talk to people there).
Suddenly my X account started gaining popularity. I didn’t expect that.

I found a job at an auditing firm and tried to work on audits. In 2024 I took a severe hit to my health. Because of that, I lost my job and my income.

Two years later - problems again, emergency surgery, a long recovery.

And here I am. I hope things will get better from here.

text:
没有死去的赛道，只有失败的形态。

最早的预测市场不叫 Polymarket，叫 Augur，2015 年就已经存在。只看设计的话，它和 Polymarket 几乎是两种生物。
同样的剧本也发生在 DEX 身上。以太坊上的第一个 DEX 不是 Uniswap，而是 EtherDelta。作为一个链上订单簿，EtherDelta 要求用户自己挂单、自己吃单，体验极其笨重，失败的结局从一开始就写好了。

所以在 Crypto, 赛道的熄火往往不是需求错了，而是形态错了。我们曾经失败过的所有尝试，比如 NFT、GameFi、SocialFi, 都会在某个意想不到的时刻，换个形态卷土重来。
比如今年最火的 FOMO，本质上就是 SocialFi 的一种变种。但 SocialFi 的想象力，远不止于此。

1/ 以前的 SocialFi，都做错了一件事
过去的 SocialFi 几乎都犯了同一个错误，把社交当产品，把交易当附加功能。要么是在一个社交平台里硬塞一个钱包，要么是在一个交易平台里加一个评论区。

 @MinddotWTF 的设计则完全不同，社交本身就是市场结构。
它的核心规则只有四条：

▌ 发帖即买入
你在 https://t.co/6xArRXgJnK 上发一条帖子，只要提到一个带 $ 的词，比如 $AI，系统就会用你钱包里的资金，自动买入一笔 $AI 代币。
但这不是付费发帖。你投入的本金会沿着关键词曲线买入代币。你可以继续持有，也可以随时卖出退出。
表达观点，就必须用真金白银下注。

▌ 一个词，就是一个市场
一个关键词只对应一个市场。
为什么这很重要？因为传统 Memecoin 平台有个致命伤，同名碎片化。一个叙事爆火时，会冒出十几个同名代币。热度退去后，流动性和社区散落在不同的代币里。
https://t.co/6xArRXgJnK 用唯一性来解决问题。
无论一个词下面有十条还是十万条帖子，都只有一个市场。
内容无限，资产集中。叙事不断变化，公共坐标永久存在。

▌ 持币即投票
规则很简单：
投票方向，由你的钱包签名决定
投票权重，由你持有的关键词代币数量决定
每个关键词，都是一个独立的治理单元
持有 $AI，你就只能给 $AI 社区的内容点赞成或反对；持有 $DOGE，你就管不了 $AI 的事。
只有真正关心这个社区、并为之出资的人，才能决定什么内容被看见。

▌ 交易即浪潮
前三条规则，已经让每个关键词都像一个独立运转的小国家。https://t.co/6xArRXgJnK 更特别的，是让这些彼此独立的市场继续保持连接。
平台设计了一个名为“RGB 层”的公共空间。当你买入某个关键词时，不仅会推动这个词本身的价格，也会推动整个平台的上涨。

与此同时，用户还可以获得两层额外收益。

第一层：买入额度循环
它的运作方式是：
你使用 1 SOL 的买入额度完成买入
系统向你发放 2 个新邀请码
每个邀请码对应 1 SOL 的买入资格
朋友使用你的邀请码买满 1 SOL 后，你会恢复 1 SOL 的买入额度
恢复后的额度可以再次使用，并继续产生新的邀请码
买入额度并不是平台赠送的 SOL，而是一种买入资格。每次买入，用户仍然需要支付真实资金。

第二层：手续费分成
你邀请的用户，此后每次通过发帖完成买入，手续费中的 80% 直接分成给你。
这些收益会在每笔买入发生时自动结算，不需要手动领取。

2/ SocialFi，已经进化到 3.0
如果把 SocialFi 粗分成三代，逻辑会非常清晰。

1.0 创作者经济，代表是 Rally。核心是帮创作者变现。
2.0 去中心化社交图谱，代表是 Lens、Farcaster。核心是把关系和数据还给用户。
3.0 注意力即市场，代表是 https://t.co/6xArRXgJnK。核心是把发帖、交易、治理统一为一个动作。

拿它和 https://t.co/Vsiq8445md 对比，区别就更明显了。
https://t.co/Vsiq8445md 的逻辑是，我付费购买你的访问权，进入一个私密聊天室。社交内容和交易资产是分离的。
https://t.co/6xArRXgJnK 的逻辑是，一个关键词就是一个注意力市场。你发帖表达对叙事的看法，同时必须用资本为这个叙事下注。

3/ 一次高难度的实验
https://t.co/6xArRXgJnK 彻底抛弃了传统社交的广场模式，试图用一个原子动作，把社交表达、交易、社区治理全部统一起来。
它的优点是设计极具想象力，但机制比较复杂。作为一次高实验性的设计，它能否成功，只能留给时间来检验。

text:
PONS未来一定能成长成10B的大标，原因如下：

1. Robinhood的团队，非常善于造热点。

这一点从Robinhood创始人持续给市场制造话题，天天给KOL送CX话题就可以看出。

这其实和现在的BSC很像。Robinhood团队最大的故事是什么？几千万传统Web2券商散户。

对于我来说，这几千万散户可能没什么价值，但对于币圈KOL来说，这简直就是他们最喜欢的CX点。

币圈本质就是一个热度市场。Robinhood手里握着巨大的流量，只要Robinhood稍微放个屁，一堆KOL就会跟着附和。

所以总结一下：
Robinhood不缺会玩的创始人，也不缺给它舔脚的KOL。

2. Robinhood真正想做的，其实是RWA。

但RWA有一个天然的问题：真正的大规模用户还没来。
尤其是亚洲、非洲、拉美这些潜在增量市场（欧美市场根本不需要链上美股，因此我说robinhood的几千万散户没有价值），RWA真正完全落地可能还需要5-10年。

所以Robinhood现在需要解决的问题很简单：在RWA真正爆发之前，怎么持续制造用户和热度？

答案就是——Meme。结果非常理想。他娘的，赌狗全来了。所以Robinhood第一批用户，本质上就是一群Web3赌狗。

这也是为什么现在Robinhood生态里，Meme项目这么多。

但这反而给PONS带来了一个非常重要的东西：
持续不断的流量。

RWA可能是5-10年的长期故事，但Meme可以每天给你制造热度。而PONS，就是被动吃掉这些热度。

3. PONS上面不只有Meme，还有大量DeFi项目在发射。

为什么？因为PONS他娘的真的大方。70%的LP费用给项目方，剩下30%中的80%直接回购并销毁代币。对于一个DeFi项目来说，最难的事情是什么？

冷启动。

产品再好，如果没人知道，也没卵用。而PONS发射台现在恰恰是一个自带流量的发射平台。

第一波热度已经来了。现在已经有数不清的项目方在制作垃圾项目——当然，中间也会有少数真正不错的项目，这些项目都需要抢流量。

而PONS目前就是那个最有热度的台子。没有之一。

于是出现一个很有意思的飞轮：项目越多 → 热度越高 → 交易越多 → 手续费越多 → 回购越多 → PONS持有者持续吃到收益。

这些项目方，本质上都在给PONS持有者送钱。

4. Robinhood现在的TVP还很低。目前只有大约 1B。

我的判断是：
做到5B，可能根本不需要一年。一旦Robinhood生态规模持续增长，成为TVL Top 5，我认为几乎是板上钉钉的事情。

更重要的是：未来会不断有新的DeFi项目、链游项目、Meme项目，甚至各种类型的代币在Robinhood生态里发射。

而这些项目产生的收入，其中一部分最终都会变成：
PONS螺旋升天的燃料。

很少有一个标的，能让我这么看好。当然，我上面说的任何一点，都欢迎反驳。

我认为这套逻辑是非常自洽的：
Robinhood负责造流量 → Meme负责吸引第一批用户 → PONS负责承接项目 → 项目越多，交易越多 → 手续费越多 → 回购越多 → PONS继续上涨。

author: jasonlk
quoted_text:
The Latest CRO Confidential with @samdblond s out! "$0 to $600M in Under 4 Years. The ElevenLabs GTM Playbook"

Carles Reina was the fourth employee and first GTM hire at ElevenLabs. Four years later: $600M+ ARR and an $11B valuation. Today he's a Partner at Baobab Ventures, helping the next generation of startups scale.

In the latest CRO Confidential, hosted by Sam Blond (CEO and Co-Founder of Monaco), Carles breaks down exactly how they built it. The revenue ramp alone is jaw-dropping:

$0 to $100M ARR in 20 months
$100M to $200M in another 10 months
$200M to $330M in another 5 months
$330M to $600M+ in another 6 months

#1. Distribution from day one

ElevenLabs never bet on a single channel. Every market got its own thesis: why launch here, direct or reseller, what does GTM look like in the first 90 days? Core markets were sold direct; everywhere else, resellers got the technology into market fast. Distribution plus relentless experimentation was the whole game.

#2. The grants program that killed the competition

Carles came back from holiday with one question: how do I kill my competition? The answer: give startups with 25 or fewer employees free credits for 3 months. They gave out tens of thousands of grants, made a ton of noise about it, and pulled demand away from every competitor in the market. Over 10% of ElevenLabs' enterprise revenue eventually came from upselling those grant recipients as they grew.

#3. The 20X quota model

This one's controversial. At ElevenLabs, a $100k base salary meant a $2M quota — 20x — with uncapped commissions. Reps regularly hit 300-600% of target, and average attainment across the entire GTM org ran 167% every single quarter. Carles' theory: he'd rather have a lean team of killers crushing quota than a bloated team missing it and complaining. And when a market genuinely broke, they'd grant quota relief — the commitment was that comp would always stay fair.

#4. Only pay commissions on recurring revenue

Sign a giant one-off or a 2-month POC? Zero commission — because it added nothing to valuation. Roughly $1M of real recurring revenue was worth ~$33M in valuation, and reps were paid generously on that. Incentivize the outcome that matters, not the inputs.

#5. What he'd do differently: enablement and senior sellers, earlier

Two regrets. First, sales enablement came too late — it's always underinvested until the team is too big to onboard properly. Second, hire senior sellers earlier. Hungry young reps are great, but people with 20 years of relationships who know procurement compress timelines dramatically. Either regret fixed might have gotten them to a billion faster.

#6. Wire AI into GTM, but sell the team on productivity, not replacement

Carles pitched the founders on building an AI SDR, an AI AE, and an AI customer success manager. The team's first reaction: "am I going to get replaced?" They proved the opposite. The AI SDR answered inbound emails in minutes and improved conversion rates. The AI CSM worked long-tail and mid-market upsells automatically — and the human account owners still got paid the commission. Productivity story, not replacement story.

#7. Test 100 things. You only need one to work

Carles told the team he only needed one experiment to hit to add another $100M in ARR. So run everything in parallel, kill what fails fast, and treat a failed experiment as a win — you learned something. Add to that: make it insanely easy to do business with you, from pricing to onboarding to time-to-value.

👉 Distribution is everything, incentivize recurring revenue (not meetings), be famously fair to your salespeople — reps who get rich make everyone around them believe — and let AI do the work agents are best at while humans do the relationships and the creative bets no agent would ever come up with.

Watch the full episode: https://t.co/H4d5GI1GfP
