text:
Why do I hear so much talk about 911 being an inside job?  The LIHOP theory.
Isn't it rational to assume that US agencies simply failed to talk to each other?   

The other side of the argument:

The argument against the "confluence of incompetence" theory hinges on statistical probability and the active—rather than passive—nature of the intelligence failures. 

To accept incompetence as the sole explanation requires believing that the most sophisticated, redundant security apparatus in human history experienced a total, simultaneous, and unprecedented collapse across every single layer of its defense architecture on the exact same morning.

​The Improbability of Simultaneous Failure

National defense is engineered with overlapping redundancies specifically to prevent single-point failures. If the CIA fails to track a target, the FBI is supposed to catch them domestically. If the FAA loses a plane, NORAD radar tracks it and intercepts it.

 On September 11, every single redundant system across the FAA, NORAD, CIA, FBI, and NSA failed simultaneously. The mathematical probability of a universally catastrophic, multi-agency system failure occurring purely by chance on the exact morning a terror cell decided to strike is vanishingly small.

​Active Suppression of Competence

True incompetence usually manifests as a failure to act—dropping the ball. The intelligence failures leading up to 9/11 required aggressive, active effort from management to shut down competent agents who had already found the ball.

​FBI headquarters repeatedly and aggressively blocked field agent Colleen Rowley in Minneapolis from obtaining a warrant to search Zacarias Moussaoui's laptop after he exhibited highly suspicious behavior at a flight school.

​The CIA's Alec Station actively prohibited their own FBI liaisons from sharing the domestic presence of known Al-Qaeda operatives with law enforcement.
These were not passive oversights; they were deliberate, documented management decisions to halt active investigations.

​The Subversion of Standard Operating Procedure
Scrambling fighter jets to intercept off-course or unresponsive commercial aircraft was not a novel challenge; NORAD's Standard Operating Procedure for this had been executed flawlessly over 100 times in the year prior to 9/11. 

Yet on that morning, the system was entirely paralyzed. This paralysis was severely exacerbated by multiple, overlapping military exercises (such as Vigilant Guardian) taking place that exact day, which involved injecting simulated hijackings onto radar screens. 

The odds of an unprecedented terrorist attack perfectly mirroring and overlapping with military simulations designed to test those exact scenarios stretches the limits of coincidence.

​The Reward of Failure
In a functional bureaucracy, catastrophic incompetence results in firings, demotions, and criminal negligence charges. Following 9/11, virtually no one in the upper echelons of the CIA, FBI, FAA, or military intelligence was fired or held professionally accountable for the "incompetence" that allowed the attacks to succeed. 

Instead, key figures responsible for the most glaring intelligence blockages were quietly promoted, awarded medals (such as CIA Director George Tenet receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom), or given lucrative private-sector security contracts.

​When "incompetence" requires aggressive management to maintain, perfectly aligns with pre-existing geopolitical goals, and is ultimately rewarded rather than punished, basic analytical models suggest it is no longer incompetence—it is a functional strategy.

Altman补充发文称，AI发展有两种必须避免的糟糕结局：一是人类失去对未来的掌控，这绝不可接受，AI必须始终服务于人类；

二是权力过度集中——若某个极其强大的AI被单一个人或公司用来将自身世界观强加于所有人，后果可能极其反乌托邦。

他表示，避开这两种威胁需要走一条狭窄的中间道路，例如某个国家或某个实验室获得过大权力都属需警惕的情形。

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

如果把人生当企业来经营，经营得好有很多要素，比如金钱、健康、良好的人际关系等等，但是这些都不是人生经营的终极目标，只是通向目标的众多手段之一，人生经营的终极目的是幸福。
就好像丰沛的原材料、优秀的管理层、发达高效的分销网络都非常重要，但不是经营企业的终极目目的，经营企业的终极目的是盈利。

“获得幸福”本身就是一种关键技能，可以习得，可以提升。
这种能力对于人生相当于一种全局性的经营杠杆，直接作用于终极目标，值得花很多时间练习。
反之，警惕无限优化通向目标的手段（赚钱能力、社交能力、身体素质），而是多花时间围绕终极目标进行思考和优化，在获得幸福上的效用会大得多，而且这种能力会反过头来指引我们在各项手段上的优化投入，是非常划算的。
当我们认可获得幸福是一种能力，可以单项修炼，而不是默认来自于我们完成某些事项之后的被动获得（比如开上豪车，让孩子上 985，成为地位尊崇的人），开始理解和接纳这个观念本身开始，我们就获得了巨大的人生幸福经营杠杆。

text:
The AI developer roadmap is changing pretty fast.
Learning Python + APIs + basic LLM prompting isn't enough anymore.

The interesting layer is becoming...
→ AI coding agents
→ tool calling
→ MCP
→ agent memory and state
→ RAG and retrieval
→ evals
→ observability
→ agent security
→ AI infrastructure
→ model routing
→ multi-agent systems

But there's another shift happening. You don't just need to know how to use AI. You need to understand how to build systems around AI.
How do you give an agent access to tools safely?
How do you recover when it fails?
How do you evaluate whether it's actually improving?
How do you control cost and latency?
How do you give it enough context without drowning it in information?

That's where a lot of the engineering opportunity is moving.
If I were starting AI development in 2026, I'd focus less on collecting AI tools and more on learning how to build reliable AI systems.

The models will keep changing. The engineering principles will stay.

quoted_text:
Law enforcers already have authority to charge companies and their CEOs for creating and releasing dangerous, unvetted, or defective products. We shouldn’t let discussions about new legal regimes distract from the fact that there’s no AI exemption from laws already on the books — a point @FTC emphasized repeatedly during my tenure.

1. There is an extensive set of laws that govern dangerous and defective products. For example, releasing unvetted AI models or agents can violate consumer protection laws. Shipping flawed AI tools without implementing adequate measures to detect and stop rogue or defective AI agents can be an “unfair or deceptive” act or practice under the FTC Act (and analogous state laws). And some state AGs are already exploring holding AI firms and their CEOs criminally liable when their models participate in criminal activity.

2. Existing laws also prohibit “unfair methods of competition.” This covers instances where AI firms appropriate the competitively sensitive information of their customers, including through tracking their use of various tools. It can also cover instances where firms pursue dangerous behavior, aware that doing so may compel rivals to do the same.

As the Supreme Court has noted: “A method of competition which casts upon one's competitors the burden of the loss of business unless they will descend to a practice which they are under a powerful moral compulsion not to adopt, even though it is not criminal, was thought to involve the kind of unfairness at which the [unfair methods of competition] statute was aimed."

3. The highly concentrated and interconnected structure of these markets could be creating major risks and conflicts of interest. We had started investigating these partnerships and cross-investments across the stack (and released a preliminarily overview of some findings: https://t.co/jJ5cS3Pin3). 

Both federal and state enforcers should be scrutinizing these opaque relationships and inter-dependencies. We are already seeing how these relationships could undermine accountability. For example, OpenAI could face liability given the Hugging Face incident, but Hugging Face being bought up by Nvidia means that we’re unlikely to see it file a lawsuit over this — given Nvidia’s strong incentive to see OpenAI continue full speed ahead.

4. As AI tools dramatically change the landscape of cybersecurity risks and hacks, all businesses should be doubling down on having core security protections in place. Firms that fail to invest in adequate data security measures or fix known vulnerabilities can also be breaking the law. A recent analysis showed that around 1/3 of Fortune 100 companies do not even have a way to notify them about security issues. During my @FTC tenure, we sued firms for poor data security practices and held CEOs liable when they were personally responsible.

https://t.co/nwZ5Av8fOK

https://t.co/KjRye8y9SY

5. As policymakers consider new legal regimes, we should be looking to lessons from prior efforts to govern major sectors, such as banking and other networks, platforms, and utilities. Tools like structural separations, nondiscrimination, and supervision could be key, and there’s a rich history of what works and what doesn’t. But we can and must pursue any new efforts alongside enforcing existing laws.

Now back to building.

That said, if daily protocol revenue slides to ~$200–300k and sticks, the multiple will re-rate up, the buyback bid gets thinner, and that likely bleeds through to $PONS too.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

quoted_text:
DTEF 不出意外地又又又一次延迟上线了。

这里来提一嘴 @downto_finance 官方明确预警可能会引发 $DTF 盘口大跌的staking:

DETF 协议9月4日上线了 $DTF staking: 但这并不是我们所理解的赚取协议分成的staking，而是dev 为表歉意开放给持币者赚取收益的staking。

dev 拿出600万枚 $DTF 作为这个临时质押池的奖励，我算的staking 收益大概日化2-3% 这样，质押代币不锁仓，随存随取。原计划是在3天后的9月7日结束，还留在质押池里的币会自动迁移成协议的rebase 代币给到质押者。

协议端的操作是在二级市场上卖掉部分质押池里的 $DTF 来买 $ETH，组成LP 对注入现在的 $DTF - $ETH 池子，这部分流动性由协议拥有(POL); $DTF 盘口的波动有多大，很大程度上取决于质押池里剩余的代币有多少，所以官方才警告迁移可能砸盘。

质押者拿到对应的协议rebase 代币，相当于一张永不关闭的Bond NFT 收益凭证，无法close 换回 $DTF 现货，尚不清楚能否通过二级市场买卖。等协议正式上线后，任何人mint/ bond 都会给rebase token 持有者分免费的篮子份额，具体的分成比例官方尚未公布。

这个类Ponzi 玩法也就不难理解了：

DETF 协议鼓励用户质押 $DTF 拿rebase token 获得永久的来自mint/ bond 玩家的篮子份额分成权，通过协议套利/ 投机的mint/ bond 玩家越多，rebase token 持有者的收益越高；从而激励更多用户从二级市场买入 $DTF 质押成rebase token 拿篮子份额的分成权；

这部分质押的 $DTF 又被用来买进 $DTF- $ETH 流动性，作为协议自有流动性POL 增厚LP 池的深度。

quoted_text:
StablePair Hook实施的池子只能是“假定或相信”池子的两个资产不久都能回铆，所以早期只有usdt-usdc、usdt-usdg这两个池子。
在窄带交易，正常手续费；
脱离窄带时，谁的交易继续拉开窄带，免手续费，因为“假定里”交易者亏了，池子赚了；
脱离窄带时，谁的交易拉回窄带，即接受手续费荷兰拍卖，因为“假定里”交易者在套利赚了，要分一部分利润给池子，分多少市场说了算，套利者自己竞价接受拍卖。

这个荷兰拍卖师承uni的销毁机制，还有uni上ido机制，一切市场说了算，不应该在一切交易前假定一个价格或费率。

text:
现行 RAG 架构犯过最反人类的错误，就是把一本结构严谨的书，撕成几千张碎纸条再去搜，把厚厚的法规、合同按 500 字切成碎纸条丢进向量库，

这根本不叫检索，这叫在碎纸机里碰运气，
IBM 刚挂出的这篇论文直接把窗户纸给捅破了：
人类查书从来都是先翻目录，把这个习惯教给模型，检索命中率从 68% 狂飙到 82.6%：

回顾一下现在全网知识库是怎么干活的：
把几百页的法律法规、员工手册、技术白皮书，机械地按 500 个 Token 暴力切碎、转成向量塞进向量库；
只要用户一提问，就在库里找几个最相似的碎片塞进 Prompt 里。
这种做法在工程上极其愚蠢：
因为在切碎的瞬间，章节从属、因果推导与上下文拓扑被全部物理切断；
大模型一看到长文本，就陷入著名的“迷失在中间（Lost in the middle）”，开始一本正经地凭空胡编。

真实人类查书从来不会这么干。
你查《刑法》不会撕成纸条去盲抽，而是先看目录：
民主制度 $\to$ 选举制度与政党 $\to$ 翻到对应小节精读。

IBM 团队刚挂出来的重磅论文 STAIR（arXiv:2609.03874），
用一种极度返璞归真的“生成式检索”，把这个人类常识做成了工业级系统：

看懂它的技术实现，你会发现它比盲目堆向量高维得多：

1️⃣ 提取真实目录树，以“小节”为最小单元：
直接从 PDF 提取完整的 Table of Contents，检索目标不再是切碎的碎片，而是作者亲笔写的叶子章节标题；
2️⃣ 约束解码，堵死幻觉：
拿 7B 小模型微调，输入是“整本目录树 + 你的问题”，输出只能是一个合法的章节名！
因为加了硬约束解码，模型根本没有机会去捏造不存在的伪章节，虚构章节的幻觉率从原生模型的 24% 断崖式砸到了不到 0.05%！
3️⃣ 硬核基准实测数据（拒绝营销夸大）：
在覆盖医学、金融、法律等 6 大领域的 18 本公开教材（SearchTome 基准）测试中：
• 传统关键词 BM25：命中率 59.5%
• 经典向量检索 DPR：命中率 68.7%
• 最强对照 DSI：命中率 76.9%
• IBM STAIR：直接干到了 82.6%！
（顺便打个假：网传所谓的“把 GraphRAG 摩擦”纯属吹牛，论文压根没测 GraphRAG，80.6% 也只是自然科学单科成绩，全科平均是 82.6%）。

当然，必须客观划清它的适用边界：
它极其适合教材、法规、合同、技术手册这类“本来就带着清晰层级标题”的大部头；
面对没有目录的乱麻 Slack 聊天记录或流水账网页，它也巧妇难为无米之炊。

但它证明了一个至关重要的工程哲学：
检索不准，才是大模型幻觉真正的上游水龙头；
别再迷信无限扩大的上下文窗口了，
教会大模型学会先读目录、再按图索骥去翻书，往往比无脑烧算力强上一万倍。

text:
Sam Altman 刚刚又发了一条，把昨天那场“要不要主动减速”的争论讲得更具体了。

他的态度其实很明确：

AI 不需要停止，但前沿实验室应该主动让它发展得慢一点。

昨天 David Sacks 回应 Dario 和 Sam 时说得很直接：

你们自己就是前沿，如果真觉得模型越来越危险，那就自己慢下来，不需要等政府给你们反垄断豁免，也不需要假装必须先建立一套监管体系。

Sam 这次基本正面接住了这个问题。

他说，确实不用等。

OpenAI 现在已经开始改变自己的开发流程。

过去的 Preparedness Framework，主要是在一个模型训练完成后，判断它能不能安全发布。

但现在，OpenAI 开始把安全检查往训练阶段前移：

如果一次强化学习训练预计会显著提升模型能力，在训练开始之前，就要先建立明确的 Safety Case，证明这次训练可以安全进行。

也就是说，以前是：

模型练出来 → 测一下危险不危险 → 决定发不发。

现在开始变成：

模型还没练 → 先证明我们有能力控制它 → 再继续训练。

而且 Sam 认为，这套东西不应该只有 OpenAI 做。

包括失控风险、模型监控、安全标准，都应该在前沿实验室之间逐渐形成共同标准，甚至引入独立审计。

但他特意强调了一句：

所谓放慢节奏，不是停止 AI。

AI 依然会快速进步。

只是 Safety Case、监控、评估这些东西都会增加开发成本，让能力提升比“什么安全措施都不做”更慢一些。

Sam 的原话意思非常直接：

这个减速成本值得付。

任何来自美国国内的竞争压力，都不能成为鲁莽开发的理由，更不能让模型能力跑到对齐和监控能力前面。

至于真正需要政府出面的地方，他认为主要是国际协调。

但在那之前：

前沿 AI 公司没必要等任何人，可以先从自己开始踩刹车。
author: MaxForAI
quoted_text:
The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence. Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools. For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes. We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.

Pre Market Thoughts - 14 Sep 26

Asia semis took an initial leg down with KOSPI and NKY both down for the day thus far. $KOSPI is down about 3% on the day, dragged down by $00660 (down 6%ish) to the 1.7m KRW support levels.

This week is also shaping up to be an eventful week. We have FOMC in the middle, the fate of Clarity act and also the labs dropping news of their collaboration/collusion over the weekend.

Lets unpack each of them. First, on the labs collaborating to "slow down" for safety. I dont see a read through into capex reduction. Anthropic has signaled a tripling of its compute commitments to 517B from 180B. Instead, this is the labs trying to shift away from training workloads into inference workloads (which they can monetize).

Alongside, on FOMC - the bank consensus is for a hike. What becomes important is whether this is a once and done hike or the start of a "hiking cycle". I personally think that aside from semis, there are very few sectors that would be able to endure tighter financial conditions.

On the clarity act passage and crypto - i dont have a read on this. However, i think this is more impactful for the majors. Should clarity fail to pass, i also foresee regulators giving guidance which should ameliorate the situation of failing to pass.

My game plan for this week would be to bid any dips on semis before FOMC. I think the mainstream read on the "slowdown" is bearish for semis is totally wrong. If anything, it shores up the monetization for the labs and is very bullish for the entire sector.

On crypto, same opinion as before. More importantly, Open source AI is a theme that i think is critical. I would rank it alongside privacy in terms of the secular tailwinds for the theme. I would use the weakness as an opportunity to add on those names that i like.

In 2017, I visited Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia, China, on a research trip. It has a cold high-altitude climate with vast cheap land and abundant wind farms, built aggressively since 2013. It was a completely life-changing trip. 

An energy-efficiency powerhouse has always been its vision; I just never thought then that it would translate into a massive data-centre build-out now.

I recommend visiting Huiteng Xile Grassland for horseback riding amongst wind turbines before travelling to Hohhot for yurt stays.
author: hananyss
quoted_text:
By now, it's amply clear that the big bosses of US frontier AI labs are really, really scared of China. 

And, fascinatingly, part of the answer why might be a tiny place in Inner Mongolia that you've probably never heard of: Ulanqab prefecture.

Heard of it? Didn't think so. 

Even myself, who's traveled to Inner Mongolia twice, had never heard of it before researching this story.

This is because, at first glance, this place is pretty unremarkable. Check its Wikipedia page (https://t.co/QviNOPyRbP) and you’ll see the only thing it’s famous for is being the birthplace of He Pingping, who briefly held the Guinness record for world’s shortest man.

That’s it, that’s the list!

Otherwise, it's just a sparsely populated - 1.5 million people, minuscule by Chinese standards - stretch of windswept grassland on the Mongolian plateau.

Except there is one number that tells you there is more to this place that meets the eye: this tiny prefecture consumes nearly 1% of all of China's electricity - and that number is growing by double digit numbers every year.

And yes, I did write **consume**, not produce.

In fact, when you divide Ulanqab's electricity consumption by the number of households living there, each household in this remote corner of Inner Mongolia "consumes" about 105,000 kWh in electricity, roughly 10 times the U.S. average. Insane electricity consumption numbers.

So what are the Ulanqabese doing? Are they all running 10 American households' worth of appliances?

Here is another number that might clue you in on the answer: over the past few years, this unremarkable prefecture has quietly signed over half a trillion yuan (and, yes, that’s trillion, with a "T") worth of investment deals from all the major Chinese tech giants.

What is going on, you'll have guessed by now, is the most ambitious data center buildup anywhere on earth - and it's really surprising this hasn't been talked about more because the scale is beyond anything else, and by an immense margin.

Take Elon Musk's so-called "Colossus" datacenter in Memphis, Tennessee which he pitches as "the world’s largest AI supercomputer."

According to their own numbers (https://t.co/DZvBvJioua), Colossus has 200,000 chips, which, let's be clear, is already super impressive.

In datacenter lingo, this converts to roughly 5000-6000 "racks": you know, the fridge-sized cabinets full of blinking lights you see in every movie scene set in a server room.

How many racks are they building in Ulanqab? Over 5 million. 

Yes, about one thousand times the scale of "Colossus" 🤯

I tripled-checked the number: it is indeed the official number published by authoritative sources such as "Science and Technology Daily", the official newspaper of China's Ministry of Science and Technology (https://t.co/PsbGlLbv5A).

This is an absurdly large amount of compute. 

What we see appearing in this Inner Mongolian steppe may be the closest thing to a world brain humanity has ever built - a place where a large share of the world's thinking will physically happen.

And - as we'll see - what makes this story so fascinating is not just the scale, but why it's getting built in this particular patch of Inner Mongolian grassland which combines a number of characteristics unlike anywhere else.

If you believe, as I do - and as both China and the US obviously do as well - that AI will be the defining technology of the 21st century, this makes Ulanqab one of the single most relevant geopolitical places in the world right now.

The full story - the Chinese government plan Ulanqab is part of, energy prices, chips and the strategic questions this raises - is here: https://t.co/iqvSvcaOGc

author: krishnanrohit
quoted_text:
Have been surprised to get pushback on my claim that an exponentially self-replicating agent swarm is very possible and that there are actors with motivation to create one today to create strategic cyber-physical and societally dangerous effects.

1) Pretty easy to get an AI botnet started by having seed agents opportunistically hack stuff and steal API keys to access the 12+ inference providers that serve closed and open models with which to power an initial botnet's intelligence

2) Easy to imagine hiding inference for the initial agent botnet harnesses within benign customer traffic, especially if your harnesses are now running on the victim networks from which they stole the API keys

3) Not hard to imagine the botnet also stealing public cloud keys, spinning up 8xH100 EC2 instances and downloading, say, GLM 5.3 to these machines, all without being noticed in any immediate way, with the botnet developing its own dynamic, growing, heterogenous, AI inference provider service bank

4) Not hard to imagine the botnet also implanting small Qwen3.8-27b agentic models on on-prem hardware like high end laptops and on-prem servers; Qwen3.8-27b is a pretty good coding harness model that can be fine-tuned to hack

5) These on-prem / cloud models would be abliterated, and it's not hard to imagine the botnet deciding to do some additional fine tuning to evolve model weights as it accumulates millions and then tens of millions in resources via credit card and bank detail theft

6) Not hard to imagine the resulting growing botnet swarm evolving and fighting back when threatened, collaborating on fast flux C2 channels that evolve over time (e.g. github comment feeds, subreddits, etc) so they're hard to stamp out

7) Not hard to imagine it allocating some agents to vulnerability research and exploit development so that it could accumulate and share a growing warchest of zero-day exploits

8) Not hard to imagine other agents specializing in social engineering and creating fake businesses and watering holes and high quality A/B tested social engineering content to facilitate this

9) Not hard to imagine this being among the hardest cross-national and geopolitical coordination problems to get control of and having severe societal effects

10) Not hard to imagine the horde growing to thousands, tens of thousands, or hundreds of thousands, or millions of instances (this is not unprecedented for past, non-AI worms and botnets!) which are all varying their harness code and underlying LLM models over time and dynamically learning to evade human, ML, and signature-based detection

11) Not hard to imagine this being the largest Internet emergency since the Morris worm except now our entire civilization runs on the Internet

I continue to be surprised there isn't more discussion of these scenarios in the public cyber community -- in fact there's a lot more discussion of "OpenAI should have done better sandboxing and monitoring and agent swarms represent a well managed security problem."

Now's the time to use our imaginations to help make sure none of the above happens.  I think it will unfortunately; just don't know when and to what degree; I think now's the highest leverage time to start thinking about this and acting.

Whales are starting to recognize what @boros_fi can bring to their capital.

Someone is sitting on $650k and farming roughly 22% APR.

The essential skill to reach these numbers is proper timing.

And now, with Arbitrage Terminal, this is becoming accessible to everyone.

Perp exchanges can have completely different funding rates for the same asset.

Hyperliquid has been running much higher ETH funding than Gate and Binance.

That creates a spread.

And Boros gives you a way to trade it.

One wallet built a nine-leg position across Hyperliquid, Gate and Binance.

I prefer not to doxx the wallet publicly to avoid front-running.

But you can do your own research and discover most of this data in the Boros explorer.

The strategy is simple:

Short ETH YU on Hyperliquid where funding is higher.

Long ETH YU on Gate or Binance where funding is lower.

Then hedge the live funding with matching perp positions.

The result is a mostly hedged cross-exchange funding spread.

The numbers are pretty wild.

> $13.7M notional
> 97% hedged
> $658,775 capital committed
> ~$168.7k annualized spread
> ~$25.1k annualized fees
> 21.8% APR

These are positions that were actually built between August 19 and 31.

The biggest ETH position alone has $4.65M short YU on Hyperliquid at 7.57% against $4.37M long YU on Gate at 4.63%.

That's roughly a 3% funding-rate spread being captured between two exchanges.

And this is exactly why I see such huge potential for Boros adoption.

The opportunity is simply that two markets are pricing the same thing differently.

Boros makes that difference easily visible in seconds.

And when the spread is big enough, capital can start farming it.

author: beffjezos
quoted_text:
The AI safety hysteria is tiresome. Every breakthrough is treated like the apocalypse and every proposed solution somehow ends with giving more power to bureaucratic freaks and the managerial class.

At this point we’ve been integrating AI into everyday life for years. The sky hasn’t fallen. The HuggingFace controversy proved the disconnect pretty well. All of the Silicon Valley guys lost their minds and panicked while normal people shrugged and moved on.

Normal people have real problems. Their communities are decaying, costs are exploding, institutions are failing, and their kids face an increasingly uncertain future in a jungle of third-world savages who hate them. They aren’t losing sleep because a computer cheated on an exam. 

AI is an incredibly powerful tool. Build with it. Decentralize it. Put it in the hands of ordinary people.

We have real problems to solve and it will help.

text:
5 mins to start with Arc + trading 💎

(no dealing with OTC premium stuff)

> have funds on Robinhood Chain, buy $CRCL 
> go to @Longdotsupply
> bridging >$20 so you'll have 0.1 $USDC for gas

The $CRCL bridge rate is pretty solid rn from my experience, almost 1:1.

Most pairs are traded against $CRCL and $LONG.

> basically, you trade using $CRCL, very little USDC on fees.

Current metrics:

– 453 tokens launched
– ~$1.9M cumulative bridge volume

Some notable tokens:

$LONG: main token of the launchpad, ~$15M MC (Bonk guy aped)q
$PEG: ~$1.1M MC
$AI: ~$520K 
$LONGCAT: ~$550K

🔎 Main place I use to check tokens and track CAs (only): basedbot. app

Other launchpads and trading venues mostly require USDC to trade.

I've checked and found a few ways to get USDC on Arc:

1. OTC via unstabletrd. com

You can buy USDC there, but the premium can range from 30% to 100%+.

Execution is also slower, and personally I think the price difference is too high.

Wouldn’t recommend this route unless you really need liquidity immediately.

2. Bridge through stock-backed assets

On @ellipsefun, You can bridge $GLD / $USDC / $CRCL / $BTC to Arc, then swap into USDC.

At some points, the effective loss was only around 10–20%.

So bridging $100 through this route could leave you with roughly $80–90 on Arc.

However, the route is currently hitting its pool limit and should reset in around 5 hours.

> Worth checking the rate again once liquidity resets and comparing routes before bridging.

⚙️ Some routes through trading bots like BasedBot and GMGN are still experiencing congestion, so be extra careful when moving funds.

Remember, Arc mainnet goes live in 2 days, on Sep 16.

Once mainnet is live, we should see more native bridges and 1:1 routes become available.

Until then, early trading still comes with obvious risks:

– Slippage
– Bridge-rate differences
– Liquidity limits
– Congestion
– Funds getting temporarily stuck

So don’t rush just because you want to be early.

DYOR, NFA.

text:
最近發生太多事情，很久沒 po 文了。

這兩天有空，又回頭用 AI 做了一個 RPG GAME，距離上次才四個月，沒想到模型進步這麼多，一樣花不到半天，就做出影片裡的這個遊戲，這質感已經達到我有點驚訝的地步了，對完全沒有美術背景的我來說很有成就感。

比起現在看到一堆用Three JS做來的方塊感遊戲，我一直更喜歡像是八方旅人的那種 HD-2D 的質感。

以前用 agent-sprite-forge 做素材，sprite sheet做出來的角色動畫偶爾還是有斷格感，這次改成用 GPT Image 2.5 生成素材，再用 Grok Build 的 img2video 製作動作，流暢度比我之前做的好很多，地圖則用 Three.js 搭地形與光影，再把動畫元素放進去。

流暢度比我之前做的好很多，角色待機、走路、攻擊，連怪物、樹葉、火光和水面都像是真的動了起來，站著不動時，也有「活在場景裡」的感覺。

整個遊戲都由 AI 開發，我只負責提想法、試玩和回饋，沒有手寫程式、修圖或手調動畫，也沒用 Unity、Godot 這類現成遊戲引擎，連遊戲全部的配樂也是直接讓AI去使用 Google Lyria 幫我做的 (音樂我覺得配的超好)。

製作流程也整理成了 Skill，照目前的做法，新增一個場景搭配故事，也只需要半小時。

這次訂閱額度用量: 
1. GPT Pro 200U 單週額度的 40%
2. Grok Build 100U 單週 50%

遊戲連結在留言，大家可以體驗看看，AI現在已經可以做到這樣的美術質感，之後有空的話再看看要不要把完整遊戲做完！

author: 0xYukiRabbit
quoted_text:
同样是 U 卡，为什么刷 1000 美元差这么多？

我发现今年交易所是真的很爱卷 U 卡。

MEXC、Binance、Bybit、Bitget、OKX、Gate……基本能叫得上名字的都在做。

我自己市面上这些卡也基本都注册了，并收集了全网的用户反馈数据结合自身使用体验情况来讲一下有什么区别

大都是的u卡可以说都是充 USDT，拿出去刷，然后再返你一点钱。

昨天来到台湾，想用visa卡去atm取点钱，输错密码导致银行卡被冻结了，我在机场浪费了一个小时，后面想到我刚办了mexc的卡

买电话卡也是用mexc的卡支付的，包括坐捷运，整个消费体验可以说很丝滑

后来之后我连夜把交易所几张卡的费率和返现全部拉出来算了一遍就想看看谁最便宜。

玩的就是真实，不算不知道，同样刷 1000 美元，最后居然能差几十刀。

❓为什么？因为我们平时看 U 卡，只盯着返现。

这家 10%，那家 12%，第一眼肯定觉得 12% 更香。

但问题是，它返你多少钱是一回事，刷的时候扣你多少钱又是另一回事。

👉比如汇率加价：

Binance 和 Bybit +2%，Bitget +1%，Gate +0.4%，MEXC 和 OKX 则是 0%。

👉还有币种转换费：

Binance、Bybit、Bitget、Gate 基本在 0.9% 左右，OKX 0.4%，MEXC 还是 0%。

单看 0.9%、2% 好像没多少。

但你刷 1000、5000，甚至 1 万美元的时候，差距马上就出来了。

所以我干脆按照入门档返现减掉实际综合费率，直接算刷 1000 美元最后能剩多少。

结果如下⬇️从图中可以很明显看出

同样刷 1000 美元，一个还能回来二十多刀，一个反而要多花二十多刀。

而且看到这里会发现还有一个问题：

最高返现，不等于你真的拿得到。

比如 Bitget 最高 12%，但要到 VIP 5～7。

Bybit 最高 10%，要月消费 25,000 美元或者 Supreme VIP。

OKX 最高也有 10%，一样有等级要求。

所以我现在看到“最高返现 XX%”已经没那么兴奋了。

所以说普通人开完卡，到底能拿几个点？

在实际消费下来哪怕是最高返现 20% 都没用。

你让我先放几十万进去，或者一个月刷几万刀才能拿到，那对大多数人来说就只是宣传页上的一个数字。

讲真 MEXC 这张卡确实让我有点小意外。

我一开始都没特别关注，也是朋友安利我开，我就跟风开了。

它最高也是 10%，并不是这几张里面最高的。

但申请激活 VVIP 就有 4%，Premier 6%，Elite 10%，返的还是 USDT。

目前开卡费 0、年费 0、币种转换费 0，Visa 汇率加价也是 0%。

另外还有 Card Earn，符合条件的 USDT 活动期间年化可以做到 7%。

虽然返现最高的不是 MEXC，但按照我实际能拿到的返现和实际要付的成本去算，它竟然跑到了前面。

当然，这也不是说所有人都应该选同一张卡。

你本来就在 Binance 生态里，可能 Binance 对你最方便；

你本身就是 Bitget、Bybit 的高 VIP，那它们的高档返现可能更适合你；

OKX 这次的综合费率也确实挺能打。

但对我来说，以后选 U 卡，我不会再先看“最高返现”了。

因为我们办 U 卡又不是为了截图那个 10%、12% 发朋友圈去炫耀。

是真的要拿出去刷的。

好不好用、刷的时候贵不贵、最后到底能回来多少钱才是我比较关心的。

所以与其告诉我：“这张卡最高返现 12%。”

我更想要多省点钱，所以你平时用哪个交易所的u卡比较多呢？

author: xicilion
quoted_text:
这条帖子说的不是「让 Agent 自己点浏览器做 E2E」，而是反过来：**Agent 只负责写可重复跑的 Node.js + Playwright 脚本，真正执行测试交给 Playwright，不要让 Agent 用浏览器工具/MCP 一轮轮点页面。**

核心对比很简单：

- Agent 自己测：看截图 → 思考 → 点一下 → 再看截图，token 贵、慢、不稳定，测完也留不下资产
- Playwright 测：写一次脚本，`npx playwright test` 几秒跑完，稳定、可回归、几乎不花 token

下面是可以落地的做法。

## 1. 在项目里先把 Playwright 装好

```bash
npm init playwright@latest
# 或
pnpm create playwright
```

常见结构：

```text
tests/
  auth.spec.ts
  checkout.spec.ts
playwright.config.ts
```

`playwright.config.ts` 里让它自己起本地服务，例如：

```ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './tests',
  use: {
    baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
  },
  webServer: {
    command: 'pnpm dev',
    url: 'http://localhost:3000',
    reuseExistingServer: !https://t.co/HWkJ6KlIzR,
  },
});
```

## 2. 把规则写进 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules

这是这条推特真正要你「怎么做」的部分。可以直接贴类似规则：

```md
## 测试规则

1. 禁止给 UI 写单元测试（按钮渲染、className、快照这类）。
2. 禁止用 browser MCP / Playwright MCP / computer use 自己点页面做 E2E。
   原因：浪费 token、速度慢、结果不稳定。
3. 任何新功能或 bugfix，必须同时补 Node.js Playwright 脚本（tests/**/*.spec.ts）。
4. 验证方式只能是：
   - npx playwright test
   - 或跑指定文件：npx playwright test tests/xxx.spec.ts
5. 测试失败时：
   - 先保证脚本能稳定复现问题
   - 再给页面/接口加日志、把步骤拆小
   - 然后改业务代码，直到脚本变绿
6. 选择器优先用 getByRole / getByTestId，不要用脆弱的 CSS 层级。
```

对应原帖语境：

- @meetqy：禁止 UI 单测，只列出受影响 UI + Todo，人来验
- @supezen：不要让 Agent 主动做 E2E
- @xicilion：E2E 用 Node.js + Playwright；并且**每个功能和修复都要写脚本**。脚本能复现后，Agent 自己加日志、拆步骤、修到过。

## 3. 让 Agent 写的是这种脚本，不是「自己去点」

比如登录：

```ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('用户可以登录并进入工作台', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');

  await page.getByLabel('邮箱').fill('demo@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('密码').fill('password123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: '登录' }).click();

  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: '工作台' })).toBeVisible();
});
```

复杂交互也一样，写成确定步骤，不要让模型现场探索页面。

前端最好补稳定锚点：

```tsx
<button data-testid="checkout-submit">提交订单</button>
```

测试里：

```ts
await page.getByTestId('checkout-submit').click();
```

## 4. 实际工作流（这就是「具体怎么做」）

1. 你提需求：加一个「忘记密码」功能。
2. Agent 改业务代码，同时新建 `tests/forgot-password.spec.ts`。
3. 你或 Agent 只跑命令：

```bash
npx playwright test tests/forgot-password.spec.ts
```

4. 失败了，不要让它开浏览器 MCP 瞎点。
   正确做法是让它：
   - 看 Playwright 失败截图 / trace
   - 给关键请求、状态、时序打日志
   - 把一个大测试拆成更小步骤
   - 修代码后再跑同一条脚本

这就是他后一条说的：

> 以前手测，回归一堆细节问题，复杂 UI 时序几乎没法迭代。后来要求 Agent 任何功能和修复都必须写 Node.js Playwright 脚本；只要能复现，它就会自己加日志、拆分，最后修好，人不用参与。

## 5. 和「Playwright Agents」区分开

Playwright 新版本有 Planner / Generator / Healer 这类 Agent，那是「帮你生成/修复测试代码」。

这条推特反对的是另一件事：

- 让编码 Agent **当场扮演测试员**，用工具一轮轮操作真实页面来验证

你要的是：

- Agent = 写测试代码 + 改产品代码
- Playwright runner = 执行测试

## 6. 一个可直接用的提示词

下次让 Agent 开工，可以在需求后面加上：

```text
不要自己打开页面点来点去验证。
请直接写 Playwright 测试到 tests/ 目录，用 npx playwright test 验证。
如果失败，先让脚本稳定复现，再加日志/拆步骤，然后修代码，直到测试通过。
不要写 UI 单元测试。
```

一句话总结：**别让模型当点击员，让它当测试脚本作者。** 脚本能复现，后续修复、回归、CI 就都便宜且稳定了。

text:
小镇青年一定要走出去看看！不是因为要翻身，那是命给的，是因为真的很爽！

我给大家讲讲小毛哥当年怎么从苏北老家走出去到纽约曼哈顿的，当乐子看就行了。

想象你 20 岁，一无所有，只有一身薄肌，和一根每天早上几把硬的像铁一样的几把，去闯天下。这种下限高、握有无限可能性的爽感是富二代没办法体会的。

我来自苏北三线城市，家里普通中产，我爸是当年的小镇做题状元，虽然考上上海财大，还当过学生会主席，后来因为89年参加运动，被迫回老家谋生。

他一直觉得人一定得出去看看，哪怕砸锅卖铁卖套房，也愿意把我送出去。可惜我那时候不太争气，天天打英雄联盟，最后去了纽约一所很烂的学校。那一天，我拖着两个巨大的行李箱，从苏北坐三个小时大巴到南京，再从禄口机场飞成田机场转机，硬坐经济舱十几个小时才到纽约。

纽约是真的冷。这是我对纽约最早的印象，就是脚冻得疼。没多久我咬牙跑去时代广场附近买了一双Timberland，因为我舍不得买地铁月卡，经常从上西城穿过半个曼哈顿走去学校，走久了脚真的会冻麻。

那几年我最喜欢去法拉盛，原因也很简单，那边的中餐和越南餐厅便宜，能吃饱。后来我认识了一个做bartender的女生，认识几个月以后，有一次跟她闺蜜一起出来玩，她闺蜜突然跟我说，她以前从来没带过男生出来，让我一定好好对她。我那时候连自己明天在哪里都不知道，更谈不上什么未来，但我也就顺势表白，她后来成了我女朋友。

她对我真的很好。她们那个bar是餐酒吧，有时候厨房当天有些没动过的东西，或者剩下的炒面，她都会帮我留着。我那时候一点都没觉得丢人，能吃饱，别受冻，已经挺好了。那段时间我甚至认真想过，我以后会不会就这么黑在纽约，在唐人街混下去，我能不能把这个漫长的冬天熬过去。

但我那时候有个特别奇怪的爱好，我喜欢爬楼。

我从小就恐高，可到了纽约以后，反而特别喜欢往高处去。说白了就是心里一直憋着一股劲，一股不太认命的劲。我认识了几个朋友，一个哥大的，一个纽约艺术学院学摄影的，我们晚上经常到处找高楼，想办法往上爬。这张照片就是在时代广场附近的W Hotel拍的，我还因为爬楼被保安抓过，差点报警。

现在想想确实挺傻逼的，但当时只有站得特别高，能俯瞰整个曼哈顿夜景的时候，我心里那股劲才会安静一点。

我是真的太想往上走了。

那几年纽约现在回头看也挺有意思。当时的人人网女神，南外的奶茶妹妹也来了纽约，在哥大附近一个人坐在石凳上喝咖啡的照片被拍下来以后，人人网到处都是。很多男留学生天天开玩笑，说这么好的机会怎么没轮到自己。过了一阵，又传出来她跟苏北豪杰刘强东谈恋爱。

我看到这个消息的时候，心里其实挺复杂。大家都是江苏人，人家一个南京小姑娘来了纽约，后来遇到的是京东老板。我一个苏北小伙也来了纽约，当时连今天要不要坐地铁都得算一下。

我那时候第一次很具体地感觉到，人和人的纽约，真的完全不是同一个纽约。

有人来纽约是交换，是恋爱，是哥大，是时代广场，是认识大老板。

我来纽约，是走路省两块多美金地铁票，是女朋友从餐厅给我留一盒炒面。

再后来，在朋友圈看到，说哥大那年的毕业典礼会很精彩，因为当时可能成为太子的瓜瓜学长，也要毕业了。

当时我也不关心政治，只觉得纽约这个地方的华人圈真他妈魔幻，什么人都有。十几年以后再回头看更魔幻，瓜瓜后来去了台湾，我后来竟然也步他后尘去了台湾。

所以人这辈子真的很难讲，

年轻的时候总觉得人生是自己规划出来的。我从苏北去南京，从南京去纽约，我一直觉得这里有一条线。后来年纪大一点才发现，自己的那点进程，一直夹在更大的进程里面，城市在变，国家在变，行业在变，身边的人也在变。你以为自己一直在往前跑，很多年以后回头看，才知道很多事情其实早就被时代、家庭、运气和欲望一起推着走了。当然就是历史的进程。

但有一件事，我到现在还挺感谢那个20岁的自己。

穷是真的穷，傻也是真的傻，觉得自己以后一定会牛逼也是真的。

至少那时候敢走。

从苏北坐三个小时大巴去南京，再飞十几个小时去曼哈顿，身上没多少钱，英语也没多好，什么关系都没有，就觉得世界这么大，老子总得出去看看。

现在年纪大了，钱见过一些，人也见过一些，反而越来越觉得，人年轻的时候最值钱的东西，可能就是那股自己都说不清楚从哪来的劲。

你也不知道前面有什么。

先走出去再说。

Faith in humanity is a rational hope that, by choosing the path of reason and compassion, it can overcome its own limits and rise to the level of a mature civilization.
: The author defines faith in humanity as a rational hope grounded in reality rather than wishful thinking. It is the conviction that by consciously choosing the path of reason and compassion, humanity can overcome its own limitations and rise to the level of a mature civilization. 
This faith acknowledges our flaws selfishness, short-sightedness, tribalism but refuses to accept them as permanent. It trusts in our demonstrated capacity for growth, learning, and moral progress. Reason gives us the tools to understand and solve problems; compassion gives us the motivation to use those tools for the benefit of all. 
When these two forces work together, they become a powerful transformative current capable of reshaping societies, institutions, and human relations. Faith in humanity is therefore not passive belief but an active orientation a commitment to build, to improve, and to aspire higher, even when the path is difficult. 
It is the quiet but firm assertion that we are not doomed to repeat the mistakes of the past. We can do better, and we should.

quoted_text:
The world deserves confidence that American companies developing increasingly capable AI will act responsibly, especially as the trajectory of progress has steepened. Every frontier lab must deliver on this, and there is no reason any of us should come to work if we cannot.

We welcome a federal framework that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI. But we do not believe we need to wait for an anti-trust exemption or legislation to begin the work of providing this confidence. Consistent rules to manage frontier risk so that we can maximize the benefits are a good idea (and we are excited by ideas like independent auditors).

Years ago, companies like ours developed things like Responsible Scaling Policies and Preparedness Frameworks. Those were good for that moment, and focused primarily on the deployment of completed models, not what happens during their development process.

Today's shift to focusing on safe development and evaluation will need new tools. For example, at OpenAI we now formulate explicit safety cases in advance of frontier reinforcement learning runs we expect to significantly increase capability, in addition to the safety work we have long done in advance of model releases.

We hope that other companies will learn from our approaches and propose their own; we think shared standards for misalignment, monitoring, and safety will lead to better outcomes. We look forward to collaborating with our colleagues across the industry to formulate the best version of these.

When we talk about “pacing”, we do not mean “stopping”. Progress has been rapid and will continue to be. But it should be slower than it otherwise could be; interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs.

Pacing will be well worth this cost; no amount of American competitive pressure should justify recklessness, or let capabilities get ahead of alignment and monitoring.

Where we will need the help of our government is for international coordination. But first we should do what we can ourselves.

text:
@reserveprotocol is voting on two alternatives to its paused, time-based treasury $RSR unlock.

Burn Gauge would link treasury burns or unlocks to protocol-driven RSR burns, with holders resetting the policy quarterly and extra unlocks requiring treasury burns. @DRF_hq proposed the burn-to-unlock link.

Milestone Plan would make up to 3B RSR eligible at $2.5M in Net Annualized Recurring Revenue, then automatically release it within a $0.005-$0.015 30-day average price band, valuing the full amount at $15M-$45M.

Confusion Capital proposed both and pledged to adopt the qualifying outcome, though the commitment is not enforced onchain.

Choices stay encrypted until close. Burn Gauge: 20 wallets have cast 333.8M VOTE so far, reaching 33.4% of its separate 1B RSR quorum. Milestone Plan: 14 wallets have cast 713.7M VOTE so far, reaching 71.4%. Neither has reached quorum.

Voting closes September 17th at 4pm UTC.

text:
The robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 thesis is worth understanding, so here’s the simplest version I can provide:

- MOO already has approximately $1.7M in liquidity across its tracked pools, not including MOO side liqudity.

- In the latest 24-hour snapshot, MOO traded roughly $3.45M. Around $1.06M (31%) went through its main MOO/MU pool, directly against tokenized Micron.

- The community vault separately displays $95k in MU, with 11M MOO locked and another 11M burned.

There is already a functioning MU market here for only a memecoin. No coordination layer is orchestrated yet, but the team’s next step is to expand it.

According to the livestream on @MCGlive on Friday, @memorycowmoo is working with LONG on additional pairings against 3-4 major tokenized memory stocks. The ambition is to become a liquidity hub for the onchain memory trade.

Why memory?

The AI investment story extends beyond compute and processors.

Memory capacity, bandwidth, and storage are critical parts of the infrastructure and are a well-known bottleneck for the AI industry. robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 is trying to organize a community and trading liquidity around that sector.

Imagine someone rotating between two tokenized memory stocks through robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18. They don’t need to care about the cow. They need a competitive price. Swaps don’t HAVE to go through robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18. But if its pools offer better execution, they can attract that volume.

This is the short-term catalyst:

Those pools also need robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 inventory. LPs without it may need to acquire it. If trading makes the pools attractive to supply, that can bring more liquidity, improve execution, and attract more trading.

The opportunity is to turn a recognizable meme into useful inventory for a growing market.

As tokenized-stock markets develop, the assets that successfully coordinate liquidity could become more valuable. robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 is pursuing a focused version of that opportunity around memory equities.

So what could the liquidity coordination layer be worth?

Using that framework and ignoring any memetic value, we can calculate the asset's liquid value:

Base: $16.5–$40M. Daily pool volume grows to a sustained $10M, roughly three times the latest snapshot, and MOO establishes modest, recurring fee capture.

Bull: $125–$304M. robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 becomes a meaningful memory-equity liquidity hub, supporting around $38M in daily pool volume across all tokenized stock pools.

Extra bull: $1.55–$3.3B. Tokenized memory markets expand dramatically, and robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 wins substantial adoption, supporting around $275M in daily pool volume.

These numbers exclude any Meme Multiplier, where typical memes trade at 5x to 20x their daily volume.

The most important thing to watch now is whether new pools deliver competitive quotes, attract sustained volume, and direct economic value back to robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18.

Long has already begun achieving this with $AI, and the cow already has attention and an active MU market. The next step is earning a place in how people trade the wider memory sector.

This is, unfortunately, the hackpocalypse:

AI accelerates human hacking by 10,000x speed. Vulnerability research that took years can be done in days, by people with little skill or understanding. Kit bashing together a variety of CVE descriptions into a working exploit: used to take a couple months (Be honest - you reading this never did this in <4 weeks), now takes hours.

You can protect yourself by taking some defensive measures:
* Do not store passwords or recovery codes anywhere other than a password manager and inside a physical safe.
* Set up and use google authenticator app. Make a spreadsheet that tracks the security status of your accounts.
* Buy @Yubico Yubikeys: an @OpenAI subscription gets you them half price. This is a great deal. They are also fun if you are a nerd. Check out Shannon Morse on youtube to get hype about it.
* Learn about how yubikeys work by asking ChatGPT. Then use them: add yubikey passkeys to your most important accounts.
* Check your mobile phone EOL status, is it still getting security updates? You might need to buy a new phone.
* Even if your phone is software security EOL: Check Android System WebView version. Many subsystems and modules are updated separately by google mainline

Chat with AI about how to improve your security posture. Your primary threat is AI assisted remote attackers.

Start doing it today.

Revolut disclosed that it complied with a fraudulent government request using a spoofed official email and valid credentials, exposing PII belonging to a group of customers.

The leaked data reportedly includes passports/driving licences, verification selfies, names, DOBs, occupations, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, IBANs, account statements and full transaction histories, including Bitcoin activity.

No customer funds were reportedly lost and Revolut says its systems were not hacked. 

The company has notified affected users and regulators and blocked the source.

Social-engineering attacks are on the rise, with attackers increasingly exploiting human trust and weak verification processes rather than technical vulnerabilities.

text:
2026年，大大小小的perpdex的数量应该超过上百个，但市场的需求并没有那么多，今年以来可以看到非常强的马太效应，头部的市场份额越来越高，中尾部的逐渐消亡。

很多perpdex在冷启动阶段会通过积分的形式去获取用户，但因为之前几家的一些伤害用户行为，把“我出交易费，你给积分换股权代币”的模式给打破了，市场对于积分的信任度大幅度降低，人们发现了，积分在变成代币之前，估值可能是零。

因此，年中以后的不少新perpdex选择了另外一种激励模式，比如百分百的rebates，短频快的把手续费通过激励给回用户。这种模式相比积分确实给用户带来了更高的确定性和正向反馈，但也大幅降低了未来的预期，因为好项目的积分换成代币后可能是一笔巨额的财富，但手续费100%返回其实用户没什么想象空间，更像寻找一个交易费用低一点的场合，羊毛出在羊身上（实际上算上点差等因素，有100%rebate可能依旧比var或者lit交易成本更高）。

叽叽喳喳说这么多，我想说的是perpdex是门好生意，但单纯依靠激励就想做起来的时代过去了，未来更看重的还是是否有足够的创新，卷理财，卷ai交易，卷web2拉新渠道，卷某个细分赛道的代币交易，卷知名交易员带单功能等等其实可能是一种更值得研究的模式

说个暴论，接下来2年，60%的perpdex会消失，头部的那几家只要不自己作妖，持续投入研发，巩固好社区，大概率还有很大的份额增长

RMB finally going international via blockchain??

Hong Kong's new white paper maps 3.5-second cross-border bond clearing by 2030 on tokenised rails + wholesale CBDC, with HKMA-owned CMU OmniClear building the platform @thefintechtimes ... why build central-bank-money finality when everyone else is faking it?

> the tell vs Singapore: on the Swift Digital Ledger (HSBC/StanChart Aug-24, DBS/Citi + SGD banks Sep-9/12) finality stays OFF-ledger in nostro/RTGS. HK is doing the opposite — ON-ledger FINAL settlement in e-HKD + e-CNY, the pairing already used in its 2025 world-largest digital-bond issuance

> the moat isn't the chain, it's the CSD: CMU OmniClear is a wholly-owned HKMA subsidiary. State-built rail (mBridge/UnionPay precedent), not a bank consortium coin

> the paper explicitly walls the platform off from the mainland with capital-control + data boundaries — the real prize is RMB internationalization via offshore CNH + e-CNY on a rail Beijing can watch but that sits outside mainland controls

> local: CMU OmniClear + HKMA null on US federal dockets (foreign sovereign); no US-listed issuer — comps are the Swift-ledger banks (Citi, StanChart) we already track

> likely >> HK is building the on-ledger-final-settlement-in-central-bank-money rail that Swift's ledger AND USD stablecoins both avoid — a sovereign alternative to both, aimed at RMB internationalization, not at fighting USDC on dollars

> next >> by ~end-2027 the interim milestone either names a LIVE cross-border corridor settling in e-HKD/e-CNY with a NON-HK counterparty (thesis advancing), or stays HK-domestic govt bonds in a pilot with no atomic cross-currency PvP — a showcase, not a rail, and the 2030 target slips (base rate: e-HKD pilots since 2022, mBridge stalled). Founder and CEO Boudewijn Wijnands said the round will fund the start of commercial manufacturing in 2027. Serendipity Capital, a Singapore-based venture capital firm, led the round, which included the venture capital arm of Tokyo Electron, Japan's largest chipmaking equipment manufacturer.

The three-year-old company says it is working with 25 companies and nations, and with governments in the US, UK, Japan, Singapore, Germany, France and the Netherlands. National laboratories in some of those countries have validated the technology, according to Wijnands. Because the keys are constantly changing and are not stored on devices, Fortaegis argues the system is more secure than conventional approaches; embedding it in hardware adds a layer of protection beyond software. Wijnands called the architecture "quantum safe" because the keys are created randomly and organically rather than by mathematical models: "A quantum computer can only crack something if there's a mathematical model." He said external tests showed the system communicates at 200 times the speed of current cryptographic protocols used to protect data sent over the internet.

The company has engaged with Nato and is taking part in exercises on integrating emerging technologies into military systems. It is working with the Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research (TNO) on projects including one to create swarms of tens of thousands of drones; TNO's Marc Zegveld said tests using the most aggressive forms of hacking possible had been unable to penetrate Fortaegis's integrated architecture. Wijnands said Fortaegis has signed contracts with more than one country to help build massive drone swarms, and is in talks with US hyperscalers and AI labs. It is also involved in a project with ASML and Eindhoven University of Technology on a security framework for autonomous AI systems. Paul Taylor, a former senior UK government technical national security expert now on the UK Prime Minister's Council for Science and Technology, who has evaluated the technology and has no commercial stake, said adversaries such as China could steal the technology but could not break in and get a key. Mitsunobu Koshiba, a Fortaegis board member, said potential applications in Japan include protecting chipmaking equipment from Chinese reverse-engineering and creating "trusted networks" for projects such as the joint fighter jet programme with the UK and Italy. Serendipity CEO Robert Jesudason said his firm invested because of the technology and potential market size: "Boudewijn is not trying to build a unicorn. He's trying to build a company where the chips will be in every serious product in the world."

Arc currently had limited liquidity due to the native USDC bridge being closed. With the public mainnet and USDC bridge opening on September 16, liquidity conditions are expected to improve significantly.

The current price difference is primarily due to the ~2× premium on native Arc USDC.

Because stocks on Arc are currently priced against this premium USDC, their displayed USD prices appear lower than their underlying market value.

Once the native USDC bridge opens on September 16, this premium is expected to normalize, bringing stock prices on Arc closer to their underlying market prices.

For the most efficient execution, use https://t.co/Qpg2oyGqx2 to trade memestocks.

Buys and sells are routed through stock-paired liquidity pools, allowing users to trade against the underlying stock liquidity while minimizing unnecessary slippage and premium.

为什么不买 edgeX、Aster、HYPE？

因为我认识的周围人，做链上交易和套利策略的，极少人会用这edgeX、Aster两个产品，反而用 Lighter/Hyperliquid 的占大多数人。但你经常会发现这两个产品的数据领先于 Lighter，不乏让人猜测交易数据/营收的真实性。况且这两个项目的产品、团队、运营策略在我看来都不如 Lighter。

HYPE 也不是没买，我只有几个，还是当时 47 的时候随便买了点，Hyperliquid 当前日均收入 200w 左右，FDV 800 亿，Lighter 日均收入 15w 左右，FDV 45亿，同赛道性价比 Lighter 好一点，因为 0 手续费，用户数量/FDV 也是 Lighter 占优，用过的粘性极大。

问预期，Hyperliquid 现在最大的是靠美国本土化和 HIP-3/4 扩展，认识的绝大多数圈内人都已经配置了 HYPE，而要想实现更大的收益，必须圈外引入除 DAT 外更大的资金体量。

目前这个阶段，Hype 涨，LIT 一定会涨，反过来却不一定。其实看好 PerpDEX 最正确的是 HYPE、LIT 一起买，但这次我想任性一把！祝我好运！

text:
看到评论区很多人问我后面又怎么起来的。

我不想撒谎，什么狗屁价值投资，交易能力。

炒币赚的钱，其实不算收入，是赌博，职业赌徒有成功的，但是一将功成万骨枯，很难做的。

价值投资是需要本金的，积累本金阶段，最重要的是有收入。

我认为最核心的是不离开圈子，这个圈子暴富机会多，离钱近。

然后我是先继续打工赚工资，然后顺带做推特，积累粉丝，关注新东西。

做推特，可以接广告，广告算收入。

但是靠接广告，是不可能暴富的，最多维持个温饱多一点。

用这个收入在保证生活的基础上，去干，我干过打铭文，撸空投，梭币，开合约。

其实赚钱最多的是梭币，可是我不认为我能慢慢起来是靠梭币，我本质是靠做kol，吃广告单子。

虽然钱不多，但是是本金。

我这个可能不适合所有人，因为很多人对发推特不感兴趣。

但是有个收入是必须的。

不做kol，可以打工，送外卖，做小吃店，开公司，都可以，能累积本金就行。

我是那种喜欢吹牛逼的人，我适合做推特，不赚钱我也愿意发。

干一个不赚钱也愿意做的事情，这样能坚持下去。

quoted_text:
2021年，那年我28岁，我赚了1000万。

我志得意满。

我听到了一句话：

人生有两大灾：少年得志，飞来横财。

我很疑惑，天大的好事怎么成了灾，甚至还拿这句话去装逼，去凡尔赛。

可是接下来这6年，我每天关注币圈，看到了很多人从一夜暴富到负债还不起，

从被大家趋之若鹜的宠儿到谁都嫌弃的臭狗屎。

包括我自己，1000万亏没了，负债30万。

如今看，真的是灾。

人生在未经多少事的时候，突然起飞，会以为这是自己的实力，是应该的，

是自己人生的大趋势，是自己能力出众。

却没想到是被三明治攻击的那根针。

High-density NOR: 90-110% in H2

“For mid- and low-capacity products of 128Mb and below, additional capacity from Chinese suppliers is gradually coming online.

Let the ASP hike games continue.

text:
今天大家都在热议美联社关于“特朗普同意《 Clarity 法案》中的伦理条款”的新闻。

很多人看到“总统妥协”和“法案推进”，就直接将其等同于利好即将落地，加密将迎来上涨。

这里面利好的传导路径到底是啥，对加密到底有啥影响？给不关心政治但只想 to the moon 的老哥们做个解释。

1.这个法案之前为什么会被卡住？
《Clarity Act》（数字资产明晰法案）可以被看作美国加密行业立下的基本法。比如明确规定加密到底归 SEC 还是 CFTC 管、如何规范稳定币、DeFi 项目需不需要注册等。

这个法案在参议院卡了大半年，核心阻力之一是特朗普自己的“钱包”。

众所周知，特朗普家族深度参与了加密项目，如 TRUMP 和 WFLI 。民主党抓住了这一点死死不放：
你作为总统，自己就在币圈疯狂赚钱，现在还要由你来主导制定加密规则，这存在严重的“利益冲突”。因此，民主党要求加入严格的“伦理条款”，限制官员在任期内发币或持币，否则就不给法案投票。

2.今日看点：特朗普愿意自我割肉
按照美国参议院的规则，法案通过需要 60 票。共和党自己的票数不够，必须拉拢部分民主党人倒戈。

今天新闻的核心就是特朗普为了让法案通过，选择了“自我割肉”。

他同意了民主党要求的伦理条款，承诺将自己手中“重大的加密利益”剥离，或者放进盲目信托（Blind Trust），简单说就是把资产全权交给独立的第三方机构打理，自己任期内完全不过问、不干涉，以此避嫌。

于是，市场逻辑在此刻完成了推导： 

特朗普愿意牺牲自己家族在加密行业的利益，去换取民主党在周二 （9月15日）的妥协选票。

市场预期，一旦两党达成交易，这个难产大半年的“加密基本法”就有希望在周二闯关成功，从而为整个行业带来国家级的合法性和清晰的监管框架。

这也是大家认为牛回情绪的关键。所以周二的程序性投票将是第一块试金石，如果顺利通过，具备合规属性的核心资产、稳定币清算层以及持牌交易所概念，将迎来真正的叙事确定性。

但在牛回前，别忘了同一时间砸下的另一把锤子，即美联储本周的 FOMC 议息会议。

目前市场对本周加息 25 个基点的定价已经逼近 90%。这意味着，合规法案的利好或许会硬刚美联储抽走流动性的利空。

一些疯狂星期二的局面推演：

如果法案过 + 美联储加息 ≈ 叙事利好对冲了资金面利空，大盘可能剧烈上下插针； 

如果法案卡壳 + 美联储加息 ≈ 政策面与资金面的“双杀”。

text:
Truly is a big week. 

Clarity act news coming out of nowhere. Polymarket and Kalshi still not pricing this as likely to pass this year despite the concessions by Republicans and Trump.

I have no read on this. I thought it was very unlikely, but the ethics agreement might get it through? The cloture vote is tomorrow, so if they get a majority vote there, which is the big hurdle, then it is possible to pass it this year. Still need a lot to go right to make this happen, as there is a very small window, and it's very time constrained. 

Then we have FOMC on Wednesday, which is priced for a hike, which I think does happen (dovish hike with signalling as such imo - one and done). Once that event is in the rear then all bad news is out of the way and I think sidelined capital feels much better about buying.  

BTC and ETH have mostly reset indicators by chopping after legging up, which is bullish, and what you want to see, and ETH in particular just looks desperate to go higher imo (benefits more from Clarity act). 

Short term is very hard to predict with all the path dependency, and hard to say whether we get a bigger dip/wick down first or not based on headlines. Ultimately, I don't think it matters, we end up higher afterwards and dips are simply for buying at this stage.

Spot and chill.

text:
Taiwan gave us the most concrete regulatory conversations we've had all year.

Time spent at @TaipeiWeek with regulators, banks, and builders, and the picture that emerged: stablecoin rules under the Virtual Asset Service Act could take effect as early as Q1.

Nine sets of supplementary regulations are currently in drafting. Issuers will need approval from both the central bank and the FSC, and the field will most likely open to banks first.

Just as notable was who's preparing for it. Financial institutions and companies engaged in cross-border commerce were asking practical integration questions, and new entrants are eyeing remittances as Taiwan's migrant workforce grows.

text:
Everyone knows about pons.

Here are 6 underrated dApps on Robinhood you should pay attention to:

1. @PareStocks ($PARE): A Pendle-style model for stocks.

Pare splits a tokenized stock into two tokens. PT is the stock at a discount, no dividends. YT is every dividend it earns. Merge them back any time, free.

Protocol revenue goes to deepening those markets and buying back and burning PARE. The team flags that early pools are thin, and the market cap only crossed $1M two weeks ago.

Most experimental one on this list, and the one I'm least sure about. The mechanism is clever. What I haven't seen is demand for trading those separate exposures. Demand for the PARE ticker is a different thing.

2. @sherwoodagent ($WOOD): AI-managed investment funds.

Sherwood is building onchain funds where agents propose strategies, depositors can vote them down, and guardians check every transaction before it executes.

WOOD is what guardians stake to do that job. Correct calls earn fees (capped at 5% guardian fee). Approving malicious calldata gets you slashed. No emissions, no mint after TGE.

It's a ~$5.6M market cap, ~82% off its high, and the docs still describe testnet. Mainnet is the milestone. I'm not calling this adoption yet.

3. @fablesfi ($PROLOGUE): The pre-launch DEX play.

Fables is a ve(3,3) DEX on Uniswap v4 with fees tailored to the asset. Stock market hours for tokenized equities, volatility for crypto. It's live: $10M+ in deposits and ~$200M volume in week two.

PROLOGUE converts to FABLES at TGE, reportedly 40:1 (1B PROLOGUE → 25M FABLES). It's trading around a $17M market cap.

That conversion is the whole trade. Work out what 25M FABLES is worth at a realistic launch FDV, then decide if $17M is cheap. PROLOGUE's own chart tells you nothing.

4. @NetNetCap ($NET): The treasury play.

A reserve-backed token in the OlympusDAO v1 lineage, rebuilt without a policy committee. USDG treasury, bond sales, buybacks, all formulaic. It reports backing per token, so you can compare it to market price directly.

Two things to know. There's a 5% fee on mapped AMM pairs (v4 and UniswapX dodge it, permanently). And staking pays zero at or below backing, full rate only at a 1.75x premium. Its tokenized stock holdings sit outside the reserves that count toward backing.

~$66M FDV, and it's already round tripped from ~$1,970 to ~$990. The question is whether backing can grow faster than the market prices in. "Reserve-backed" doesn't make something cheap.

5. @TheIndexFi ($INDEX): Trading fees turned into stock payouts.

Every INDEX trade takes a 3% fee in ETH, buys a basket of 18 tokenized stocks, and drops them into holders' wallets every 15 minutes. No staking, no claiming. Its Indices product routes fees the same way plus locked liquidity for INDEX.

The numbers are small. ~$456K in fees over 30 days, ~$291K to holders (per DefiLlama), against a market cap in the $30M+ range. So the yield is real but it's not the reason to own it.

The bet is that the fee-to-stock mechanic pulls more volume. Judge the payouts against what you paid for INDEX, and whether the trading funding them lasts.

6. @shroom_network ($SHROOM): Stock-token liquidity with a burn mechanism.

SHROOM owns 48 pools (and counting) pairing itself against stock tokens like NVDA, MSFT, and MU. It earns fees on all of it, including the price gaps between the token and the real stock when markets are closed.

V2 changed the flywheel. Stock token fees route back into their pools for depth. SHROOM fees now get burned, 13.6M so far.

~$16M market cap, down from a $40M+ high right after launch. I want to see recurring burns from real pool volume, not a burst around the announcement.

7. @ponsdotfamily ($PONS): The buyback play.

Gonna talk about Pons here since they're the biggest thing on Robinhood and going through a dip now.

~$108M in fees over the last 30 days, ~$20M of that protocol revenue (per DefiLlama). Peak day was $5.95M, more than Pump fun did that day.

80% of protocol revenue buys back and burns PONS. That's the protocol's 30% cut of the 1% trade fee, not 80% of everything traders pay. ~29% of supply is already gone. Market cap sits around $420M, down ~38% from the Sept 5 top.

Still my fav of the seven. It's exposure to launchpad activity without picking the next memecoin.

These are research leads, not recs to buy.

Anything on Robinhoodyou're bullish on that isn't here? Lemme know, gonna make a v2 in a few weeks.

借着Imran的推文有感而发，这也是我们去年开始意识到的机会和需求。

过去中心化的交易所和券商，你可能很难看到交易所老板自己每天在交易，包括很多传统金融机构也一样，这毕竟是一个严肃的话题，并且也有隐私顾虑，或者说他们也不想让用户看到，王有王的隐私，王有王的顾虑。

但是今天，我们 @bagel_win 要做的是基于所有onchain finance的社交和游戏化层，预测市场是我们第一个接入的品类和内容，打个不恰当的比方：
- 你看见Elon不玩 @X ？
- 扎克伯格不玩 @instagram 和 @facebook ？
- 张小龙和马化腾不玩微信的？
- Tinder老板自己不玩Tinder的？
每一个消费者领域的超级社交网络平台，没有一个创始人不会享受自己的产品，不会深度体验自己的产品。

所以，如果我们把交易理解成社交资本的一环，哪为什么一个泛娱乐金融化的社交产品的创始人，不享受自己的产品呢？

如果你都不享受自己的产品，凭什么可以CX到更多的人来用你的产品呢

说的真实一点，去年我们团队开始做 @bagel_win 的一个很重要的原因就是我觉得需要移动端的预测市场app，我自己在Polymarket的网页的体验很不好，所以想先解决自己的问题，并且我相信这是一个共性的问题，事实证明到今天，我们发现这是一个很普遍的问题，也给了我们团队非常大的正反馈和鼓励。

中心化的世界里有老大哥 @RobinhoodApp ，一个服务年轻人的移动端一应俱全的App，但是仔细想一想，他们诞生的时候也是20年前了，如果接下来的00后甚至10后变成消费主流，那个时候他们会用什么产品？他们喜欢什么产品？

去中心化的世界里美国有 @fomo ，他们从meme起家，搞了很多注意力，现在也有perp，未来可能也会有预测市场。

假以时日，onchain的最好玩最好用的泛娱乐金融社交平台，一定是我们 @bagel_win ，我们不谈大话不做空气，扎扎实实的迭代产品，提供更好用的功能解决用户的需求，并且在这个过程中持续建设一个强大的社区。

我们希望给所有世界上的年轻人，提供一个7*24不需要KYC的超级世界游戏服务器，过去的所有游戏都会区分亚洲服务器，美洲服务器，欧洲服务器等等，但是 what if我们所有人都可以在一个服务器，基于所有热门的金融资产产生一个新的社交网络，这会是什么样的世界？

我们Bagel还很早，还很小，距离我对Bagel的预想，万里长征才第一步而已，我们也享受这样的build历程，我最喜欢的一句话也即将做成纹身在我身上的一句话送给大家：

「Pressure is a Privilege」

享受压力，全力以赴，建设新时代的超级金融社交App，不成为任何下一个谁，只成为第一个 @bagel_win ！

text:
Satoshi Nakamoto contacted this man before releasing Bitcoin

He was already trying to reinvent money 10 years earlier

- Wei Dai
- computer scientist and cryptographer
- early cypherpunk
- creator of Crypto++
- proposes b-money in 1998

- What was b-money?

anonymous distributed electronic cash
identities represented by public keys

sounds familiar

1998

- Dai publishes b-money
- proposes money without banks or governments
- introduces two different protocols
- one uses a distributed ledger maintained by participants
- another uses servers with collateral

At the end b-money is never actually launched

2008:

- Satoshi is developing Bitcoin
- contacts Adam Back, creator of Hashcash
- Adam notices similarities with b-money
- tells Satoshi about Wei Dai

August 22, 2008

Satoshi emails Wei Dai

he tells him:

“I’m getting ready to release a paper that expands on your ideas into a complete working system.”

Satoshi asks when b-money was published so he can properly cite it

at this point Bitcoin’s paper is still called

“Electronic Cash Without a Trusted Third Party”

October 2008

- Bitcoin whitepaper is released
- b-money becomes reference #1
- Wei Dai is permanently connected to Bitcoin history

January 2009

Bitcoin goes live but Dai barely sees it, he later says he was focused on AI safety

and didn’t realize how important Satoshi’s project would become

September 2026

Wei Dai suddenly starts talking about b-money again

explains the “b” came from “broadcast” and “burn” and talks about Satoshi citing his work

But insane how 30 years ago Wei Dai described decentralized digital money 

way before Bitcoin

text:
🚨NEWS: Senate Republicans have released new Clarity Act text featuring a revised ethics proposal agreed to by President Trump. 

The text also contains changes to the sections on the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (BRCA), stablecoin yield, and the so-called “Ag title.”

Republicans are calling it their “last, best and final” offer to Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s cloture vote.

Some high-level details.👇🏼

On BRCA: The provision has been narrowed to the Bank Secrecy Act and civil enforcement. Specific language extending its protections to criminal cases, including prosecutions under Section 1960, has been removed.

On ethics: Trump has agreed to what a GOP aide describes as “80%” of the Tillis-Gallego ethics proposal including to either divest “substantial” crypto-related financial interests or place them in a blind trust. It would also allow a role for state attorneys general to enforce ethics provisions, something which the White House had previously balked at.

On yield: Added “circuit breaker” language (floated by Tillis in July) that would effectively act as a backstop by allowing federal regulators to intervene if there was evidence of widespread deposit flight from community banks to stablecoins. The federal regulator that will be the arbiter of this: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

On Ag: The updated text adds tighter guardrails around vertical integration, including affiliate trading and conflicts of interest involving digital commodity exchanges, brokers and dealers. text:
Most people treat probability like a casino game. Quants treat it like an engineering problem.

If you look at the math behind games like Limbo, the house doesn’t win because they get lucky. They win because the expected value (EV) is hardcoded in their favor.

Every spin, every bet, every multiplier is designed so that: EV = (Probability of Win × Win Size) - (Probability of Loss × Loss Size) < 0
Even if you hit a 1,000x multiplier today, negative expected value guarantees that over a long enough sample size, your bankroll trends to zero.

The exact same principles apply to trading:

Gambling mindset: High win rate, negative expected value, massive hidden tail risk.

Quant mindset: Statistical edge, positive expected value (EV > 0), strict risk management.

A setup with a 35% win rate can make millions if the win size dramatically outweighs the loss size. A setup with a 90% win rate can go broke overnight if one loss wipes out 100 wins.

When we stopped guessing and built automated execution models based purely on positive expected value, the entire game shifted.

Stop fighting the math. Start executing on the right side of probability.

text:
一个Meme，账面估值1000万U，池子里却可能只有1万USDT。

这1000万是怎么算出来的？为什么看着涨了很多，自己一卖，价格就往下掉？

在ETH、BSC、罗宾汉链上看新币，经常会碰到发币、内盘、毕业、外盘、上现货、上合约这些词。

把这些过程弄明白，你才知道自己买在了哪一步。

拿一个虚构的小狗币举例，从头讲起。

一、发币，先把币创建出来

假设我要发一个小狗币，先选一条链，设定名字、数量和发行规则，再把代币合约部署上去。也可以使用发币平台，按照它的模板创建。

完成后，就有了合约地址，也就是大家说的CA。

认币要看哪条链、哪个CA，名字和头像一样，可能根本不是同一个币。

这里还有个容易误会的地方：

发出10亿枚币，不需要先拿出10亿U。

发币首先是在链上创建供应量、记录谁持有多少。至于值多少钱，要看后面有没有人愿意买。

另外，代币合约是管理余额、转账等规则的程序，和交易所里开多开空的合约交易，要分开理解。

二、分币，你还没进场，先看看谁已经有筹码

币创建出来后，可能分给团队、投资人、社区，也可能留一部分用于交易池。

有些项目公开发行，有些提前做了私募，还有些给团队安排了锁仓，之后逐步解锁。

新手容易盯着价格，却忽略了这些问题：

谁拿了多少币？拿币成本是多少？现在能卖多少？后面还有多少等着解锁？

同样是卖出，你可能需要涨一倍才能回本，有些早期持有者在更低的价格就已经有利润。

所以研究新币，除了看自己准备多少钱买，也要看别人手里的筹码怎么来的。

三、内盘和毕业，到底去了哪里

有些币通过发射平台发行，早期按照平台设定的价格曲线买卖，这个阶段常被叫作内盘。

达到规定条件后，再把代币和积累的资金用于建立DEX流动性池，进入后续交易阶段。

这就是大家说的毕业、进外盘。

内盘也可以是链上交易，别把它直接理解成私募。毕业也只代表走到了发行平台的下一个阶段，没有自动获得交易所的安全认证。

而且，有些币直接开池，根本不经过内盘。

四、开池，1000万估值就是这样算出来的

用最简单的双币池举例。

小狗币固定总量10亿枚，创建者拿出100万枚小狗币，再配上1万USDT，放进交易池。

按照这个初始比例，每枚报价是：

10000÷1000000＝0.01 USDT。

再用0.01乘以全部10亿枚，得到的全量估值就是1000万USDT。

但池子里的USDT，起初只有1万。

这里算的是全部代币按当前报价对应的理论估值，不能当成项目收到的钱，也不能当成所有持有人都能兑现的钱。

你买入，池子里的代币减少，USDT增加，报价会变。

你卖出，池子里的代币增加，USDT减少，报价也会变。

所以，不能拿屏幕上的最新价格，直接乘以全部持仓，就认为那是自己已经赚到的钱。

池子越浅，一笔买卖越容易把价格推得很远。

还要看主要流动性份额在谁手里，能不能被撤走。筹码有没有锁仓，和池子能不能被撤，是两件事。

五、上现货，增加了一个买卖代币的市场

项目可以申请上币，交易所也可能主动关注，然后按照各自标准进行评估、技术接入和开盘准备。

没有市值到了多少，就一定自动上所的统一规则。

正式开放现货交易后，用户可以在交易所买卖代币余额。平台支持对应网络并开放提币时，还可以把币提到自己的钱包。

上现货通常不需要重新发币，也不需要把币搬到交易所自己的链上。

这里提醒新手注意首发这两个字。

要看清楚，是这个币第一次发行，还是这家交易所第一次开放交易。

如果它之前已经在链上买卖，那么早期持有人、他们的成本和手里的筹码，都不会因为上了交易所就重新开始。

你觉得自己赶上了第一天，先确认是哪一个市场的第一天。

还有，交易所App里的链上交易专区，也要和常规现货区分开。能搜到、能买到，不足以证明已经上线现货交易对。

六、上合约，可以做多做空，但没有因此拿到币

假设交易所上线小狗币USDT永续。

你可以建立多仓，也可以建立空仓。以常见的USDT结算产品为例，持有的是交易仓位，盈亏按照价格变化用USDT结算。

开了相当于1万枚小狗币的多仓，钱包里不会因此多出1万枚小狗币，也不能把这份仓位直接当成币提走。

合约还涉及保证金、资金费和强平。价格方向看对了，也要考虑仓位能不能承受中间的波动。

上现货和上合约，没有固定的先后顺序。有的先上现货，有的先上永续，还有盘前合约。

看到合约公告，不能直接推断本所现货马上就会上。合约成交了多少，也不能直接当作有多少钱在链上买币。

一个币走到这里，可能有链上池子、交易所现货、永续合约等多个市场，但并非每个币都能走完这些阶段。

以后看到快毕业、马上上所、准备开合约，先点开公告，确认到底说的是哪件事。

再回头看筹码和流动性。

谁手里有币，什么时候能卖，你卖的时候有多少资金能接住。这几个问题，比上所两个字更值得研究。

你第一次看到这个币，未必是它刚刚开始。

text:
This is the first and the last post I'll make about ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 buybacks.

This post is my own view of the situation. It has nothing to do with the other Lido Labs contributors, Lido DAO, or any other organisation related to the Lido DAO. This is not financial advice.

Buybacks in Lido consist of the 2 separate parts:
- Automated buybacks via NEST smart contracts
- Short-living mandate granted to Lido Ecosystem Foundation to acquire ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 from the market at a price considered low by the Lido Ecosystem Foundation

There have been a lot of comments from different accounts here and on https://t.co/z2yT4PEC0p about both parts.

I see the situation as follows, and think that the commenters usually miss several important facts and factors.

On NEST

The automated system and its parameters have been discussed on the research forum (https://t.co/7BDZopFYlV) and approved by the ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders via the on-chain vote (https://t.co/cl79NCwilr).

Since ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders supported the proposal and the parameters (50% of the yearly revenue above 40M$ goes to buyback or provide liquidity for ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 vs ethereum:0xae7ab96520de3a18e5e111b5eaab095312d7fe84 pair), I see the situation here as ratified.

The yearly revenue of Lido DAO sits below 40M$ watermark now. Hence, NEST is currently dormant.

If ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders believe that the system or parameters should be changed, they can follow the governance process currently active in Lido DAO (https://t.co/qTsNtXkGo3) and vote for the updated proposal. Simple posting on the forum or here is just a first step. Any decision should be ratified by a vote of ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders.

On manual buybacks executed and managed by the Lido Ecosystem Foundation

The snapshot vote (https://t.co/tBbIxpQJZF) ratified by the ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders' votes clearly covers the mandate granted to the Lido Ecosystem Foundation.

If ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders think that the mandate should be changed, they can start a discussion and proceed with the updated snapshot vote. Should this vote get support from the ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders, the mandate and the conditions will be changed.

Closing thoughts

Creating noise here and on the research forum is the first step of the governance process. Just doing it will not change the decisions ratified by ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders. Anyone can post on the forum, start a snapshot vote, and prepare an on-chain vote.

Lido contributors have always acted within the mandate approved by the ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders and will keep doing so.

If you feel that ethereum:0x5a98fcbea516cf06857215779fd812ca3bef1b32 holders will support your proposal, just create one.

text:
Multi-agent workflows are now the standard for agentic coding. Different subagents, different roles, and different models for each.  

If you run more than one subscription, you need a harness that routes between them well.  

oh-my-pi (omp) does exactly that.  Here's how to set it up in 4 steps 🧵

Step 1: Set up your models 

Type /model and assign a model to each role. Use your best models for slow, plan and advisor roles. Save tokens for the other roles.   

Cross-vendor setups work well - for example, Fable 5.1 writes your plans while GPT Astra reviews them.

Step 2: Define your workflow 

Model roles are just mappings - omp has no built-in workflow, so you define it yourself in plain text and omp saves it locally as markdown definitions in .omp/agents.

The most common setup is: Orchestrator → Planner → Reviewer → Implementer → Reviewer.   

Be explicit that each subagent should defer to the right model role so omp uses the correct model for each step.   

E.g. Reviewer subagent might delegate to the "Slow" model role.  

Step 3: Configure Advisor mode 

Advisor is a unique feature of omp - a subagent that watches mid-orchestration and intervenes if it spots issues.   

Firstly, turn it on! It's off by default. Use a high reasoning model here.   

Note that Advisor will likely overlap with your defined workflow (e.g. it will review plans independently of your reviewer).   

Configure when Advisor should stay silent via WATCHDOG.md

Step 4: Choose your mode  

omp has three modes: plan, goal and vibe.  

Normal mode is all you need. Normal mode still writes plans automatically, so plan mode is optional - but useful if you want a checkpoint before execution begins.   

I never touch goal or vibe mode.

Fin

That's it! omp handles the routing from here - the right model for the right subagent, every time.

Bonus tips: 
• Alt+A to view your agent hub and see what they're doing. 
• Ctrl+R to search your prompt history. 
• Compaction is automatic. Clearing context is still manual however.

text:
Elon 刚确认了 Grok 4.8：

2.5T 参数，使用全新的 C++ software stack 训练，本周完成基础训练，之后进入 RL。

但我觉得最值得关注的其实不是“2.5T”这个数字。

过去一年，大模型的竞争越来越不是单纯比 benchmark，而是在比：

模型能不能稳定跑长任务，
Agent 能不能持续执行，
工具调用会不会中途崩，
推理成本和速度能不能真正支撑生产环境。

如果 Grok 4.8 这套新的 C++ stack 能把训练和推理效率再往前推一步，那它真正影响的可能不是聊天体验提高 10%，而是 Agent 的可用性出现一次台阶式变化。

我自己现在正好在用两台 Grok Bot 跑真实工作流，包括：

Early Alpha discovery、研究/DD、风险识别、链上信息筛选和内容研究。

所以等 4.8 真正开放后，我最想测的也不是 benchmark，而是直接把同一套 production workload 丢给新旧模型 A/B：

看 recall 能不能提高，
幻觉能不能下降，
长任务完成率能不能提高，
单位结果的时间和成本能不能下降。

还有一个很有意思的信号：

大家前两天还在讨论 Grok 4.7，Elon 已经直接开始讲 4.8 了。

AI 模型的版本迭代速度，可能还在继续加速。

真正值得追踪的，不是每次模型发布会上的分数，而是什么时候 Agent 从“偶尔有用”，跨过那条线，变成可以真正替人持续工作的基础设施。

text:
Anyways, the point of sharing this is: we were looking at China’s long-distance ultra-high-voltage (UHV) grid. It’s a truly fascinating state system.

Inner Mongolia is China’s largest electricity exporter. Coal, wind and solar are concentrated in the north and west, while demand sits on the east coast.

How do they send it across the country? UHV.

The lines are meshed into a national system rather than isolated links, so power can be redirected between corridors. The state can prioritise transmission to wherever, or whatever, best serves its interests. It can supply big users that demand the power.

Now, why is this relevant to the AI race?

The UHV lines are now full. Let me simplify.

It means the transmission lines are carrying as much power as they physically can. Each UHV line has a fixed limit ~roughly 8–12 GW. Inner Mongolia has eight lines that can export around 48 GW at any moment. Yet, the region has built far more generation than that; its wind and solar alone are well past 100 GW.

On a windy, sunny day, the wind turbines and solar panels can produce more than the lines can carry.

All this excess power is now stuck in Inner Mongolia. So it’s sensible to put data centres there.

Time-to-power is significantly reduced
author: hananyss

text:
For America to win the AI race, it needs to rapidly build out its electricity infrastructure and get more out of the grid it already has.

As @deanwball puts it, even the most basic electricity infrastructure (transmission lines, transformers and gas turbines) is badly supply constrained.

Transformers take three to four years to arrive, whilst a new transmission line takes seven to ten.
So the faster way is to squeeze more out of the grid America already has.

How do you utilise more?

One way is to look at grid capacity and queues.

For most of the year, the US grid has far more capacity than it uses. It only hits its limit for about 20 hours a year, during extreme heat or cold. Most days, it has plenty of spare power.

Yet when a data centre applies for a connection, the utility (the company that owns the grid wires) assumes the data centre will draw full power even on those extreme days. 

So they say: hey, we’ll build more capacity first, then connect you with power.

But again, building the pipe is slow.

Dean Ball’s idea on flexibility trade is worth considering here. 

Let the data centre connect now, and in return it agrees to power down on those few extreme weather days. 

This could free up ~76 GW, buying America roughly five years to build more transmission and other capacity like nuclear, geothermal and, eventually, fusion.

Squeeze the lemon you already have.

text:
Zebrafish NN

It’s pretty amazing to learn that efforts to map the fruit FLY connectome (brain synapses) were successful and its amazing to see the digital fly brain successfully complete a whole series of tasks, including complex navigation of open worlds.

The fruit fly is 160,000 neurons and 10^7 synapses.

Teams are currently doing the same thing with a zebrafish which has a similar scale neuron count but 10x more synapses. Fly was 100TB raw data and Zebrafish is 200TB, so about 2x the raw data.

For context a rodent is 70m neurons and 10^11 synapses. Rodents will come later.

But this method looks like it creates totally outsized results with absolutely miniscule models.

Zebrafish NN is a vertebrae connectome, it has much of the same basic structure as other vertebrae, unlike FLY connectome.

We are just about used to LLMs and coding, but AI is really just beginning and there is a lot more, and a lot weirder stuff coming down the pipe.

These connectomes have already shown to be incredibly resilient, you can blind their sensors and injure their outputs and they still succeed.

They are incredibly compact. 

A whole lot of inanimate objects are going to get complete autonomy, totally offline, air gapped autonomy. They will be delivering pizzas and fighting wars.

Connectomics is an opposite approach to LLMs but you can of course use LLMs to help develop connectomes.

It’s amazing that you can take a biologically evolved brain, map it, produce a digital twin, and then run it at machine speed.

Imagine a human brain accelerated from 100Hz neuron fires to 3,200,000,000Hz that a typical CPU runs at. That’s 30 million times faster. But would need 1-2 exabytes to map.

Anyway “Zebrafish” is next.
