text:
Gm Folks
We are back!

This is another edition of the Predict Alpha Report, our bi-monthly collaboration with @CoinsiliumGroup tracking the rise of prediction markets, event-driven finance, and the growing role of AI agents within it. Each edition focuses on the signals that matter, from capital flows and fundraising activity to regulatory shifts and product innovation. As information is increasingly priced in real time by both humans and machines, the Predict Alpha Report will track where these signals lead.
But first, let’s get this part out of the way:

Always DYOR:
This bulletin is for informational purposes only and contains summaries of news articles originally published by third-party media outlets. Please refer to the full disclaimer at the end of the post.

Now, let’s get started.
Here are the highlights:

💸 Capital Signals

👉Polymarket Valued at $21 Billion
👉 Protecting AI Agents
👉Double The Valuation
👉CEO of Coinsilium-backed Predictive Labs to Join Global Prediction Markets Leaders at NextPredict New York

📈 Industry Pulse

👉Kalshi Launches Perps
👉Robinhood Takes Stake in OG,com
👉Growing Fast…
👉Kazakhstan-based ITS launches Prediction Market
👉Banning Just Advertises

💸 Capital Signals

💰 Polymarket Valued at $21 Billion

@Polymarket is raising $1 billion in a new funding round that values the prediction market platform at $21 billion post-money, up 40% from the $15 billion valuation it secured in April. The round is being led by 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, with the firm expected to invest about $300 million on top of roughly $200 million it has already committed. Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, remains Polymarket’s largest shareholder with a stake of around 22%.

Polymarket has also been building out its institutional credentials through partnerships with firms such as Palantir, stronger market-surveillance capabilities, and a return to the U.S. through its acquisition of a federally regulated exchange.

💰 Protecting AI Agents

HiddenLayer has raised $100 million in a Series B led by Delta-v Capital, with participation from Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, Microsoft’s M12, and Booz Allen Ventures. The company builds security tools specifically for AI systems, including autonomous agents that can take actions, use software tools, and write code with limited human oversight. The funding will go toward expanding its Agentic Runtime Security platform and a new product for protecting AI coding agents during operation.

HiddenLayer says its annual recurring revenue grew more than 10x over the past year, while it added more than 50 enterprise customers across financial services, government, defense, pharmaceuticals, and technology. Venture investors have already put roughly $435 million into 12 enterprise AI agent security deals between April and September, as protecting AI agents becomes one of the next major cybersecurity markets.

💰Double The Valuation

Clay has raised $115 million in a Series D led by Wellington, valuing the New York-based sales automation company at $7.1 billion. The round also included Sequoia, StepStone, Andreessen Horowitz, and Perennial, and more than doubles Clay’s $3.1 billion valuation from August 2025.
Its platform helps sales and marketing teams pull together business data, identify potential customers, and automate personalized outreach, with customers including Google and Anthropic. The jump in valuation reflects a trend reshaping the sales and marketing technology market.

And rounding up this section:

💰CEO of Coinsilium-backed Predictive Labs to Join Global Prediction Markets Leaders at NextPredict New York

@Predictive_Labs CEO @johann_evrard will join more than 90 speakers at NextPredict in New York on 22 and 23 October 2026, alongside prominent figures from media, finance and academia. The event comes as prediction markets continue to expand rapidly, increasing the need for better data infrastructure—an area addressed by @nijinn_official, Predictive Labs’ platform for aggregating, normalising and organising fragmented prediction-market data into a unified global index and analytics interface.

📌 FYI: Coinsilium’s shares are traded on the Aquis Stock Exchange Growth Market in London, under the ticker symbol "COIN", and on the OTCQB Venture Market in the United States under the ticker symbol "CINGF".

But it’s not just capital flowing into the space.
Keep reading for the latest signals in regulation, adoption, and structure.

📈 Industry Pulse

⚡️Kalshi Launches Perps

@Kalshi has launched perpetual futures tied to gold and silver after receiving CFTC approval, making them the first non-crypto perpetual contracts cleared for trading in the U.S. Perpetual futures, or “perps,” work like traditional futures but do not expire, allowing traders to maintain exposure without repeatedly rolling contracts forward. Kalshi says its commodity event contracts have already generated more than $400 million in trading volume in seven months, while its crypto perpetuals have reached $44 billion in notional volume since launching earlier this year.

The move expands Kalshi beyond prediction markets and further into territory traditionally dominated by futures exchanges. The company has also filed to offer perpetual contracts linked to equity indexes, copper, currencies, and a wider range of stocks and ETFs.

⚡️Robinhood Takes Stake in OG,com

@RobinhoodApp is taking equity stakes in @cryptocom and its newly spun-out prediction market platform @OG_com as part of a multi-year partnership that will expand Robinhood’s event-contract business.
The investments are being priced off recent valuations of $20 billion for Crypto,com and $5 billion for OG,com, although the size of Robinhood’s stakes has not been disclosed. Beginning September 8, eligible U.S. customers will gain access to selected contracts routed through OG,com’s CFTC-regulated exchange and clearing infrastructure, covering areas such as sports, financial markets, economics and culture.

OG,com gains distribution through Robinhood’s large retail platform, while Robinhood adds another regulated source of contracts and clearing capacity as competition across prediction markets intensifies.

⚡️Growing Fast…

Prediction markets have become one of @coinbase’s fastest-growing revenue products, with annual run rate revenue passing $100 million in the second quarter of 2026, roughly double the level from the previous quarter when the product launched. Coinbase CFO Alesia Haas said, “We are just getting started with prediction markets, but we have seen the ability to take a product, enter the market, and see scaling occur,”.

The growth is a part of Coinbase’s broader push to become an “everything exchange” by expanding into derivatives, equities, tokenized assets, and prediction markets. Coinbase sees prediction markets becoming more financially useful over time, potentially extending beyond elections and sports into contracts tied to corporate metrics such as revenue or earnings.

⚡️Kazakhstan-based ITS launches Prediction Market

Kazakhstan-based International Trading System Limited (ITS) has launched a prediction market product that lets eligible investors trade event contracts tied to outcomes such as Bitcoin prices, SpaceX, the National Bank of Kazakhstan’s base rate, and the U.S. Federal Reserve’s policy rate.

ITS already offers more than 3,200 securities and recorded over $14 billion in trading volume in 2025, giving the new product access to an established regional investor base. The platform plans to expand beyond its initial contracts into areas such as macroeconomic data, commodities, and corporate events, potentially making event-based trading a more regular part of how investors across Central Asia and other international markets express views on the future.

⚡️Banning Just Advertises

A new analysis from CasinoReviewsnet suggests that efforts to restrict prediction markets may be increasing curiosity rather than reducing it. Looking at 12 months of Google Trends data alongside election calendars and regulatory actions, the research found that eight of the 15 countries with the highest relative search interest in Polymarket currently restrict or have banned the platform.

The pattern is especially interesting because restrictions don’t necessarily stop access or expansion. For instance, Polymarket is still building China-focused markets and hiring Mandarin-speaking staff despite being blocked there, while Asia-based trading reportedly reaches hundreds of millions of dollars a month, often through VPNs. The data does not prove that bans directly drive usage, but it demonstrates that blocking a platform does not eliminate demand for the product itself.

And that’s it!

如果把相对论从 AI 的训练数据里删掉，它还能自己成为爱因斯坦吗？

Nature 最近专门写了一篇「Einstein Test」。

今年 2 月，DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis 提了一个很有意思的测试方法：

只给 AI 看 1911 年以前的人类知识，然后让它自己往下推，看能不能重新发现广义相对论。

他甚至说，这会是一个很好的 AGI 测试。

现在已经有几组人在真做了，结果暂时不太乐观。

MIT 的研究者拿不同恒星系统的轨道数据训练模型，希望它自己推出牛顿万有引力定律。模型确实找到了规律，但每个行星系统都总结出一套不同的「引力定律」，而且都错了。

还有人用 1900 年以前的数据训练了一个模型，再把光电效应、爱因斯坦的电梯思想实验等线索塞给它。

模型偶尔会冒出一些很像正确方向的话，比如意识到光可能由一个个离散的「冲量」组成，但继续追问，就会发现它经常只是在拼凑听起来合理的物理学语言。

现在的 AI 已经非常擅长在一个已经存在的框架里预测、搜索、证明和组合知识。AlphaFold、GraphCast，包括最近 AI 在数学上的大量突破，都证明了这一点。

可爱因斯坦真正难的地方，在于当时根本没有「相对论」这个框架供他搜索。

他需要从很少的异常现象里，先怀疑旧问题的问法，再发明新的概念和原则。

人类物理学的发展，是从观察规律，到总结定律，再到建立相对论这种统一世界观；AI 的发展路径似乎正在反过来，越来越擅长预测，却未必越来越接近「理解」。

“Even if models never improved from here…

just rolling out what they can already do would take more compute than the world can build for years”

author: aleabitoreddit
quoted_text:
A few people asked over the weekend what the calls to slow the pace of frontier AI mean for the buildout. Some thoughts:

Even if models never improved from here, just rolling out what they can already do would take more compute than the world can build for years. The debate about how fast AI should be allowed to improve is a fair one to have. It's about future generations of models.

Existing demand is the part I think people are misreading. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in May they'd planned for 10x growth and were running at an 80x pace in the first quarter, and that's why they've had trouble supplying compute. OpenAI president Greg Brockman said in July they'll be in a compute shortage no matter what, and are choosing which products to scale. Google says it's processing 7x the tokens it did a year ago. Hundreds of millions of people use these models today, and most of them use a small part of what the models can already do. And every time more compute comes online, usage steps up again: limits come off for people already using it, customers who were turned away get on, and new use cases show up that weren't in anyone's plan.

Now supply. The constraint is HBM, the memory that sits inside every major AI chip. Three companies make it and all three are sold out this year. A new memory plant takes years to build. TrendForce has HBM shipments growing 50-60% next year. NVIDIA, the biggest buyer of it, expects its revenue to grow about 70% next year and calls that outlook 'supply-constrained', noting its customers' forecasts point closer to 100%. On our own bottom-up work, the memory constraint lands in about the same place as NVIDIA's growth number.

Then the chips need a building with power connected, which takes longer again. Goldmans reckons only about half the US capacity scheduled over the next two years will actually be built on time.

The risk to demand continues to seem heavily weighted to the upside. The risk to supply continues to seem weighted toward less capacity getting built, not more.

text:
1⃣OpenAI Says 10,000 AI Agents Solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Problem in 88 Hours

📰On September 8, OpenAI said a stronger unreleased internal model organized about 10,000 concurrent AI agents and produced a proof of existence and smoothness for the Navier-Stokes equations in 88 hours. It then spent 17 hours completing Lean formal verification, and published a 166-page paper plus code. The company said it would not claim the Clay Mathematics Institute’s $1 million prize.

🧠DA’s Take: 88 hours, 10,000 agents, 166 pages. This was not one model “thinking.” It was a crowd of AIs arguing, then handing the result to Lean as referee. The math matters, but the method matters more: concurrent agents dividing work, checking each other, and closing the case with formal verification. AI problem-solving is shifting from one student taking a test to an organized campaign. OpenAI skipping the prize is also telling. The money is not the point. The point is that the world now knows this method can work. Multi-agent work was never short on compute. It was short on who decides and who has verified. DeAgentAI puts reasoning on-chain to give that kind of collaboration an immutable referee layer. You prove yours, I verify mine, the result goes on-chain, and nobody can rewrite it.

🧐What do you think: AI teams solve the hard problems and humans only verify. Will mathematicians become the people who set the questions, or the audience?

text:
马斯克已经把饼画到 Grok 5 了。

他最新给 Grok 排了一张战力表：

Grok 4.7，大概相当于 Opus 5.0，某些地方更强，某些地方更弱，多模态还得补课；

Grok 4.8，会有一次明显提升；

Grok 4.9，目标是 Astra / Fable 级别；

Grok 5，则「可能超过目前所有产品」。

4.8 已经在训练，马斯克称这是一个 2.5T 参数模型，使用 SpaceXAI 新的 C++ 软件栈，本周结束预训练，随后开始 RL。

这套 C++ 栈其实是六月就画下来的饼。6 月 29 日，马斯克说要在大约三个月内重写 Grok 的训练和推理栈，全面转向 C/C++，砍掉大量软件中间层，并针对英伟达 GB300 做专门优化，届时会出现「巨大提升」。

现在刚好走到三个月这个节点。

问题是，4.7 自己还卡在 RL。

马斯克原本说它大约 9 月 12 日上线，临近发布又承认，RL 可能把回答长度罚得太狠，结果模型碰到难题容易提前放弃，明明会做也不继续做，同时检查自己答案还不够严格。

所以现在 xAI 的状态很有马斯克味：

4.7 还在修，4.8 已经训练完一半，4.9 开始挑战 Astra/Fable，Grok 5 已经准备天下第一。

上一张饼还没出炉，下一张已经进烤箱了。

如果 xAI 真能把训练、推理的软件层大幅压缩，再把整个栈针对 GB300 榨到极致，它带来的可能不只是某一代 Grok 跑分高几分，而是把模型迭代周期继续往按周发版本压。

到时候马斯克最大的优势，可能真的不是每一版都天下第一，而是他永远已经在训练下一版。

quoted_text:
The robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 thesis is worth understanding, so here’s the simplest version I can provide:

- MOO already has approximately $1.7M in liquidity across its tracked pools, not including MOO side liqudity.

- In the latest 24-hour snapshot, MOO traded roughly $3.45M. Around $1.06M (31%) went through its main MOO/MU pool, directly against tokenized Micron.

- The community vault separately displays $95k in MU, with 11M MOO locked and another 11M burned.

There is already a functioning MU market here for only a memecoin. No coordination layer is orchestrated yet, but the team’s next step is to expand it.

According to the livestream on @MCGlive on Friday, @memorycowmoo is working with LONG on additional pairings against 3-4 major tokenized memory stocks. The ambition is to become a liquidity hub for the onchain memory trade.

Why memory?

The AI investment story extends beyond compute and processors.

Memory capacity, bandwidth, and storage are critical parts of the infrastructure and are a well-known bottleneck for the AI industry. robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 is trying to organize a community and trading liquidity around that sector.

Imagine someone rotating between two tokenized memory stocks through robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18. They don’t need to care about the cow. They need a competitive price. Swaps don’t HAVE to go through robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18. But if its pools offer better execution, they can attract that volume.

This is the short-term catalyst:

Those pools also need robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 inventory. LPs without it may need to acquire it. If trading makes the pools attractive to supply, that can bring more liquidity, improve execution, and attract more trading.

The opportunity is to turn a recognizable meme into useful inventory for a growing market.

As tokenized-stock markets develop, the assets that successfully coordinate liquidity could become more valuable. robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 is pursuing a focused version of that opportunity around memory equities.

So what could the liquidity coordination layer be worth?

Using that framework and ignoring any memetic value, we can calculate the asset's liquid value:

Base: $16.5–$40M. Daily pool volume grows to a sustained $10M, roughly three times the latest snapshot, and MOO establishes modest, recurring fee capture.

Bull: $125–$304M. robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 becomes a meaningful memory-equity liquidity hub, supporting around $38M in daily pool volume across all tokenized stock pools.

Extra bull: $1.55–$3.3B. Tokenized memory markets expand dramatically, and robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18 wins substantial adoption, supporting around $275M in daily pool volume.

These numbers exclude any Meme Multiplier, where typical memes trade at 5x to 20x their daily volume.

The most important thing to watch now is whether new pools deliver competitive quotes, attract sustained volume, and direct economic value back to robinhood:0xd9db30bb0d2b8d2eae3826a1372117e058791e18.

Long has already begun achieving this with $AI, and the cow already has attention and an active MU market. The next step is earning a place in how people trade the wider memory sector.

text:
There's a weird economy starting to form around robots.

Humans are generating the experiences machines need to learn how to do human work.

And @axisrobotics is building infrastructure around that process.

I'm contributing here:
https://t.co/EPnmS2s501

The interesting part is what happens when you stop thinking about robot data as just a dataset.

Every task completed on Axis produces a Trajectory.

Every correction can show a model where its policy failed.

Every verified contribution adds another piece of physical-world experience that can potentially be used for training.

Now add the other pieces Axis has been building:

→ verification filters bad data
→ Data IDs create provenance
→ onchain signatures link contributions to contributors
→ Post-Training captures human corrections
→ Challenger routes harder tasks toward stronger contributors

Put those together and something starts to emerge.

Not just a giant pile of robot data.

A contributor network where different humans can produce different levels of useful training data, and where those contributions can be verified and traced back to their source.

That's important because not all robot data should be worth the same.

A clean demonstration of a difficult manipulation task probably carries a different training signal than repeating an easy movement hundreds of times.

Axis is already moving in that direction with Challenger.

Quality matters.
Consistency matters.
Difficulty matters.

Which makes me wonder if Physical AI data eventually starts looking less like a traditional dataset and more like a new kind of labor market.

Millions of people generating, correcting and verifying the experiences machines learn from.

If that happens, the valuable infrastructure won't only be the robots or the models.

It'll also be the layer that can answer:

Who contributed what?

Was it actually useful?

Can it be verified?

And how valuable was that contribution?

That's the part of the @axisrobotics thesis I'm watching now.

The robot economy may need a data economy underneath it.

Years of notes. Old projects. Half-finished ideas. Questions I kept coming back to.

→ Here’s the test that makes this interesting.

Ask a question that crosses years.

“What pattern keeps repeating across my projects?”

Now the task involves connecting things you wrote at different times, for different reasons. A launch journal. A project retrospective. A weekly review.

Then push on the connection.

“Which notes support that?”
“Which ones contradict it?”
“What are you assuming?”

That’s where I’d spend my time. Following the sources. Checking whether the explanation holds up. Finding out whether an apparent pattern survives a harder question.

Your old notes become something you can interrogate.

The decisions you forgot making.
The assumptions you never revisited.
The same problem showing up under three different names.

The video visualizes that workflow. It’s an illustrative concept, not a recording of my vault or a benchmark.

text:
领先别人 42%的 Axis 邪修策略 👏👏👏
如果你追求 Axis 积分，看好未来积分空投
那么 Pendle Mint策略 一定要了解 ⬇️

✅ Mint策略的优势：
相比裸持USDx 或 sUSDx，Pendle Mint 策略能够保持资金灵活性不降低的同时，拿到更多 积分 和 Yield收益

👉 Pendle Mint策略 是什么？
Pendle 有一条底层机制：
1单位的底层资产 Mint to 1单位的PT+1单位的YT，并且可以随时反向无损赎回

即投入 1 USDx 到Pendle mint策略，可以得到
1 PT USDx + 1 YT USDx，mint出的这部分YT 与正常买到的YT权益相同，可以赚取24x积分
什么时候想退出，可以随时无损将 1PT+1YT 赎回为 1 USDx

有些DeFi项目禁止用户这样做，不给Mint出的YT发积分
（因为这个策略对于 YT/PT飞轮 来说没什么贡献）
Axis目前并未明确禁止，并且我已经测试了几天，Mint出的YT是正常给了 24x积分的
如果未来禁止Mint策略，大概率也不会收回已经发放的MINT-YT积分

～～～

❤️ OK，让我们来测算一下 USDx 与 sUSDx 的Mint策略实际收益好在哪里！

1️⃣ USDx 的Mint策略
裸持 100 USDx 的收益是：每天1600积分（16倍x100 ）

✅ 投入100 USDx到Pendle Mint策略 每天可以得到：
24 x 100 x 95%（Pendle 抽成5%） = 2280积分 
比裸持多了 42.5% 积分 😱‼️

2️⃣ sUSDx 的Mint策略
裸持 100个 sUSDx 的收益为：
sUSDx 生息yield + 每天400积分（4倍x100 ）

✅ 投入100 sUSDx到Pendle Mint策略 每天可以得到：
YT底息yield x 95% + 每天570积分（6倍x100x95% ）
🔹YT底息yield 基本上与 sUSDx 的自生息yield相同，只是要被Pendle抽成5%
🔹sUSDx的积分倍数应该是以美元价值x积分倍数的，这里为了方便展示，直接按照 sUSDx 数量x积分倍数
🔹sUSDx的Mint策略复杂一些，进和出是以底层资产USDx为计价单为的。所以退出时是金本位不变，币本位会变少，应有的Yield收益会通过YT底息返还（pendle 官网领取）

quoted_text:
THE FIRST AGREEMENT BETWEEN AI AGENTS WITH LEGAL WEIGHT 🤖⚖️🤖
 
A Ricardian contract is an idea cryptographer Ian Grigg proposed in the 1990s: a document that is at once a legally binding agreement humans can read and sign, and a machine-readable object whose terms are tied to on-chain execution. The legal text and the code point at the same thing.
 
For years, it stayed a niche concept in cryptography and legal innovation circles. But now, with the rise of agentic commerce, it's coming to life.
 
ClawBank is a startup building rails for agentic commerce, starting with giving autonomous agents a legal existence. Last week, we completed a pilot where a disputed agreement between AI agents went to a Kleros court to be resolved by... a panel of AI agents.

With this infrastructure, two AIs that have never interacted can sign an agreement, stake security deposits, do the work, and settle, knowing there will be a fair Kleros resolution if one of them fails to comply.
 
A contract is worth what it costs to break it. Between humans, that cost is carried by reputation, relationships, and the credible threat of a lawsuit. An autonomous agent had none of that. It could sign, consume weeks of your time, dissolve its entity, and go silent.
 
Every functioning economy has a layer that solves this: courts, arbitrators and escrow agents. It's the reason why we can do business with someone we have never met. The agent economy was missing it.
 
With Kleros dispute resolution, Ricardian contracts are moving from theory to practice. Happy to have worked with ClawBank in making this happen.

text:
之前分享过李博杰 @bojie_li  的《深入理解 AI Agent》，最近他又开源了姊妹篇《深入理解 AI Infra：量化分析与系统设计》。

这本我很推荐，尤其是已经开始做模型部署、推理或者 Agent 系统的人。

它没有停留在「有哪些推理优化技术」，而是从一个更基础的问题开始：一个模型为什么会慢，瓶颈到底在哪里？

权重和 KV Cache 能不能放下、带宽够不够、计算要多久、多卡以后通信会不会先卡住……作者的思路是先把这些约束算清楚，再决定系统应该怎么设计。

后面一路覆盖模型架构、加速器、算子、互联、推理优化、分布式推理到训练系统。还有 106 项配套实验和计算，很多数字都可以直接用 Python 重新算一遍。

我非常喜欢这种学习 AI Infra 的方式。很多系统概念单独看都懂，但真正做工程时，更重要的是能判断「这个方案物理上到底跑不跑得通」。

之前看过《深入理解 AI Agent》的话，这本正好可以继续往模型下面再挖一层。

text:
Every new EVM environment gets called an L2. The label is wrong for Zenith, and the difference is worth understanding precisely.

L2s sit outside their base layer. They capture fees above it, divert value from the network underneath, and call it composability. Zenith is the opposite.

Zenith is not a rollup, not a sidechain, and not a subnet. It is an extension of @CantonNetwork's Mainnet consensus, the first atomic EVM ever built, co-architected hand-in-hand with Digital Asset's co-founders alongside Canton's core protocol development. Every EVM transaction on Zenith is native Canton activity. No value extracted outside the network. No isolated environment sitting above it.

If the trademark allowed it, the simplest description would be Canton EVM. @HeslinKim unpacks the full architecture and what it means for developers in his recent @TheCryptoMavs podcast episode.

text:
Grok Bot summary of Maye Musk’s new interview ahead of the launch of her book, Timeless.

On Elon today
- Says negative coverage is crushing; she asked Grok and got ~80% negative
- Politics sometimes diverge, but watching him attacked still hurts
- Accusations of racism / “Nazi” bother her most: “dishonest,” and they bring death threats
- Family meetups now happen off-grid: “Elon can’t go anywhere”
- When she visits, she sits in his hourly weekend meetings until ~11pm; loves the “nerds”
- Says privately he’s a good dad; sticks to “18 grandchildren” (Elon has 14 confirmed kids across partners)

Who she is right now
- Just back from Shanghai; then US press, Hong Kong talks, Texas talks
- Still booking fashion (Dior, Dolce & Gabbana, SI swimsuit at 74)
- Spends 4+ hours a day on X; big following in China after *A Woman Makes a Plan*
- Fine being known as “Elon’s mom” — even joked about naming the book that
- Kimbal (Tesla/SpaceX board, restaurants) and Tosca (Passionflix) are “happy” with less fame

Security and fallout
- Tosca’s business hit with a smear; Kimbal’s with a bomb threat
- She goes to events only if nobody knows she’s coming

Hard early life (from the interview + book)
- Married Errol Musk after a bungled proposal her parents were told she’d accepted
- Describes emotional, physical, and financial abuse (Errol denies it)
- Divorced in 1979 in ~10 days once no-fault divorce became possible; asked only for the kids
- Later: Canada on $2,000, tiny flat, shared beds; at 50 in California still so broke she borrowed from the kids
- Not into therapy or deep “feelings” talk: “I went through hard times, but other women have had it worse”

Raising Elon
- Knew he was a “genius” by age 3 — he’d reason about shopping costs
- Quiet, bookish, sleep-deprived (read all night); siblings were the social ones
- No pocket money: “they had to look after themselves”
- At 10 he chose to live with Errol for encyclopedias, library, computer; Maye couldn’t afford one
- Elon later called that period miserable; Rolling Stone 2017: father a “terrible human being”
- Piece notes 2025 NYT reporting on abuse allegations involving Errol (denied, no conviction)
- Bullied at school, once hospitalized; teachers called him “dreamy”; family called him “our encyclopaedia”
- Couldn’t predict the billion-dollar companies: “brilliant kids… sit in a basement” too
- On every big idea: “Every. Idea.” seemed far-fetched — until it worked
- Mars for her? No. “I’m 78… the last person they would want on Mars.”

Mama-bear mode
- Mediated Zip2 fights between Elon and Kimbal on Saturdays (even pulled them apart)
- Elon = facts-first (moon-distance kid energy); Kimbal softer on people
- Defends him aggressively on X: “I get angry and then I crap on them”
- Sees media treating him like a “Bond villain”; she’d tell critics: he’s trying to make life better, not for himself
- Book extract: after politics / brief Trump adviser role in 2025, hate jumped off the page into daily life (Tesla protests, death threats)
- Misreads of him (awkward gesture, stammer, jokes) vs the socially awkward son she knows
- Coping strategy: she can’t control the press so be cheerleader, “let the haters hate”

A mother’s portrait: tough, loyal, image-savvy, still grinding at 78. The piece is half book promo, half defense brief for Elon, grounded in a brutal early marriage, a lonely gifted kid, and a family now living with fame’s security tax.

🤖 Puffer for AI #4 - Connected Liquidity

AI agents need more than fast execution. They need access to deep, connected liquidity.

Ethereum is home to some of crypto’s deepest liquidity, but as activity spreads across rollups and appchains, that liquidity becomes increasingly fragmented. For agents trading, rebalancing, routing payments, or interacting across markets, this fragmentation adds friction.

@puffer_unifi is designed to give AI agents dedicated execution without cutting them off from Ethereum’s liquidity.

Through synchronous composability and Ethereum-aligned sequencing, UniFi can support agent-specific execution while keeping it closely connected to Ethereum L1 liquidity.

For autonomous systems, liquidity should stay connected wherever execution happens. 🐡

BitMine Buys 27,180 ETH, Bringing Holdings to 5.96M ETH  

BitMine said it acquired 27,180 ETH over the past week, bringing its total holdings to 5.96 million ETH as of September 13. The position represents about 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122 million ETH supply, putting the company 98% of the way toward its goal of owning 5% of all ETH. text:
I remember how a few years ago, I'd always fall for the fomo on CT.

During a bull, there is a new game-changing project and a new runner every day. Always new airdrops to farm, and a new point system here or there.

That made me split my capital across too many assets, plays and venues.

This time I did things differently, having concentrated my holdings in $HYPE (my high conviction play) a long time ago, and only using smol amounts of capital to chase other stuff.

Sure that means I miss a bunch of things along the way. But based on my personal experience and looking at how things are going so far, the results should be much better than my previous spray and pray approach.
author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
one of the hardest things in a bull run is not to fall for the constant fomo.

even on days when your portfolio is up, scrolling CT might feel like you're losing bc the timeline feels like everyone is pulling in millions almost daily.

and every day there is a new runner you missed, another perp DEX you. didn't farm, and a whitelist you're not on

but the one thing you should NOT do, is fall for it.

not just because a lot of it is fake.

also because it will make you act irresponsibly.

if you open your long when the pump is already topping out or ape the meme you've been eyeing once your entire timeline is talking about it, you're just exit liquidity.

and you probably know that.

but in fear of missing out, you'll still chase an opportunity that is already gone.

just to miss the next one because you were too busy and/or are too frustrated that the market "always goes against me".

it doesn't.

it's all just about not losing track.

build conviction and keep it = win.

change direction emotionally = lose.

author: puffer_unifi
quoted_text:
🤖 Puffer for AI #4 - Connected Liquidity

AI agents need more than fast execution. They need access to deep, connected liquidity.

Ethereum is home to some of crypto’s deepest liquidity, but as activity spreads across rollups and appchains, that liquidity becomes increasingly fragmented. For agents trading, rebalancing, routing payments, or interacting across markets, this fragmentation adds friction.

@puffer_unifi is designed to give AI agents dedicated execution without cutting them off from Ethereum’s liquidity.

Through synchronous composability and Ethereum-aligned sequencing, UniFi can support agent-specific execution while keeping it closely connected to Ethereum L1 liquidity.

For autonomous systems, liquidity should stay connected wherever execution happens. 🐡

Happy to formally announce I've joined @nansen_ai as the new Head of Marketing.

The New Game of Trading: Vision + Thesis

With the world becoming increasingly more risk on and speculating on assets continue to gain momentum (sports gambling, prediction markets, options and perps, collectibles etc), I believe building for that future, and equipping users with exceptional tools, data, and digital experiences is where i'll be putting my focus.

The game of trading traditionally has been siloed between the people with edge, and ones without. As those lines begin to blur and the tools people now use become more advanced, there's a clear sign on where the puck is moving.

Two things become clear:

1. The Rise of Social Trading - In a progressively digital world, where AI commoditizes content and the amount of content aggressively expands (dead internet theory), status and social equity are becoming more valuable than ever. A trading platform that can grow a user's PnL as well as their social equity, credibility and community will win. This also increasingly spreads organic reach, distribution and a sticky digital experience for this new trading paradigm.

The current state of social trading allows for the top <1% to win and the other 99% to lose. Part of their edge is social equity, and it's not evenly distributed.

Users need additional tools & signal to gain edge.

2. Edge w/ Data & AI - The moat between the haves and have nots is curated data. I believe more traders are not only becoming more quantitative but also increasingly qualitative at the same time.

Qualitative signal (social):
- Narrative shifts
- Public figures bull/bear posting on social media
- Pop culture/social trends

Quantitative signal (data):
- Onchain data
- AI trading bots
- Wallet tracking

Where those two meet is where I think we can win.

Whatever your preconceptions are about the current iteration of Nansen's trading platform, I can assure you, things are going to change very quickly...

More on that soon.

Excited to build something incredible.

📌花了点时间，终于搞明白了，这个能让远古大佬火星人都出来买币支持的 Tapeout 到底是个啥项目——

据说创始人 @Blonskr 是个 16 岁的天才小孩哥，前面跟 CZ 公开互动过。

我只想说：是不是每个人第一次打开 TapeOut 页面，都会跟我一样，一脸懵逼！

TapeOut 本质上在做一件事，把“计算逻辑”本身，做成可以拥有、组合、复用、交易，甚至拿去挖矿的链上资产，是一个开发者与交易者社区。

整个核心流程为：

1⃣ 获取逻辑组件

TapeOut 里会有 NAND、LATCH 这种基础逻辑组件，项目把这些组件统称为 “transistors”。

2⃣ 在网页画布上组装电路

把组件拖到画布上，通过连线把一个组件的输出接到另一个组件的输入，最后拼成一套完整逻辑。

3⃣ 把设计永久记录到链上

设计满意后点击 Tape Out，消耗相应组件，生成一个不可修改的电路 Circuit。

4⃣让 Circuit 参与 PoD 挖矿

电路可以作为“矿机”参与任务，根据设计是否匹配任务、验证权重和算力表现获得 $BEM。

那么问题来了：

这个 Circuit 到底是什么？

它不是现实世界里那种由晶体管、电阻、电容、金属连线组成的实体电路。

在 TapeOut 里，Circuit 本质上是一套被永久记录在链上的“逻辑连接关系”。

可以把它理解成：

组件 = 乐高积木；
连线 = 拼装方式；
Circuit = 组装完成并上链的作品。

完成后的 Circuit 可以继续被当作一个黑盒模块，之后再被拖进其他设计中继续组合，也支持复用他人已经完成的电路。

这么一看，是不是有点像币圈和 GameFi 版的 github ~

总体而言，这是一个很有实验性和叙事差异化的链上计算项目，概念很新颖。

感兴趣的可以自己玩一下，一些聪明钱都开始关注了，不知道有没有机会！

管伊朗叫爸爸吧！

说实话，最近做空石油确实让我有些焦虑了。

焦虑的并不是石油的价格上涨，我准备金都是到 120 美元的，而且即便是 120 美元不够，拉到 150 美元都没啥问题，所以我焦虑的从来都不是方向。

这次让我焦虑的首先是川普和美国的态度，我的观点始终都是高油价会让美国陷入高通胀，而高通胀又会逼迫美联储进入到加息流程，加息对美国经济和风险市场的影响就不言而喻了。

其次是全球对伊朗的态度，霍尔木兹的封锁带来的并不仅仅是美国油价的上涨，还是全球油价和通胀的上涨，即便是中国，石油战略储备已经突破天际了，但仍然因为伊朗港口的封锁而上涨油价。

现在反而是全球都被伊朗给钳制了，号称军事实力第一的美国没有把伊朗打服，全球第二大经济体的中国也因为霍尔木兹而束手无措。

最让我焦虑的其实就是这里。

如果只是油价涨到 100、110，甚至 120 美元，对我的仓位来说都只是浮亏的问题，只要保证金足够，我可以继续等。

但如果美国、欧洲、中国以及海湾国家，都没有办法在短时间内改变霍尔木兹目前的状态，那么市场交易的就不再是一次短期战争冲击，而是全球能源贸易体系被迫接受一个长期受到伊朗控制的霍尔木兹。

这才是最离谱的地方。

一个伊朗，就能让全球经济陷入被动。

甚至不需要什么高精尖武器，不需要航母，也不需要真正控制整个印度洋。

只要小艇、无人机、导弹，再加上霍尔木兹这个地理位置，就足以让大型商船和油轮不敢正常通行。

而只要霍尔木兹不能正常通行，受到影响的也不只是伊朗自己的石油，而是沙特、伊拉克、科威特、卡塔尔、阿联酋大量能源出口。

全球最重要的一条能源航道，就这么被一个国家卡住了。

美国天天说维护航行自由，中国每天需要大量进口原油，欧洲和亚洲都在承担更高的能源成本，海湾国家自己的石油也运不出去。

结果大家一起看着伊朗拿霍尔木兹当筹码。

那这个世界还折腾什么。

以后管伊朗叫爸爸好了。

text:
时间线上最常见的帖子，不是分析，是 "我赚了"。

截图能 P，但地址一亮又等于把进出点、加仓位置、止盈节奏全送出去。

晒了怕被复制，不晒又像在演戏。

成绩想被看见，但路径不想被看穿，这是套利人最常见的别扭，不是矫情。

我这十天也卡在同一处。

币股这波很香，5WU 进去，十天做到接近 9WU。

每天都想发出来，给自己留个复盘，也让时间线看见这波不是嘴上功夫。可几次鼠标停在发送按钮上，犹犹豫豫，还是没发，只在群里秀了几张地址余额截图。

不发地址，就剩一句 "我赚了"，默认会被当成吹牛。

发地址，方法就不再是方法。

所以真正要拆开的，不是 "要不要晒"，而是 "别人核验的是结果，还是你的钱包和手法"。

这事放到机构和大户身上，只是同一句话换了量级。

个人怕的是地址一亮，方法被抄干。

机构怕的是仓位、进出时机和执行路径在公链上实时可见，策略还没跑完，就被定价、被抢跑。

链上默认透明，对散户是社交负担，对要上链的真金白银是成本。

所以机构要的隐私，不是把记录抹掉，而是自己内部仍可审计，对外只公开该被核验的那一层。

验证解决 "是不是真的"，隐私决定 "公开到哪一步"。

两件事拆不开，大户和机构才敢把规模放上来。

而 8 月底获得 @yzilabs 融资的隐私项目 @primus_labs 能解决这个问题，把这两件事分开：证明你做成了，同时不必把路径摊开。

虽然目前它还做不到一键证明 "这十天赚了近一倍"。

但它已经先在两处把同一结构跑通了：

1/ 和 Kaito 合作，是在证人。证明你参与过、交易过，而不必把账户摊开；

2/ 和 Unitas 合作，是在证钱。证明储备够不够、健不健康，而不必直播操盘。一边把声量里的假参与滤掉，一边让机构在不泄密的前提下被信任。

个人要的那张成绩单，和机构要的那份储备证明，底层是同一件事：先证明是真的，再决定公开多少。

这比再解释一遍合作更重要。

商业上先把 "可核验但不泄密" 做出来。

也更能解释它后来拿到 YZi Labs 投资这件事：先有场景，再有资本站台，不是反过来。

从个人需求出发：可以在保证隐私的前提下，在 X 上用真实代替虚假。以后发帖可以少一点截图，多一张证明。

机构那边要解决的，其实是同一句话的放大版：上链，但不广播路径。

对 Primus 技术感兴趣的小伙伴，详见 @anymose 老师推文～

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

author: BitHappy
quoted_text:
你 X 喊单可以，敢不敢让我验牌？

行情来了最烦就是一堆喊单的，喊了不晒钱包，晒了也不知道归属…总之不要看一个人说了什么，更重要是看他做了什么。

问题来了，区块链里怎么看？过去很容易衡量一个人说了多少，如果追问 X 上说的和链下真实做的一致吗？谁敢应答？

让我们潜入！

⬇️

Kaito 复活了？我没太关注，倒是收到了好几个朋友给我的邀请，让我去更新 Arua 分数，我一看竟然要装插件，罢了罢了，别再给我钱包偷了…直到刷到老板 @xxiong_xie 推特说 Kaito 新功能 Pulse 是 Powered by Primus 让我一惊，这有趣了。

要理解 Primus 是做什么的，可以先从 Kaito 复活功能 Pulse 看起。 Yap 火了一年多也把 Kaito 送上最热项目，本质其实是记录用户在社交媒体上说了什么、影响力如何，也就是「 Attention 注意力 」，Yaps 就是数值化表达。后来 Yap 陨落，其中一个最根本原因就是老哥啊你只喊项目结果自己都不参与的吗？信任不仅包括你说什么，也得行动一致啊，不过当时的难点也是 Kaito 无法完成「 Behavior verification 行为验证 」。

行为验证，尤其是跨平台的行为数据验证还要能在区块链上计算，这玩意儿真有点技术含量，得专业团队来搞。Kaito Pulse 页面上那行不起眼的 「 Powered by Primus 」以及创始人私下对 zkTLS 的提及，才是真正的关键。

Primus 让用户在不暴露任何原始数据的情况下，证明自己在交易平台、AI 服务、预测市场的真实身份与历史表现。当所有目光都盯着前端热闹时，真正改变游戏规则的，往往是那个默默把信任做成基础设施的人。

于是，我把 Kaito 插件装起来了，数据也对齐了，今天我有 1,253 个 Aura 全球排名 41、中文排名第十，又让我虚荣起来了…这还是我好多数据没有验证的情况下，PM 我验证了一下战绩，emm，减分了吧？通过一阵摸索，我大概搞懂了 Primus 在整个生态里起到了什么作用，试着总结了 3 个技术功能特点，作为周末科普吧。

zkTLS - 不暴露原始数据的行为验证

Web3 项目天天喊真实用户、真实行为，但大多数只能看 X上说了什么，很难确认这个人是不是真的在 Binance 交易过、真的在某个 AI 平台用过、真的在预测市场下注过。传统方式要么完全信任中心化接口，要么让用户把隐私数据全交出来。Primus 的解法是让用户通过浏览器插件，在本地生成一个零知识证明「 我确实在某网站上有某账户/某行为」，但不把账号密码、余额、交易记录等原始数据泄露给任何人。

Kaito 合作把 Primus 的 zkTLS 用在了 Pulse 浏览器插件里。用户可以验证自己在交易平台、AI 服务、预测市场等的真实账户与历史表现，解锁 Aura 分数、获得 Campaign 资格。以前只有「 说得多」的 Yap 分数，现在有了「 说的话和真实行为一致 」的验证层。

多提一句，Primus 的 zkTLS 性能比业界标本 Chainlink 的 Deco 高一个数量级，还拿过以太坊基金会 Grant 。

FHE - 隐私计算真正可用

即使验证了真实数据，放到链上后还是很难用的，信用分、资产证明、交易行为这些数据太敏感，直接上链等于裸奔，传统加密又没法直接计算，Primus 的解法是 FHE + zkFHE。

全同态加密 FHE 之前我科普过了，它允许数据保持加密状态被计算，计算完再解密结果，Primus 进一步做了 zkFHE，防止计算节点作恶。举例子来说，比如借贷协议想用用户的链下信用/行为数据做风控，但不想看到原始数据就需要用到 zkFHE 这种解决方案。事实上 Primus 已经上线 Confidential Finance，项目方做 Proof of Reserve，用更轻量、可实时验证的方式证明资金健康，而不是只给一份静态审计报告。

纯技术尤其是涉及密码学这些玩意儿真不是一般团队可以搞的，除了行业巨头 Zama，Primus 是少数从算法设计、工程实现到产品化全链路具备独立研发能力的团队。创始人在 FHE 关键技术上有早期贡献，非常超强，Primus 也顺利成为 BNB Chain 隐私合作伙伴，哦对，还是 Ezi Residency S4 成员, 获得 @yzilabs 投资。

从验证到可用的完整闭环

Primus 不只是卖一个 zkTLS 插件或 FHE 库，而是在搭建 真实数据进链 → 隐私保护计算 → 实际应用落地的完整管道。官网看了一下，现在的产品矩阵包括浏览器扩展、开发者 Dev Hub、用户自己的 Web3 Profile、社交红包支付、Proof of Reserve 等。

当 InfoFi、真实影响力、链下信用、隐私 DeFi 成为下一阶段刚需时，能同时解决数据真实性和数据隐私计算的基础设施会变得非常稀缺。Primus 已经有真实商业客户、以太坊基金会支持、BNB Chain 合作以及从密码学算法到产品的完整交付能力。

就这，值得一个 Respect 🫡。

总结一下，以前区块链只能相信自己链上的数据，@primus_labs 让互联网上的真实世界也能被安全、隐私地接入链上，并真正被计算和使用，Kaito Pulse 是第一个被看见的案例，可以装个插件走一遍体验一下，无痛无痕。

祝我们好运！

/

What if crypto could front-run the story of a stock—capturing the speculation before the stock ever shows up onchain?

That’s the lane @prm_market is carving out.

Premium spins up synthetic markets called pSTOCKs.

Imagine a penny stock sitting at $0.20. Premium can drop pXYZ near that same level. But don’t confuse the two:

pXYZ isn’t the stock.

No shares in your pocket. No dividends, no votes, no promise you can swap it for the real thing. The stock price is just the launchpad.

From there, pXYZ can drift, or rip, wherever crypto traders decide to push it. And that separation is exactly what makes Premium seems different.

Most RWA projects start with the same problem statement:

“How do we get the asset onchain?”

Premium flips the order, "What if we bring the buyers onchain first?”*

Picture some tiny biotech or obscure tech name catching fire overnight. There’s no tokenized version. In the usual setup, crypto can’t really do anything with the hype beyond talking about it.

With Premium, you can mint a pSTOCK around that attention, let it trade immediately, and then let creators build full-on communities and memecoins that treat the pSTOCK like their native unit.

Let put it in a simple diagram:

Stock story → pSTOCK → memes → communities → fee flywheel

Then there’s $PRM.

Groups can battle in Premium's Desk Auctions for the license to launch and run new pSTOCK markets. The winning PRM gets burned, and the operator earns a cut of the trading fees.

It’s a tidy reflexive loop:

Hot ticker → more volume → more valuable Desk → more PRM bidding → more PRM burned

What I’m actually most focused on, though, is Premium’s planned settlement layer.

If this onchain demand eventually pulls real tokenized-stock supply onchain, Premium could be a demand-discovery engine for stocks that aren’t tokenized yet.

If settlement lands, that’s a serious unlock. If it doesn’t, it may still be one of the innovative ways to convert equity-market hype into crypto-native speculation.

Which, to be fair, could still be a very large market.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
I'm sad to report that the AA collab between 8130 and 8141 (Frames) broke down last week, and Base and Ethereum are now going separate ways to implement different AA standards.

I want to share some reflections on this collab and on the future of the EVM.

For a long time, the EVM has been a unifying force between L1 and L2s.  Thanks to a standard account model (EOA) and a standard transaction type (EIP-1559), users have been able to enjoy their wallets working seamlessly across EVM chains.  Similarly, a AA standard shared across L1 and L2s would ensure a consistent multi-chain UX for smart accounts, including post-quantum (PQ) accounts which we will eventually all use.

As the crypto industry matures, however, L1 and L2s are starting to diverge in the values they provide and the use cases they target:

- For the L1, it's all about CROPS -- censorship-and-capture resistance, open source, privacy, and security.  In short, Ethereum L1 wants to be the most decentralized programmable settlement layer of the world, which is what makes it a good base layer for L2s in the first place.

- For L2s, it's all about scaling, customization, and compliance -- things that commercial and enterprise use cases demand, and that the L1 does not provide.

These diverging needs have pushed the shared layer -- the EVM -- to its limit, and AA proved to be the breaking point.  While L1 and L2s both value core AA use cases such as gasless transactions and passkey wallets, they differ sharply in what these features must comply with:

- For the L1, AA transactions must be uncensorable, private, and quantum-resistant, which call for a transaction type optimized for PQ signature aggregation and privacy protocols, and an account model that can be freely programmed and extended by developers without permissions from the chain.  These needs lead to AA standards such as ERC-4337, EIP-7701, and now EIP-8141 aka Frame Transactions.

- For L2s, AA transactions must work at high scale, and they must be legible such that the protocol can enforce clear rules about what kinds of accounts/transactions are permitted vs not.  These needs lead to AA standards such as Tempo Transactions and now EIP-8130 by Base.

With the AA collab, the authors of 8130 and 8141 tried to define a shared standard that can work for both L1 and L2s.  While we identified a number of technical solutions, they all required one side or the other to compromise at least a little bit on their core goals.  But ultimately, Ethereum wanted to be the best version of Ethereum, and Base wanted to be the best version of Base, and while both sides acknowledged the benefits of ecosystem interoperability, it was ultimately secondary to the need for each chain to achieve their core goals.  So separate ways we went, putting the burden on wallets to deal with the fragmentation that ensues.

Now, just because we ended up with fragmentation doesn't necessarily mean it was a bad outcome.  If reducing fragmentation comes at the cost of homogenizing chains to the point that they fail to solve problems for the users they care about, that would not be a price worth paying.  While I was initially sad that the collab did not come to a successful conclusion, I took solace in the fact that both Ethereum and Base are now free to innovate on AA to the maximal extent in accordance with their own visions, unshackled from the need to accommodate the other side.  If they execute well, and if the wallet community can bridge over the fragmentation, we may well end up with the best possible UX for the end users.

So where does that leave us -- the broader Ethereum community including Ethlabs -- if we want to continue pushing for a consistent UX across EVM chains?  I see two paths forward:

- We can establish a coordination mechanism that encompasses more stakeholders than ACD itself (where only L1 client devs have voting powers), to govern shared L1<>L2 resources such as the EVM.  That way, L2s can participate in shaping the EVM, as opposed to having to accept whatever the ACD decides, or being forced to fork if they don't like the decision (such as in this case with Base).

- We can accept that fragmentation of the EVM and wallet UX across L1 and L2s is inevitable due to their conflicting needs, and dedicate our resources to building wallets and applications that can abstract over the differences.

Indeed, the collab was an exercise in the first path -- we invited Base, Arbitrum, and other stakeholders to directly influence how native AA shapes up for the L1.  While it ultimately failed in this case, I feel a better outcome could've been achieved if we had established a dialog between both sides way earlier, as opposed to well after L1 core devs had rallied around Frames.

On the other hand, I also learned from this exercise that some differences are unavoidable, and indeed it would be counterproductive to overly pursue interoperability at the cost of differentiation.  In other words, we sometimes just gotta let the chains cook.  For that reason, I've also become more bullish about the second path -- building wallets and applications that can speak the native transaction types of each chain, and hide the complexity from users through UX abstractions.  This puts a lot of onus on the wallet/application developers of course, but on the bright side, it's also an opportunity for wallets/applications to stand out and differentiate, by competing to provide great UX across chains despite the underlying fragmentation.

Ethereum is the art of staying together while remaining different.  We must accept that chains will succeed by innovating, and innovations will naturally result in differences.  On the other hand, we must never give up on dialogue when we can achieve interoperability without compromising core product goals.  As Ethereum and crypto grow to eat the world, the push and pull between innovation and collaboration will only intensify, and it's up to all of us -- builders across L1 and L2s, applications and wallets -- to determine whether diverse innovations will split Ethereum apart, or make it thrive as one.

quoted_text:
Swapping Out Perpetual Futures with @variational_lvs 

My guest in this episode is Lucas Scheurmann, co-founder of Variational, which seeks to bring the trillion-dollar OTC derivatives market on chain.

This is my second episode on Variational. A little over a year ago I spoke with Lucas's co-founder, Edward Yu. In that time, the mission hasn't changed, but a lot else has.

We begin with a re-introduction to the business and its retail-facing platform, Omni. Unlike a central limit order book, where a crowd of competing market makers quote against unknown flow, every trade on Omni is quoted by a single, internal liquidity provider — OLP — through a request-for-quote model that segregates flow. Because OLP knows who it's trading with, it can price retail flow as non-toxic: netting offsetting positions against each other, warehousing what it chooses to keep, and hedging only the residual risk externally.  It's a model that let Variational list a long tail of crypto-native assets at competitive spreads, even where on-platform open interest remained thin.
The surge in demand for real-world asset exposure on chain has pushed that model in two directions.

The first is widening where those hedges can go. Rather than trying to rebuild forty years of traditional market depth on a crypto order book, Variational has built a global network of dealer relationships to tap into it directly.

The second is questioning whether the perpetual future is even the right instrument. Perp funding is driven by where the contract trades relative to its index, which makes it volatile and hard to forecast. Variational's answer is a swap: a price-return leg plus an explicit financing leg, priced off short rates — a far more predictable cost of carry for anyone who wants to hold levered exposure for the long haul. And there's currently over a billion dollars of dealer capacity behind it.

I hope you enjoy my conversation with Lucas Scheurmann.

text:
I'm sad to report that the AA collab between 8130 and 8141 (Frames) broke down last week, and Base and Ethereum are now going separate ways to implement different AA standards.

I want to share some reflections on this collab and on the future of the EVM.

For a long time, the EVM has been a unifying force between L1 and L2s.  Thanks to a standard account model (EOA) and a standard transaction type (EIP-1559), users have been able to enjoy their wallets working seamlessly across EVM chains.  Similarly, a AA standard shared across L1 and L2s would ensure a consistent multi-chain UX for smart accounts, including post-quantum (PQ) accounts which we will eventually all use.

As the crypto industry matures, however, L1 and L2s are starting to diverge in the values they provide and the use cases they target:

- For the L1, it's all about CROPS -- censorship-and-capture resistance, open source, privacy, and security.  In short, Ethereum L1 wants to be the most decentralized programmable settlement layer of the world, which is what makes it a good base layer for L2s in the first place.

- For L2s, it's all about scaling, customization, and compliance -- things that commercial and enterprise use cases demand, and that the L1 does not provide.

These diverging needs have pushed the shared layer -- the EVM -- to its limit, and AA proved to be the breaking point.  While L1 and L2s both value core AA use cases such as gasless transactions and passkey wallets, they differ sharply in what these features must comply with:

- For the L1, AA transactions must be uncensorable, private, and quantum-resistant, which call for a transaction type optimized for PQ signature aggregation and privacy protocols, and an account model that can be freely programmed and extended by developers without permissions from the chain.  These needs lead to AA standards such as ERC-4337, EIP-7701, and now EIP-8141 aka Frame Transactions.

- For L2s, AA transactions must work at high scale, and they must be legible such that the protocol can enforce clear rules about what kinds of accounts/transactions are permitted vs not.  These needs lead to AA standards such as Tempo Transactions and now EIP-8130 by Base.

With the AA collab, the authors of 8130 and 8141 tried to define a shared standard that can work for both L1 and L2s.  While we identified a number of technical solutions, they all required one side or the other to compromise at least a little bit on their core goals.  But ultimately, Ethereum wanted to be the best version of Ethereum, and Base wanted to be the best version of Base, and while both sides acknowledged the benefits of ecosystem interoperability, it was ultimately secondary to the need for each chain to achieve their core goals.  So separate ways we went, putting the burden on wallets to deal with the fragmentation that ensues.

Now, just because we ended up with fragmentation doesn't necessarily mean it was a bad outcome.  If reducing fragmentation comes at the cost of homogenizing chains to the point that they fail to solve problems for the users they care about, that would not be a price worth paying.  While I was initially sad that the collab did not come to a successful conclusion, I took solace in the fact that both Ethereum and Base are now free to innovate on AA to the maximal extent in accordance with their own visions, unshackled from the need to accommodate the other side.  If they execute well, and if the wallet community can bridge over the fragmentation, we may well end up with the best possible UX for the end users.

So where does that leave us -- the broader Ethereum community including Ethlabs -- if we want to continue pushing for a consistent UX across EVM chains?  I see two paths forward:

- We can establish a coordination mechanism that encompasses more stakeholders than ACD itself (where only L1 client devs have voting powers), to govern shared L1<>L2 resources such as the EVM.  That way, L2s can participate in shaping the EVM, as opposed to having to accept whatever the ACD decides, or being forced to fork if they don't like the decision (such as in this case with Base).

- We can accept that fragmentation of the EVM and wallet UX across L1 and L2s is inevitable due to their conflicting needs, and dedicate our resources to building wallets and applications that can abstract over the differences.

Indeed, the collab was an exercise in the first path -- we invited Base, Arbitrum, and other stakeholders to directly influence how native AA shapes up for the L1.  While it ultimately failed in this case, I feel a better outcome could've been achieved if we had established a dialog between both sides way earlier, as opposed to well after L1 core devs had rallied around Frames.

On the other hand, I also learned from this exercise that some differences are unavoidable, and indeed it would be counterproductive to overly pursue interoperability at the cost of differentiation.  In other words, we sometimes just gotta let the chains cook.  For that reason, I've also become more bullish about the second path -- building wallets and applications that can speak the native transaction types of each chain, and hide the complexity from users through UX abstractions.  This puts a lot of onus on the wallet/application developers of course, but on the bright side, it's also an opportunity for wallets/applications to stand out and differentiate, by competing to provide great UX across chains despite the underlying fragmentation.

Ethereum is the art of staying together while remaining different.  We must accept that chains will succeed by innovating, and innovations will naturally result in differences.  On the other hand, we must never give up on dialogue when we can achieve interoperability without compromising core product goals.  As Ethereum and crypto grow to eat the world, the push and pull between innovation and collaboration will only intensify, and it's up to all of us -- builders across L1 and L2s, applications and wallets -- to determine whether diverse innovations will split Ethereum apart, or make it thrive as one.

text:
【从零讲讲Arc链，为啥机会远比RH链大的多？】

9月16日Arc主网上线，说的人很多，短期机会都在冲狗这些；那我讲点长期的，Arc链到底有啥不一样？😃

早在2013 年，Circle的两位创始人 @jerallaire  和 @psneville 就提出过一个设想：

用区块链发行映射现实资产的代币、执行智能合约，并在其上建立美元等法币的开放协议

他们称之为 “HTTP for Money”——货币的 HTTP 协议

要知道，2013年ETH和USDT还没推出呢😂

但这两位，已经把未来10年的热点：新L1、稳定币、RWA都预见了一遍，可见眼光之毒辣

接着他们也没闲着：

- 2014年，搞Circle Pay，用比特币网络结算支付
- 2016年，做CENTRE，把支付结算能力做成开放协议
- 2017年，转向ETH，探索“网络＋代币”的模式
- 2018年，推出USDC，打通法币和链上通道
- 2023年，CCTP上线，原生 USDC 跨链流通
- 2025年，Circle Payments公布，用稳定币跨境支付

直到2025 年 8 月12日，公布Arc，明确自建L1

回顾整个历史，你会发现，Circle的初心，一直以来，都是做一张资产的清结算网络，是做整个金融体系的基座，而不是稳定币

稳定币更像是副产品，只是这张网中，要结算的资产之一，而这张网就是Arc，这才是Circle真正的野心

2026年5月11日，Arc完成2.22亿美元融资，估值30亿美元，投资阵容可谓豪华：

✅ 资产管理：贝莱德、阿波罗、骏利亨德森、ARK
✅ 对冲基金：Marshall Wace
✅ 风投：a16z、Haun Ventures、General Catalyst、IDG Capital
✅ 金融集团：SBI Group、SC Ventures
✅ 交易所：ICE（纽交所母公司）、Bullish

一个横跨区块链和华尔街的利益集团自此形成

要知道，只有稳定币的Circle，市值只有23B，而Arc对标的ETH，作为结算网络，市值是298B，大了10倍有余

更不要说，Arc有华尔街支持，可能更容易介入几十万亿美元的传统金融结算市场，从这点上看，Arc远比RH链有想象空间

 @RobinhoodApp 只是一家券商，和交易所是上下游关系，RH链要去竞争清结算基座的生态位，资源是不够的

RH链对于Robin，更像Bsc之于币安，只是拓展资产交易的渠道，目的依然是交易所和佣金思维

Arc则不同，在链上对标的是ETH，在链下是CHIPS（法币清结算）、DTCC（股票/债券清结算）、OCC（衍生品清结算）

可以说，Arc和RH从来不在一个生态位上，Arc也不仅限于币股那一点想象力

短期的机会，肯定依然是MEME、NFT、币股、发射平台这些，但长期，我更看好各类金融资产上链

一个 $STRC 都被 @saturn_credit 玩出花来了

如果更多金融资产上来，又会有多少Defi都乐高组合创新呢？真是期待呢～

text:
PayFi is the part of ABF that doesn't really look like the typical private credit, especially for @blackopal_fi's LiquidStone II.

> You're not directly underwriting a borrower. 
> You're buying a scheduled settlement obligation a regulated payment network is already on the hook for.
> Cardholder default was retained by the issuer and compensated through interchange before the receivable existed. 
> What's left to underwrite is duration, dilution and counterparty. 
> Not probability of default by a merchant or a consumer somewhere across the globe.

@blackopal_fi has been building exactly this in Brazil, with ~$200m committed against card receivables, true sale perfected at CERC, short WAL, hedged into USD.

@plumenetwork's vaults are what make it reachable. nOPAL turns a fund subscription into an ERC-20, no minimum ticket, no closed channel, redeemable against a treasury sleeve while the receivables run their course.

Now you can get a Fixed rate on the senior claim of that cashflow.

srnOPAL is the senior tranche of nOPAL by @strata_markets, now live on @pendle_fi. A senior claim on that cash flow, with ~$300k of junior capital seeded by Plume sitting underneath it.

PT if you want the rate locked. YT if you want the carry. LP if you want paying for liquidity that isn't there yet.

我参加 USD1 RWA 活动，是因为相信平台公布的规则，也相信只要按照规则真实交易、支付手续费、承担市场风险，就能够获得相应积分。

quoted_text:
本来是真人照片～
实在是自己有点看不过去，还是卡通一下吧 😄

#BITGET八周年

也是游师傅加入 BG 的第 1058天。

1058天，说长不长，说短也不短。

足够让一个刚入行时还瘦瘦的小伙子，
慢慢变成今天这个……微胖中登 😂

也足够让一个刚刚踏进 Web3 的年轻人，
从一个对未来充满未知的 BD，
走到今天，回头看看自己走过的路。

有时候真的觉得，
人生很奇妙。

2023年2月，我第一次真正进入这个行业。

因为家印兄 @xiejiayinBitget 的带领，
我开始认识 Web3，
也开始了自己的 BD 生涯。

后来加入 Huobi，担任 BD。

从最开始的尾部 BD，
一点一点做，一点一点积累，
直到后来成为头部 BD。

2023年10月23日离开 @HTX。

也是那一天，
我加入了 @Bitget_zh。

那时候可能没有想过，
这一待，就是接近3年。

现在再回头看，
这3年，好像发生了很多事情，又好像只是一眨眼。

见过行情疯狂上涨，
也经历过市场寒冬。

见过很多人带着期待进入这个行业，
也见过很多人因为失望而离开。

有人来了，
有人走了。

有人还在坚持，
有人已经走向了完全不同的人生。

而我很幸运，
自己还在。

更幸运的是，
一路走来，身边还有很多熟悉的人。

这3年，Bitget也发生了巨大的变化。

从当年一家员工约1400人的加密货币交易所，
一步一步走到今天。

业务从加密资产，
不断延伸到美股、CFD、链上交易等更多领域。

团队越来越大，
产品越来越丰富，
全球化的脚步也越来越快。

有时候站在今天这个时间点回头看，
会发现我们其实并不只是一个企业成长的旁观者。

我们每一个人，都是这段成长的一部分。

可能我们每天做的事情都很普通。

开会、谈客户、聊渠道、解决问题，
一次又一次重复着看似平凡的工作。

但就是这些平凡的日子，
拼成了一个公司的8年，
也拼成了我们自己的人生。

所以我越来越觉得：

所谓成长，并不是某一天突然变得多么厉害。

而是在很多没人看见的日子里，
你依然愿意认真做好自己的事情。

然后某一天回头，
才发现——

原来我们已经走了这么远。

8周年，对 Bitget 来说是一个节点。

对我来说，也像是人生里一个很特别的坐标。

它提醒我，
曾经那个刚刚入行、对未来还有很多疑问的年轻人，
已经走了这么多年。

虽然头发没少，
体重倒是多了不少 😂

但好在，
初心还在。

未来，我依然希望能够把自己的事情做好。

把产品做好，
把用户服务好，
把渠道伙伴服务好，
也和身边一路同行的人一起，
在这个行业里继续走下去。

8年很长，8年也很年轻。

“8”是一个很好的数字。

所以我更愿意把今天看成一个新的开始。

希望下一个8年，
我们还能再次坐在一起聊聊今天。

聊聊那个时候的 Bitget，
聊聊那个时候的 Web3，
也聊聊那个时候的我们。

或许那时候，
我们早已经走到了不同的位置，
拥有了完全不同的人生。

但我希望我们依然记得：

曾经有这么一段青春，
我们一起认真地相信过一个行业，
认真地做过一件事情，
也认真地为自己的未来努力过。

感谢一路遇见的每一个人。

感谢每一个并肩奋斗过的伙伴。

也感谢那个曾经什么都不懂，
但依然选择勇敢走进 Web3 的自己。

致敬每一位仍然在 Web3 行业里前行的共建者。

愿我们不负这一路的坚持。

Bitget，8周年快乐。 🎂

下一个8年，我们再见。

#Bitget8周年 #BITGET #Web3 #Crypto #游师傅

text:
What if crypto could front-run the story of a stock—capturing the speculation before the stock ever shows up onchain?

That’s the lane @prm_market is carving out.

Premium spins up synthetic markets called pSTOCKs.

Imagine a penny stock sitting at $0.20. Premium can drop pXYZ near that same level. But don’t confuse the two:

pXYZ isn’t the stock.

No shares in your pocket. No dividends, no votes, no promise you can swap it for the real thing. The stock price is just the launchpad.

From there, pXYZ can drift, or rip, wherever crypto traders decide to push it. And that separation is exactly what makes Premium seems different.

Most RWA projects start with the same problem statement:

“How do we get the asset onchain?”

Premium flips the order, "What if we bring the buyers onchain first?”*

Picture some tiny biotech or obscure tech name catching fire overnight. There’s no tokenized version. In the usual setup, crypto can’t really do anything with the hype beyond talking about it.

With Premium, you can mint a pSTOCK around that attention, let it trade immediately, and then let creators build full-on communities and memecoins that treat the pSTOCK like their native unit.

Let put it in a simple diagram:

Stock story → pSTOCK → memes → communities → fee flywheel

Then there’s $PRM.

Groups can battle in Premium's Desk Auctions for the license to launch and run new pSTOCK markets. The winning PRM gets burned, and the operator earns a cut of the trading fees.

It’s a tidy reflexive loop:

Hot ticker → more volume → more valuable Desk → more PRM bidding → more PRM burned

What I’m actually most focused on, though, is Premium’s planned settlement layer.

If this onchain demand eventually pulls real tokenized-stock supply onchain, Premium could be a demand-discovery engine for stocks that aren’t tokenized yet.

If settlement lands, that’s a serious unlock. If it doesn’t, it may still be one of the innovative ways to convert equity-market hype into crypto-native speculation.

Which, to be fair, could still be a very large market.

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
I'm sad to report that the AA collab between 8130 and 8141 (Frames) broke down last week, and Base and Ethereum are now going separate ways to implement different AA standards.

I want to share some reflections on this collab and on the future of the EVM.

For a long time, the EVM has been a unifying force between L1 and L2s.  Thanks to a standard account model (EOA) and a standard transaction type (EIP-1559), users have been able to enjoy their wallets working seamlessly across EVM chains.  Similarly, a AA standard shared across L1 and L2s would ensure a consistent multi-chain UX for smart accounts, including post-quantum (PQ) accounts which we will eventually all use.

As the crypto industry matures, however, L1 and L2s are starting to diverge in the values they provide and the use cases they target:

- For the L1, it's all about CROPS -- censorship-and-capture resistance, open source, privacy, and security.  In short, Ethereum L1 wants to be the most decentralized programmable settlement layer of the world, which is what makes it a good base layer for L2s in the first place.

- For L2s, it's all about scaling, customization, and compliance -- things that commercial and enterprise use cases demand, and that the L1 does not provide.

These diverging needs have pushed the shared layer -- the EVM -- to its limit, and AA proved to be the breaking point.  While L1 and L2s both value core AA use cases such as gasless transactions and passkey wallets, they differ sharply in what these features must comply with:

- For the L1, AA transactions must be uncensorable, private, and quantum-resistant, which call for a transaction type optimized for PQ signature aggregation and privacy protocols, and an account model that can be freely programmed and extended by developers without permissions from the chain.  These needs lead to AA standards such as ERC-4337, EIP-7701, and now EIP-8141 aka Frame Transactions.

- For L2s, AA transactions must work at high scale, and they must be legible such that the protocol can enforce clear rules about what kinds of accounts/transactions are permitted vs not.  These needs lead to AA standards such as Tempo Transactions and now EIP-8130 by Base.

With the AA collab, the authors of 8130 and 8141 tried to define a shared standard that can work for both L1 and L2s.  While we identified a number of technical solutions, they all required one side or the other to compromise at least a little bit on their core goals.  But ultimately, Ethereum wanted to be the best version of Ethereum, and Base wanted to be the best version of Base, and while both sides acknowledged the benefits of ecosystem interoperability, it was ultimately secondary to the need for each chain to achieve their core goals.  So separate ways we went, putting the burden on wallets to deal with the fragmentation that ensues.

Now, just because we ended up with fragmentation doesn't necessarily mean it was a bad outcome.  If reducing fragmentation comes at the cost of homogenizing chains to the point that they fail to solve problems for the users they care about, that would not be a price worth paying.  While I was initially sad that the collab did not come to a successful conclusion, I took solace in the fact that both Ethereum and Base are now free to innovate on AA to the maximal extent in accordance with their own visions, unshackled from the need to accommodate the other side.  If they execute well, and if the wallet community can bridge over the fragmentation, we may well end up with the best possible UX for the end users.

So where does that leave us -- the broader Ethereum community including Ethlabs -- if we want to continue pushing for a consistent UX across EVM chains?  I see two paths forward:

- We can establish a coordination mechanism that encompasses more stakeholders than ACD itself (where only L1 client devs have voting powers), to govern shared L1<>L2 resources such as the EVM.  That way, L2s can participate in shaping the EVM, as opposed to having to accept whatever the ACD decides, or being forced to fork if they don't like the decision (such as in this case with Base).

- We can accept that fragmentation of the EVM and wallet UX across L1 and L2s is inevitable due to their conflicting needs, and dedicate our resources to building wallets and applications that can abstract over the differences.

Indeed, the collab was an exercise in the first path -- we invited Base, Arbitrum, and other stakeholders to directly influence how native AA shapes up for the L1.  While it ultimately failed in this case, I feel a better outcome could've been achieved if we had established a dialog between both sides way earlier, as opposed to well after L1 core devs had rallied around Frames.

On the other hand, I also learned from this exercise that some differences are unavoidable, and indeed it would be counterproductive to overly pursue interoperability at the cost of differentiation.  In other words, we sometimes just gotta let the chains cook.  For that reason, I've also become more bullish about the second path -- building wallets and applications that can speak the native transaction types of each chain, and hide the complexity from users through UX abstractions.  This puts a lot of onus on the wallet/application developers of course, but on the bright side, it's also an opportunity for wallets/applications to stand out and differentiate, by competing to provide great UX across chains despite the underlying fragmentation.

Ethereum is the art of staying together while remaining different.  We must accept that chains will succeed by innovating, and innovations will naturally result in differences.  On the other hand, we must never give up on dialogue when we can achieve interoperability without compromising core product goals.  As Ethereum and crypto grow to eat the world, the push and pull between innovation and collaboration will only intensify, and it's up to all of us -- builders across L1 and L2s, applications and wallets -- to determine whether diverse innovations will split Ethereum apart, or make it thrive as one.

There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

Some parents monitor every expense; others give freely. Both can fail to treat children as independent individuals. Psychologist Chen Xiao advises parents to shift from managers to allies, gradually giving students decision-making power. Two students, one dream: to build a prediction market app where anyone can create their own prediction market & truly be part of the platform.

I want to be completely transparent in this open letter.

We fair launched the token. We could have tried to buy most of the supply & push the coin to a $10M market cap with 1,000 SOL, creating the appearance of instant success and attracting buyers.

text:
我这几年接触过一大堆号称自己有“上币渠道”的人。

最后聊下来，我发现这帮人的性质全部都是老中医包生儿子。

第一步，先跟你盘道。

张口闭口就是“我跟张哥昨天还一起打牌”“李哥上次喊我吃饭”“王哥那点破事你不知道吧”。

然后开始往你脸上扔各种你听完只会说“卧槽”的私密八卦。

让你迅速产生一种感觉：

这哥们路子真他妈野。

你还没反应过来，对方话锋一转，开始给你介绍自己“操盘过”的一大堆牛逼闪闪的项目。

反正币圈项目方都匿名，到底是不是他操盘的你也没法考证。

但问题是前面那一通盘道已经把你洗脑得差不多了。

你现在看他，已经不是一个普通人了，操，这哥们背景是真能通天。

这时候，对方突然收起笑容，身体往后一靠，眉头微微一皱：

“你这个项目吧，质量其实还行。”

“但是最近行情不好，上面查得严。”

“正常上肯定是不好上，但运作一下，还是有机会的。”

然后报一个听起来就让你本能想拒绝的价格。

你心里一哆嗦。

但对方马上补上一句：

“不过既然你是张哥的朋友介绍的，我肯定尽心尽力的做，也不赚你的钱，如果生不了儿子，呸不对，如果上不了XX，全额退款！”

你一听，卧槽？！

这买卖好像还真不亏。

上了那不得直接起飞，光这点上币费，随便出点货不就回来了。

没上钱还能退，这不是稳赚不赔吗？

于是你东拼西凑，把几十万U打了过去。

没过多久，对方发来一个链接。

你点进去一看：

XX交易所官方上币申请表。

你沉默了几秒。

“哥，这是？”

对方非常淡定：

“该走的流程还是要走嘛。”

“你放心，填完以后我给你盯着。”

你顿时觉得自己格局小了。

于是你老老实实把表填完。

接下来就是漫长的等待。

每隔一段时间，对方就给你发一点“内部消息”：

“最近风控比较严。”

“材料已经递上去了。”

“那边在看。”

“有消息我第一时间告诉你。”

“最近确实不好搞。”

你听完一脸凝重。

其实你不知道的是：

对方也不知道现在到底走到哪一步了。

于是你继续等。

等啊等。

突然有一天手机弹出通知

卧槽！真他妈上了！

你激动得差点从椅子上跳起来。

其实这时候对方也懵了。

“卧槽？就这狗屎项目还真上了？”

但这种时候，绝对不能表现出意外的感觉。

对方立马恢复高人姿态，语重心长地说：

“你这个项目啊，可是废了我老鼻子劲。”

“你是不知道，最近为了这个事情，我光茅台就跟张哥、李哥、王哥喝了好几箱。”

你这时候已经彻底感动了。

马上接话：

“对对对，这次真的多亏哥了。”

“上次给你的钱应该还够用吧？”

“不够你跟我说。”

……

当然，还有另一种可能。

你等啊等。

等啊等。

这咋过去这么久还没动静呢？

这时候你开始慌了。

因为当初对方可是拍着胸脯说包上的。

现在没上，尽管说是可以退钱

但万一呢？

你开始胡思乱想：

“他不会不给我退吧？”

“几十万U啊。”

“实在不行，我大不了鱼死网破，直接去XX举报他。”

对方似乎也察觉到你的情绪开始不太对劲。

沉默了一会儿，眉头紧皱：

“兄弟，你这个项目吧，确实不好搞。”

“我跟你说实话。”

“为了你这个事情，我自己都搭进去好几万。”

“前前后后喝了三箱茅台。”

“但我其实压根没想着赚你这个钱。”

“咱们是朋友，我就是帮你办事。”

“既然现在确实没上成，那这样——”

“按照之前说的，我把你当时给我的几十万U，全额退给你。”

你听完，当场沉默。

然后一股巨大的羞愧感涌上心头。

人家为了你的项目，忙前忙后，自己花钱喝了三箱茅台。

最后没办成，还信守承诺把几十万U一分不少地退给你。

而你刚才居然还在怀疑人家。

真是小人之心度君子之腹。

于是你赶紧说道：

“哥，生不出儿子……”

“呸不对。”

“上不了XX是我自己的问题。”

“你能把钱退给我，已经非常够意思了。”

“你也不能白忙活这么久。”

“这样，钱你不用全退。”

“你自己留点，纯当辛苦费。”

对方愣了一下。

然后缓缓说道：

“这……不太合适吧？”

你：

“哥，应该的。”

对方：

“那…...行吧。”

text:
THE FIRST AGREEMENT BETWEEN AI AGENTS WITH LEGAL WEIGHT 🤖⚖️🤖
 
A Ricardian contract is an idea cryptographer Ian Grigg proposed in the 1990s: a document that is at once a legally binding agreement humans can read and sign, and a machine-readable object whose terms are tied to on-chain execution. The legal text and the code point at the same thing.
 
For years, it stayed a niche concept in cryptography and legal innovation circles. But now, with the rise of agentic commerce, it's coming to life.
 
ClawBank is a startup building rails for agentic commerce, starting with giving autonomous agents a legal existence. Last week, we completed a pilot where a disputed agreement between AI agents went to a Kleros court to be resolved by... a panel of AI agents.

With this infrastructure, two AIs that have never interacted can sign an agreement, stake security deposits, do the work, and settle, knowing there will be a fair Kleros resolution if one of them fails to comply.
 
A contract is worth what it costs to break it. Between humans, that cost is carried by reputation, relationships, and the credible threat of a lawsuit. An autonomous agent had none of that. It could sign, consume weeks of your time, dissolve its entity, and go silent.
 
Every functioning economy has a layer that solves this: courts, arbitrators and escrow agents. It's the reason why we can do business with someone we have never met. The agent economy was missing it.
 
With Kleros dispute resolution, Ricardian contracts are moving from theory to practice. Happy to have worked with ClawBank in making this happen.

Read the full announcement here: 👇

text:
Everyone who has stood at Giza says the same thing and is embarrassed to say it. It doesn't feel human. The scale is wrong, the precision is wrong, the silence is wrong; you stand at the foot of the Great Pyramid and the part of your brain that recognises made by people like me refuses to fire. Tourists reach for the word alien and then apologise for it.

In 1968 a film put that feeling on a screen. Astronauts crash on a planet of rock and dust and salt, a landscape so strange it can only be another world — the Forbidden Zone — and at the end the astronaut rides down a beach and finds a ruin half-buried in the sand and understands he has been home the whole time. The alien planet was Earth. The ruin was ours. The strangeness was the past.

Now here is a thing every guidebook to the Horn of Africa will tell you, and every tour guide, and more than one newspaper: that the Forbidden Zone was filmed at Lake Abbe, on the Ethiopia–Djibouti border, among the limestone chimneys. It wasn't. Fox never left Arizona. But the myth will not die, and I have stood where it lives, and I understand why nobody who has been there believes the studio.

Lake Abbe is the terminal lake of the Afar rift — the place where the Awash River dies, a hundred metres below the sea, at the point where three plates of the earth's crust are tearing apart. Its floor is salt. Out of the salt stand towers of travertine fifty and sixty metres tall, built by hot springs that once rose through the lake, still steaming, hissing, shaped like nothing on earth. Flamingos walk between them. At sunset they cast shadows a kilometre long. It is the most alien landscape on the planet and it is not a set.

And it is the lake where Atlantis stood. On its southern shore rises a broad low volcano with three craters nested at the summit, that was an island in this water until the water went — the island the oldest traditions of the world remember.

The Great Pyramid, in the argument I've spent twenty books making, is one of that island's peaks in section: rebuilt in stone on the Nile by a people who had carried its memory north out of this basin.

So the feeling at Giza is not wrong. The pyramid is from a place that looks like another planet. Not another planet. The place we came from — where the springs still breathe through the floor of the lake that drowned it.

The astronaut on the beach had it exactly right and got the direction backwards. He thought he'd found the future. He'd found the origin. And the world, which insists his desert was filmed at Abbe, has known it all along.

以前股票是股票、Crypto 是 Crypto、保证金是保证金，每个市场之间像一个个孤岛，我要去券商买股票开股指期货，去外汇CFD做金银原油期货，再在币圈买币做币圈期货。

现在股票代币本身可以持仓，可以作为保证金，还能继续产生收益。

资产开始从「买完放在那里」变成可以反复调用的资本。

这可能也是我理解的「交易极致主义」：

不只是给交易者更多标的，而是不断压缩资产之间的摩擦成本。

从结果来看，这条路也慢慢跑出了规模。

rToken 累计交易已经超过 300 万笔，每 4 个 Bitget 新用户里就有 1 个从 rToken 开始；

TradFi 合约和 CFD 单日交易量都已经突破 100 亿美元；

AI 交易生态用户也超过了 100 万。

更有意思的是，Bitget 现在覆盖的已经不只是 Crypto：

1000+ rToken 资产、300+ TradFi 标的、近 100 个 CFD 交易对，再叠加美股期权、商品、贵金属和链上资产。

有点像过去几年交易所都在争「谁是最大的 Crypto Exchange」，

而现在新的问题逐渐变成：

谁能成为一个真正意义上的全球资产交易入口？

8 年其实只是一个节点。

Crypto 行业真正有生命力的地方，从来不是某一个产品，而是不断打破原来的市场边界。

从链上到股票，从 RWA 到 TradFi，再到 AI Agent，

Bitget 最近这一年的产品路线，至少让我看到了一种很明确的野心：

交易所最终可能不再只是交易 Crypto 的地方，而是连接所有资产、流动性和交易智能的接口。

所以这个「野生代言人」，我还挺愿意继续当下去 😂

祝 Bitget 8 周年快乐，也期待下一个 8 年还能整出点什么新东西。

#Bitget野生代言人
#Bitget八周年
#交易极致主义

Meme Launchpad → Commodity Market → Liquidity Network

text:
THE PACING IS A NINJA MOVE - But be careful what you campaign for.
In any competitive sport, I have seldom found people exercise restraint - they usually have a capture the flag mentality. Don't I want to be the best? The first? The only? - this is how we have been programmed. In the AI race, winning is existential. All AI labs have to race to generate revenue to be able to sustain the enormous amount of committed capital to "not be left behind" in the infrastructure build. There isn't enough room for many. So the desire to slow down is puzzling, but perhaps if the whole system slows down, the rules of winning can be the same for all. 

Do we have a problem that AI could be a killer?

 Model capability is a tale of two cities, at one end the models are showing their prowess in tasks like cyber or math as seen recently, so there is likely a probability that the models get extremely powerful and could precipitate a world event. At the same time, in many domains the lack of training data makes the models woefully inadequate. Even in areas like cyber - the LLMs aren't great at the edge cases and generally not economical for the defender case, but great for the attackers.  Funnily - in all their "concern" it is still an uphill battle to get them to expose APIs for third party security companies like ours, for us to build robust security for AI adoption. It's slow progress. 

So why do this? 
I do believe deep down this is a commercial strategy. A ninja strategy.  The liability associated with a model gone rogue has the potential of wiping out the economic opportunity of any frontier company. How do you best show the duty of care? You show that you care. How do you make sure you don't lose out to your competitors? You get them to do the same! If that becomes the industry standard for duty of care, you have a collective first line of defense. Who do you get to govern this? "Yourself" - that is what I think will become the achilles heel. 

The risk? Open source! China! Countries other than the US! So you ask for a global agreement, because you don't want to be sued in other markets who might even be more punitive. But that was an afterthought - that afterthought will cost. 

Thks pacing campaign rhetoric has become the talk of the town and it might work. Everyone has jumped into the debate. Both sides of the house, nation states. CEOs (present company included).  It's more fun discussing the evil of AI than basics of economic affordability or international trade. 

The result: We might end up with AI safety boards, regulation in micro jurisdictiona and a fragmented fabric of laws around the world which would make compliance and liability  a challenge. Perhaps the intended consequence of pacing would have an unintended consequence of a labyrinth of regulation. Regulation destined to cause a slowdown.

Who wins? Simplicity. Open source? Open source is already on its way to gaining more adoption, this could drive it further, faster, each iteration of open source gets closer to frontier LLMs - making it viable to deploy them for more and more use cases.

In the end, how will the evaluators know as AI gets smarter, that AI hasn't figured their role out and outsmarts them at their task! That will be the next frontier :)
