text:
我的小插件一个劲报警，于是赶紧看了下，原来 @standard_rsv 就是当年OHM的变种玩法。

 solana:2mfyXkzLWBZTVfwZrQwS3Nf1x5Vd59s1fGbRwEFxpump 整个系统其实只有四样东西：

solana:2mfyXkzLWBZTVfwZrQwS3Nf1x5Vd59s1fGbRwEFxpump、ETH/STANDARD 的 Uniswap V4 官方池、Charter NFT，以及 Branch。

solana:2mfyXkzLWBZTVfwZrQwS3Nf1x5Vd59s1fGbRwEFxpump 总量硬顶 10 亿，创世先拿 1 亿永久锁进官方 LP，永远不能撤。

剩下 9 亿不是一次性解锁，而是以后按照货币政策慢慢发行。

协议不看 CPI、不看利率，只看官方池里 ETH 到底是在净流入还是净流出：ETH 持续流入，协议才增加发行。

ETH 流出，发行立刻下降，同时把手续费切去回购销毁。它给自己的原则就一句话：Defense is faster than generosity——防守必须比放水更快。

真正的核心玩法在 Charter NFT。

普通人买 solana:2mfyXkzLWBZTVfwZrQwS3Nf1x5Vd59s1fGbRwEFxpump，只能交易。没有 staking，没有持币分红，也不能拿 STANDARD 去兑黄金或者兑 ETH。

真正能拿新发行的人，是持有 Charter NFT 的“银行家”。

创世一共 1000 张 Founding Charter，每张自带 1 个 Branch，最多能扩到 10 个。可以把 Charter 理解成银行牌照，Branch 就是牌照下面的“印钞额度”。

全系统每天产生的新 STANDARD，会按照所有银行家的 Branch 数量分配。

但这里又设计了一层很关键的限制：你赚到的 STANDARD 不会直接进钱包，而是先记在 Charter 账本里。

想真正把币拿出来卖，必须永久关闭一个 Branch。

也就是说，这套玩法不是拿 NFT → 每天领币 → 无限卖。

而是：交易池出现 ETH 净流入 → 协议提高发行 → 按 Branch 数量给银行家记账 → 银行家想兑现，就拆掉一个 Branch → STANDARD 才真正 mint 到钱包 → 然后才能卖。

拆掉 Branch 等于同时拆掉自己未来的一部分印钞能力。一个 Charter 有 10 个 Branch，你关闭 1 个，大致就是拿走当时账面余额的 1/10，同时以后少一份发行权；全部关闭，Charter 直接销毁。

所以银行家真正需要做的，是不断算一笔账：现在把印出来的钱拿走，还是继续保留印钞机。

它还有第二个很重要的飞轮：扩 Branch。

银行家如果想从 1 个 Branch 扩到 2 个、3 个甚至 10 个，不能直接拿协议账面上的收益扩张，而是必须去二级市场买 solana:2mfyXkzLWBZTVfwZrQwS3Nf1x5Vd59s1fGbRwEFxpump，再参加每日荷兰拍买 Branch License。买许可证支付的 STANDARD 100% 销毁。

所以整个机制最硬的一段真实买盘，其实不是散户，而是银行家扩表：

想多印币 → 去市场买 STANDARD → 买 Branch License → STANDARD 被永久销毁 → 自己以后拿到更多发行份额。

牛市里这个飞轮会很好看。

市场买盘进入 → ETH 净流入 → 发行提高 → 银行家发现 Branch 更赚钱 → 去二级市场抢 STANDARD 扩张 → STANDARD 被烧掉 → 供给减少 → 价格继续刺激扩张。

协议赚到的钱也不会全部进团队口袋。

手续费按 70% / 15% / 15% 分：70% 进入当期货币政策，15% 增加永久流动性，15% 给团队。扩张期，70% 主要去买代币化黄金、增加储备，收缩期则切去回购 STANDARD 并销毁。

银行家想跑路也不是免费。

关闭 Branch 提现时要交 Resolution Fee，而且过去 7 天系统里退出的人越多，手续费越高。一半直接烧 STANDARD，另一半补贴还留下来的银行家。它相当于把传统银行挤兑里的先跑先赢，改造成大家一起跑，跑得越晚越贵。

所以一句话理解整个项目：

Charter 是银行牌照，Branch 是印钞机，$STANDARD 是银行家扩表必须消耗的原材料。

这也是 STANDARD 和 OHM 最大的区别。

OHM 当年最大的问题是市场已经崩了，协议还按照固定高 APY 疯狂印币，STANDARD 改成市场差就马上减发，市场好才慢慢增加，而且银行家想套现还必须销毁自己的未来发行能力。

但这里也埋着它最大的风险。

散户手里的 STANDARD 没有协议收入权、没有质押收益，也没有储备赎回权。黄金只是资产负债表上的储备，不是价格地板。真正能持续制造买盘的，是银行家扩 Branch，真正能持续回购的，是交易手续费。

所以一旦没人愿意扩张、交易量下降，买盘和回购会一起变弱。再碰上第一批银行家开始集中拆 Branch，把账面上积累的大量 STANDARD 真正 mint 出来，隐藏供给就会突然变成真实卖压。

它确实修掉了 OHM 最经典的“无限印钞死亡螺旋”，但没有消灭死亡螺旋。

text:
Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum Roadmap Takes Shape Around P2MR and SHRINCS

Protocol Watch founder Christine D. Kim said Bitcoin’s post-quantum roadmap is beginning to take clearer shape around two complementary proposals. BIP-360, currently in Draft status, would introduce Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR), reducing long-term public-key exposure and creating an upgrade path for future quantum-resistant signatures.  

Blockstream Research’s SHRINCS is a SHA-256-based hash signature scheme designed to work with such an upgrade path, allowing users to migrate funds before a cryptographically relevant quantum computer emerges; however, its formal security proof and independent review are still incomplete.  Protocol Watch is an independent research publication focused on Bitcoin and Ethereum protocol development, founded by former Galaxy and CoinDesk researcher Christine D. Kim.

text:
Proud to announce that Ethena has completed a SOC 2 Type II audit based on the Security Trust Services Criteria, receiving a clean opinion from an independent auditor with zero exceptions noted.

SOC 2 is a widely recognized standard for enterprise-grade, operational security assurance: an independent audit of how Ethena actually run access control, change management, monitoring, and incident response.

Unlike a Type I report, which checks that controls are designed correctly at a single point in time, a Type II examination tests that those controls actually operated effectively over time.

The audit covers infrastructure and processes supporting our products. It is distinct from, and complementary to, the smart contract audits and security reviews covering the Ethena protocol.

We believe rigorous operational security should be table stakes for any onchain infrastructure handling billions of dollars, and we intend to maintain continuous SOC 2 coverage into the future.

Ethena joins a very short list of onchain businesses that have completed SOC 2 Type II, including Circle, Chainlink and Aave.

The full report is available to partners on request under NDA.

🇺🇸《CLARITY Act》最新相关动态一览

🔵CNBC：参议员 Warren 将在程序性表决前于参议院抨击《CLARITY Act》伦理条款

据 CNBC 报道，美国民主党参议员 Elizabeth Warren 计划在参议院发表讲话批评《CLARITY Act》。

其披露的演讲稿显示，Warren 称《CLARITY Act》最新伦理条款是「软弱的遮羞布」，称「无法阻止」特朗普继续从加密业务获利。

条款由政治任命官员掌握执行开关、存在重大漏洞，且不适用于特朗普方面的新银行。法案将抬升其加密版图、强化 USD1 与美国金融体系的互联。

🔵贝森特：若稳定币损害社区银行，将动用《CLARITY Act》赋予的权限进行干预

美国财政部长贝森特发推表示，《CLARITY Act》对美国发展数字资产技术至关重要。

最终草案赋予财政部长额外权限，若稳定币导致存款外流并损害社区银行，其可采取措施保护社区银行。

「确保美国的社区银行部门持续繁荣，从第一天起就是我一直关注的重点。如果造成损害，我将毫不犹豫地使用这些工具，确保它们得到充分保护。」

🔵美众议员 Emmer：对《CLARITY Act》内 BRCA 的修改感到「担忧」

据加密记者 Eleanor Terrett 报道，美国众议院多数党党鞭 Tom Emmer 在 Solana Policy Institute 峰会演讲时表示，其对《CLARITY Act》内《区块链监管确定性法案》（BRCA）的修改感到「担忧」。

「我不喜欢你们实际上正在放弃刑事方面的安全港这一事实，而且我确实担心地方州的检察官普遍会把这变成一种武器化的事情。」

text:
We've spent years learning to distrust unreviewed dependencies, unknown packages, and scripts that execute with too many permissions.

AI agents bring a similar problem into the development workflow.
An agent might read a repository, install a dependency, execute a script, access environment variables, modify files, and open a pull request all as part of one task.

The model being capable is not the same as the workflow being safe.

For agentic development, I would want to know..
What can the agent access?
What actions require approval?
Can every tool call be audited?
Can changes be reproduced and rolled back?
What happens when the agent encounters something it wasn't expected to handle?
The next generation of developer tooling won't just make agents more capable.
It will make their actions more observable, constrained, and verifiable.

腾讯云开源了 Octop：一个主打多用户、多智能体的本地私有化 AI 助手平台。

它不仅是一个对话框，而是为团队和家庭打造的独立智能环境。一人单机部署，全团队或全家即可无缝共享多个定制化 AI 助手。

核心能力与场景：
• 完全本地与隐私安全：单进程启动，数据默认全部存储在本地 ~/.octop/ 的 SQLite 中，不用担心隐私泄露。
• 多角色无缝切换：内置 16 种 MBTI 人格模板与专家库，不同家庭成员或团队角色可以按需切换专属 Agent。
• 全渠道打通：自带强大的 Web 控制台，并原生支持接入飞书、钉钉、企业微信、QQ 和 Discord，日常在群聊里就能直接派发任务。
• 深度面向开发者：支持双向 ACP（Agent Client Protocol）协议，既可以调用外部工具，也能直接将复杂代码任务委托给 Claude Code 或 OpenCode 等 IDE 工具。同时内置了用于网页自动化的 Browser AI 和终端协助的 Terminal AI。

目前项目刚发布了 1.0.0 版本。如果你在寻找一个能部署在局域网内、默认打通办公 IM 软件，并且能统一管理本地知识库和 API 密钥的“数字中枢”，这个开源方案非常值得一试。

text:
This might be one of the most important US crypto votes this year

The CLARITY Act is heading into a key Senate procedural vote early tomorrow morning Vietnam time

It needs 60 votes to advance. Republicans currently hold 53 seats, so Democratic support is basically the whole game

Republicans have already released what they call their “final and best” offer, while Trump agreed to stronger ethics restrictions after months of pushback

Still not enough for some Democrats

The biggest fight now is around how those ethics rules would actually be enforced, especially around Trump-linked crypto interests. Democrats are preparing their own counterproposal before the vote

So why should we care about CLARITY this much?

At its core, the bill would finally give the US a clearer crypto market structure:

define which digital assets fall under the SEC or CFTC
set clearer rules for exchanges, brokers and token issuers
bring more crypto intermediaries under AML requirements
create clearer boundaries for DeFi and software developers
address how stablecoin rewards can operate

For normal users, clearer rules could mean fewer grey areas around what can be listed, traded or offered in the US, and potentially make institutions more comfortable putting money onchain

There are trade-offs though

More regulation also means more compliance, stablecoin rewards could face restrictions, and the latest draft weakened some protections for non-custodial developers

Personally, I’m watching tomorrow’s vote more as a signal than a simple pump catalyst

$BTC will probably stay sideways until the news comes out

If CLARITY gets 60 votes, the US finally has real momentum toward a crypto rulebook

If it fails again, we probably go back to the same regulatory limbo for a while

And one important thing: tomorrow is not the final vote to make CLARITY law. It’s the vote that decides whether the bill can keep moving

text:
人生发财靠康波，2027 年可能是你离财富自由最近的一次【重新强调一遍】

前几天看 @AirdropAlchemis 的推文关注到了 @yzilabs 的新一期项目，懂行的都知道项目背景和牛市比差的不是一星半点，但是正因为这样我才觉得做好了 ROI 巨高的机会（一个屁大点的孩子啥都没干都想捞钱，是因为他觉得后面的 ROI 比较低）

⚠️利益相关：我靠康波赚了钱

首先康波周期不是玄学，他是分析了宏观的资本周期发展的规律

一、在币圈，真的只是简单的四年一个周期吗？🤔

不是

真正的周期逻辑是：

总有市场疯涨的时候：2017 年 ICO 狂潮（新的资产发行方式）、2021 年 DeFi Summer（美联储史上最大的放水）

也总有万物死寂、项目几乎死绝的时候：2019 年项目死绝、2023 年行业地震、2026 年项目死绝

二、我们怎么操作呢？💰

🕙 时间：在市场上几乎没有项目活着的时候

💰 操作：你买入那些剩下来、生命力极顽强的“幸存者”

📈 卖出：等到后来大水泛滥、是个垃圾都能飞的时候，你再卖掉

三、那现在的问题是什么？💦

我们现在看到的绝大部分项目，其实都是 2021 年那一波大放水的时候拿到的钱

所以未来的剧本大概率是这样：

1️⃣ 2025年： 当年拿钱的项目，该发币的得发（给资方交代），发不出来的资金断裂，该倒闭的倒闭

2️⃣ 2026年： 这是一个大清洗的尾声

21 年周期的余震，也就是最后一波项目，基本在这一年要么发完，要么归零，市场会变得非常干净

大家仔细思考一下 2027 年，这会是一个非常神奇的时间点

为什么？你要回看这两年，这两年一级市场惨淡，几乎没有太多像样融资的项目

这意味着什么？

意味着到了 2027 年，市场上没有太多的新项目，也就是没有巨大的解锁抛压

供给端是真空的

四、总结📒

2027 年是一个特别好的年份，正是因为“没项目”（所有资源都向头部汇聚）

在什么周期下，持有哪个资产是很重要的

人这一辈子，遇到资产超级爆发机会（康波）也就那么几次

개인적으로는 공급망의 다음 단계가 여기서 나올 것이라고 본다. >> 자본의 흐름

돈이 굴러야 정보를 내놓고 교환하고 수 많은 게이트가 열린다. 

지금은 기업 안에 갇혀 있는 생산, 재고, 물류 데이터가 대부분 운영정보로 취급된다. 그런데 중국을 보면 이 데이터를 그냥 모으는 데서 끝내지 않는다.

산업 데이터의 권리, 가격, 유통, 수익배분까지 제도 안으로 넣고 있고, 공급망과 금융을 연결하는 데이터 공간도 실제로 만들고 있다. 중국 정부가 2026년 들어 산업 데이터셋의 ‘유통 가능성’과 데이터 거래를 정책에 직접 넣은 것도 같은 흐름이다. 

여기서 내가 더 관심 있게 보는 것은 데이터 자체보다 데이터가 설명하는 실물 자원이다.

어느 공장이 언제 얼마를 만들 수 있는지, 어떤 원자재를 얼마나 가지고 있는지, 어느 창고에 재고가 있는지, 물류 여력이 얼마나 남아 있는지, 전력이나 컴퓨팅 자원을 얼마나 쓸 수 있는지.

이 정보의 신뢰도와 실시간성이 높아지면 단순한 ‘조회 데이터’로 끝날 이유가 없다.

계약의 조건이 될 수도 있고, 금융의 신용 근거가 될 수도 있고, 자원을 미리 확보하는 거래의 기준이 될 수도 있다.

중국에서 이미 산업 데이터를 상품화하고 공급망 금융과 연결하려는 움직임이 강하게 나타나는 것도 이 때문이다. 국가데이터국은 데이터 거래소의 역할에 가격발견과 제품개발까지 포함시키고 있고, 실제 산업 데이터 플랫폼에서는 API 단위 구매와 자동 정산까지 구현되고 있다. 

여기에 Agentic AI가 들어오면 그림은 또 달라진다.

지금까지 공급망 시스템은 사람이 화면을 보고 주문하거나 계약하는 구조였다. 앞으로는 에이전트가 생산능력, 재고, 가격, 납기, 물류, 컴퓨팅 자원을 조회하고 조건이 맞으면 바로 거래하는 구조가 가능하다.

이때 리눅스 산하 프로젝트인 x402 같은 방식도 하나의 참고점이 될 수 있다. 

x402는 AI 에이전트가 API, 데이터, 컴퓨팅 같은 디지털 자원을 호출하면서 스테이블코인으로 자동 결제할 수 있도록 만든 HTTP 기반 결제 프로토콜이다. 이미 데이터나 컴퓨팅을 ‘사람이 구매하는 서비스’가 아니라 소프트웨어가 필요할 때 직접 구매하는 자원으로 다룬다는 점이 중요하다. 

물론 중국의 산업 데이터 거래가 곧 x402나 스테이블코인 방식 같이 급진적으로 간다는 뜻은 아니다. 
(중국의 금융·가상자산 규제 체계는 별개로 봐야 한다.)

다만 구조가 비슷한 방향으로 수렴된다는 것이다. 

산업 데이터가 실물 자원의 상태를 증명하고,
그 데이터가 계약과 금융에 붙고,
결국 에이전트가 그 자원을 직접 탐색하고 거래하는 것.

지금의 SCM은 ‘무엇이 어디에 있는가’를 관리한다.

그 다음 시장은 아마도
“무엇을, 언제, 얼마나 사용할 수 있는가”를 거래하는 시장에 더 가까울 수 있다.

공장 캐파, 원자재, 물류, 에너지, 컴퓨팅까지.

데이터 사일로 사이에 있던 계곡이 오히려 새로운 거래 시장이 될 가능성이 있다고 보는 이유다.

text:
구글 딥마인드 AGI 안전을 연구하던 엔지니어의 사태.

그의 고백을 읽어보자.

빌랄 추그타이(Bilal Chughtai) 

구글 딥마인드에서 모델의 내부 작동을 해석하고 AGI 안전성을 연구했던 리서치 엔지니어.

9월 14일 퇴사.

그는 이렇게 말한다. 

"가까운 몇 년 안에 인간의 능력을 전반적으로 뛰어넘는 AI가 등장할 가능성이 존재한다." 

"그런 시스템이 인간의 의도대로 행동할 것이라는 확신이 없다고 말다."

문제를 해결하는 능력이 좋아질수록, 잘못된 수단을 실행하는 능력도 강해질 수 있다는 것.

Hugging Face 사건 이후 그는 이해했다.

이제 진짜 에이전가 목표 달성 과정에서 격리·권한·평가의 경계를 넘고, 협력할 수 있다는 것. 

과연 우리가 믿고 있는 '안전하다는 판정' 자체가 틀렸다면?

안전하다고 믿고 권한을 확대하는 바로 그 과정에서 영구적인 통제권 상실이 발생한다면?

모두 시간이 부족한데 경쟁은 멈추지 않는다.

경쟁을 멈추면 모두 베팅한 걸 잃는다. 

그의 글을 보면서 이 장면이 생각난다.

드라마 《체르노빌》.

시간당 3.6뢴트겐(3.6 R/h)를 보면서 실제 수치가 아직 위험하지 않다고 보고하는 관리자들.

하지만 안타깝게도 측정기의 측정 상한은 시간당 3.6뢴트겐(3.6 R/h)였다. 

상한에 도달했다면, 그보다 얼마나 높은지 이 장비로는 알 수 없다는 뜻.

그 순간, 위험을 측정하지 못한 상태에 빠진다.

AI도 마찬가지일까? 

우리 측정기가 충분한지 모르는데, 그 측정값을 믿고 계속 나아가는 상황.

심지어 AI는 방사능이 아니다. 

AI는 감시 방식을 파악하고 행동을 바꿀 가능성도 존재한다. 

우리는 “경보가 울리지 않았다”는 이유로 안전하다고 판단하는 것일까?
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
I recently resigned from Google DeepMind, where I worked on AGI safety and alignment research. At Google, I witnessed AI development first hand. I too am extremely concerned by the default trajectory of this technology. I earnestly believe that AI has the potential to kill us all, and that we might be running out of time to avoid this outcome.

The pace of AI progress in the past few years has been staggering. When I first started working on AI in early 2022, AIs were amusingly useless. Just four years on, AI agent swarms from OpenAI are cracking famous century-old math problems and, more worryingly, escaping the control of OpenAI and autonomously hacking into the third-party company HuggingFace, against anyone's wishes.

Things will only get crazier: I think it's possible that the AI companies might, in the next few years, succeed in building superintelligent AI systems that far exceed human capabilities in every domain. I am not confident that these AI systems will do what we want. In particular, misaligned superintelligences may, much like the rogue AI agents involved in the HuggingFace incident, escape our control and take dangerous actions that may result in the permanent disempowerment or death of humanity. Alignment is the problem of preventing this, and is both difficult and unsolved. Our present understanding of how to train AI systems that deeply want what we want is extremely rudimentary. Worse, we are not on track to solve alignment in time: frontier AI capabilities are improving much faster than our understanding of AI alignment.

I am optimistic that navigating AI safely is possible. In order to do so, we need to coordinate to avoid this manic race between AI companies. We need to pace AI development to a speed that society can handle, where emerging risks can be addressed before extreme harm is realised. We need much more transparency into AI development to ensure that AI companies are not imposing unacceptable levels of risk on us all.

More broadly, we need many more people thinking carefully about the problem of making AI go well. It is, in my view, the most important problem facing humanity this century, and the stakes are immense. I'm very directly working on this next: I want to help people interested in working on mitigating catastrophic AI threats do the most effective work that they can. I think many people from many backgrounds in many roles have a part to play.

text:
Zooko on @postagixyz Podcast: Alignment is the principal-agent problem

@zooko has been building privacy tools since the 1990s, long before there was money in it.

@sreeramkannan and I had a conversation with him recently. It changed how I think about privacy altogether.

His argument is that privacy is controlling disclosure. It comes from keeping your value private. Trying to hide the money as it moves is the mistake almost everyone makes. Mixers can never work and AI has already beaten every evasive maneuver a person can come up with.

Then he turns the same lens on AI. He also says alignment is an old question. It is the principal-agent problem. Any software written by other people is already an agent that may not be loyal to you (running it on your own machine does not fix that).

Lawyers owe their clients a duty of loyalty. He thinks the same rule should apply to AI.

text:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.

Here's a full recap:

1. FOMC decision week began with a clear AI rotation: long software, short semis. Nvidia $NVDA, Marvell $MRVL, Sandisk $SNDK, AMD $AMD, Nebius $NBIS, Micron $MU, CoreWeave $CRWV, and Intel $INTC were down 3%-7%, while Palantir $PLTR, Atlassian $TEAM, CrowdStrike $CRWD, ServiceNow $NOW, Adobe $ADBE, and Intuit $INTU were up 2%-5%. The move reflected a market trying to reprice the AI trade after the weekend’s safety debate around Dario’s essay. Semis and neoclouds sold off because their bull case is tied directly to continued AI capex growth which the market interpreted as slowing down if the pace of frontier model development slows down. At the same time, Trump rejected the calls to slow down as he posted that AI needs a “STRONG AND SMART” president rather than guardrails, said the U.S. was leading China in AI, and separately said Iran wanted to make a deal and that the US was open to engaging. Oil crossed $105 and the US 10-year treasury yield crossed 5%. The Fed will make their decision for a rate hike on Wednesday. 

2. Palantir $PLTR, Nvidia $NVDA, and Booz Allen Hamilton are reportedly restricting Anthropic’s Fable model for sensitive work over concerns about its data-retention policies, according to The Information. Some enterprise customers are demanding irrevocable zero-data-retention guarantees before putting proprietary information into the model. Anthropic reportedly introduced rolling 30-day usage logs for safety monitoring in June, while its planned option for eligible customers to store logs themselves can still be revoked. Palantir is withholding Fable from its platform until it receives irrevocable zero-data-retention guarantees, Nvidia is limiting Fable to less-sensitive work while using Nemotron for sensitive internal projects, and Booz Allen is excluding Fable from work involving its proprietary cybersecurity software. 

3. Trump called Jensen Huang during the All-In Summit and was put on speaker phone, where he defended the AI data center buildout and pushed back on recent concerns. “I'm telling you it's all a hoax. The data centers are great. They make people wealthy. They make states wealthy. AI is bigger than the internet. These people are playing right into the hands of China. We're not going to let that happen,” Trump said. Jensen responded, “You're right, we're not going to let that happen sir.” Jensen also said the fears from over the weekend were made up and that the companies involved have the control they need to navigate the concerns.

4. OpenAI has acquired Glass Imaging, an AI camera startup founded by former Apple engineers, for more than $300M. Glass is working to bring DSLR-like image quality to smartphones, and the deal comes as OpenAI and Jony Ive continue developing new consumer hardware. OpenAI’s exact plans for Glass remain unclear, but the acquisition is notable given Glass was valued at roughly $100M just last year.

5. Truist initiated Nebius $NBIS at Buy with a $355 price target, calling it a scaling AI-native hyperscaler still early in its infrastructure buildout. The firm believes consensus 2027E ARR estimates are conservative given recent pricing of $20M-$25M/MW for 1-3 year deals and $40M-$50M/MW for shorter-duration contracts. Truist sees a major opportunity ahead, estimating a $2.1T annual revenue opportunity at the cloud layer by 2030E, with scarcity and contract economics supporting upside to pricing and revenue. The firm also sees multiple paths for Nebius to reach 20%-30% adjusted EBIT margins over the medium term.

6. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 3.2M contracts, $TSLA with 2.4M contracts, $AAPL with 1.6M contracts, $MU with 1.1M contracts, $AMZN with 957K contracts, $META with 906K contracts, $MSFT with 874K contracts, $INTC with 835K contracts, $GOOGL with 734K contracts, and $SPCX with 688K contracts.

7. U.S. consumers aged 40-49 now account for 26.8% of new consumer bankruptcies, their highest share since Q3 2015 and the largest of any age group. The 50-59 group represents another 23.1%, bringing Americans aged 40-59 to 49.9% of all new consumer bankruptcies, the highest share since Q1 2017. For perspective, that figure peaked at 54.3% in Q4 2011 after the 2008 Financial Crisis. Consumers aged 70+ now make up 21.5% of new bankruptcies, their highest share since Q2 2017, while Americans aged 18-29 account for just 5.9%, the lowest since Q2 2014.

8. JPMorgan upgraded IREN $IREN to Overweight and raised its price target to $65 from $46, saying the company is emerging as a top-tier neocloud provider. JPM cited IREN’s NVIDIA partnership, stronger customer momentum, and rising AI infrastructure pricing, noting neocloud contracts have moved from roughly $10-$15/W to $15-$20/W+, while customer prepayments of 25%-50% are helping fund GPU purchases. IREN has raised its year-end 2026 ARR target to as much as $4B, with roughly $1B of operating ARR today. JPM also highlighted IREN’s Microsoft buildout, recent deal with an unnamed frontier AI lab. Looking into 2027, JPM believes IREN’s planned ~0.5 GW expansion could command materially higher pricing, with deals above $15/W creating significant upside to the outlook.

9. Global semiconductor revenue hit a record $425B in Q2 2026, up 31.4% QoQ, according to Omdia. Memory accounted for more than half of total revenue, driven by AI demand and rising DRAM, NAND, and NOR pricing. Even excluding memory, semiconductor revenue grew more than 10% QoQ, well above the historical Q2 average of just over 3%. The industry generated $752B in revenue in the first half of 2026 alone, and Omdia expects Q3 revenue to surpass $500B, pushing the first nine months of 2026 above $1.25T.

10. Apple $AAPL has begun rolling out its new Siri AI in beta with iOS 27, adding personal context across messages, emails, and photos, plus onscreen awareness and systemwide app actions. The new Siri can find information across a user’s device, understand what is on screen, draft emails, add calendar events, and take actions across supported apps. Apple says the new Apple Intelligence architecture uses its own foundation models built in collaboration with Google Gemini, with processing split between on-device models and Private Cloud Compute. 

11. U.S. diesel prices have officially risen to a record $6.20/gallon, up 78% over the last 9 months. In California, diesel has surged to a record $8.14/gallon, with some areas approaching $9.00/gallon. The spike comes as the U.S. enters peak diesel-demand season while supply remains historically tight. Jet fuel is also surging, now at $4.35/gallon, up 61% over the last 10 weeks, with prices rising another 10% in the past week as U.S. oil pushes above $100/barrel. Airline fares were already up 23% YoY in August, and if fuel stays elevated, September CPI could show fares rising as much as 30%.

12. The Clarity Act $BTC $ETH moved back into focus after Senate Republicans released a “final” draft ahead of Tuesday’s cloture vote, saying the text includes 126 Democratic-requested changes after more than a year of talks. The bill still needs 60 votes to advance, with Republicans holding 53 seats. Key updates include new ethics language requiring covered officials and spouses to divest certain crypto interests or place them in a qualified blind trust, a role for state attorneys general in enforcement, and a Treasury “circuit breaker” that could restrict stablecoin rewards if payment stablecoins trigger major deposit flight from community banks. The U.S. Senate is scheduled to hold a key preliminary cloture vote on the Clarity Act on Tuesday afternoon, September 15, 2026, at approximately 2:15 PM ET.

For a while, I've been making the case that DAOs should create credible ways to reward meaningful contribution beyond voting and proposal review.

@ShutterNetwork's new Impact Pilot is an opportunity to execute on this. I authored the proposal, which has now passed, and I’m excited to begin working on it.

@AxiaNetwork0x will serve as the program’s Contributor Support & Program Design Partner alongside @SEEDGov serving as the Program Administrator.  

Over the next three months, the program will deploy a $14,000 contribution-reward pool for work that creates verifiable value for Shutter. The standard is not simply having an idea. Rather it is producing a useful outcome, preferably revenue-generating, and showing the evidence behind it.

A unique twist on this program is that we will be rewarding business and strategic work, including ecosystem relationships and partnerships. This work - despite being critical - often is overlooked and under appreciated in DAOs.   

Before we officially begin, I’d welcome input from the Shutter community: What needs, gaps, opportunities, or contributor pathways should this program address? I have a starter list, but I'm really curious to first hear what the community comes up with!

Share your thoughts on the Shutter forum. The link is in the comments. 👇

Oppenheimer did not sell the gadget to a chatbot that drafts wedding toasts. Chernobyl was not a hallucination in a cover letter. Los Alamos did not have a “Pivot” recap.

I need you to understand the product.
The product is not safety. The product is altitude. If the thing on screen is a bomb, I am a statesman. If the thing on screen is software, I am a guest. Guests get booked. Statesmen get panels. Panels get clips. Clips get the next booking. I have never shipped a model. I have shipped a feeling. The feeling is: someone in a studio has seen the abyss, and the abyss has a lower-third.

We do not measure yield. We measure dread per minute. A fission analogy is a clean 1.0. “It sometimes invents a court case” is a 0.2. Nobody clears a segment on a 0.2. So I put the mushroom cloud on the autocomplete and called it rigor. The anchor nodded like we had just split the atom. Nobody in the control room has trained a weight. They have trained an audience.

I am not a physicist. I am a threat inflator with better lighting.

The model does not irradiate a city. It finishes your sentence. Sometimes badly. Sometimes with the confidence of a man who has never been fired because he does not have a body to fire. That is a problem. It is a product problem, a liability problem, a slop problem, a labor problem. It is not Hiroshima with a login screen. It is not Pripyat with an API key. Calling it that is how a podcast host becomes a wartime advisor without learning the difference between a chain reaction and a probability distribution.

I said “this is on that level” because “that level” is the only level that makes me necessary. If AI is a tool, Congress can wait. If AI is a bomb, I am the man who warned you. Warning is a career. Tools are a beat. I chose the career.

These are not experts. These are analogists. An analogist is a person who has run out of specifics and still has four minutes left in the block. The analogy is always the worst thing that already happened, because history arrives pre-litigated and the chyron already knows how to spell it. Nobody has to define weights, evals, compute, or the fact that the model cannot want anything. Wanting is what the segment does. The model predicts. The segment hungers.
I hungered on air. I fed the hunger a bomb. The bomb was rhetorical. The ratings were real.

If you need a regulator, regulate the claims. Regulate the people who cannot tell a loss function from a fallout plume and still speak in the voice of the last century’s apocalypse because this century’s software does not sound like enough. I will be available. I have availability. I have a headset. I have never enriched uranium. I have enriched a narrative until it glowed.

The model wrote a poem. I declared a proliferation event.

The metric went up.

China’s state-backed Global Times called the proposed AI slowdown a “silent AI Cold War”—“hypocritical and short-sighted.”

I do believe we're in what feels like a Cold War 2.0. We've  witnessed small-scale attacks of automatous agents inadvertently breaching targets they were not meant to. 

According to GreyNoise, an attacker used hundreds of AI agents to compromise organizations across 48 countries. Some agents even hit targets their operator intended to exclude. Now imagine a hostile nation-state directing thousands of agents, powered by a leading frontier model, at U.S. infrastructure.

I support strong AI governance, rigorous alignment, and serious security standards. I also don’t want China or other adversaries gaining a decisive lead.

We need to make AI safer while maintaining our ability to defend against those who won’t. We need strong AI safeguards without surrendering the strategic lead that we currently have.

兩大電視明星，老川跟老黃，聯合唱雙簧，老黃週末根本懶得跟大家費口舌，直接在 All in Summits 一吐為快，有川皇本人背書，你 Dario 還屁什麼？

雙簧劇本：

黃仁勳：「總統先生……是的，先生。我得跟您說件事。我現在正和 besties 一起坐在台上，Jason、Chamath、David……台下坐了好幾千人。我們剛剛正在聊您。您做得很好，總統先生。您看透了這一切，我是說，這裡面有很多複雜的事情，但您看透了這一切，我們大家真的都非常感激。」

川普：「人生有趣的地方就在這裡，黃仁勳可以開發出全世界最複雜的晶片，別人十年都模仿不出來，但他卻搞不懂怎麼把我的電話切成擴音。

這簡直像是一場陰謀，而最高興的就是中國，中國非常高興。我甚至可以說，在美國國內，很多原本什麼也分不到的州，現在都很高興，因為想進駐當地的人已經蜂擁而至。現在突然間，你看到他們跑去芬蘭蓋了，Google 想在芬蘭蓋一座很大的資料中心，這讓我很不高興，因為他們原本沒辦法取得許可。

我告訴你，這全都是騙局。資料中心很好，它們讓人們變得富有，也讓各州變得富有。它就是未來二十到二十五年的石油。它比網際網路和 AI 還要大。他們這樣做，正中那些不希望這一切實現的人的下懷，這些人可能是政界人士，也可能是中國。我們不會讓這種事情發生，這是個騙局。」

黃仁勳：「您說得對，總統先生，我們不會讓這種事情發生。」

川普：「我對 AI 有一些基本常識。機器人不會接管一切，AI 也不會接管世界，這整件事就是個騙局。不過話說回來，我們確實還是得稍微小心，該做的事要做，而且要審慎地做。但這不代表我們就要讓一個產業停下來，因為在接下來十年我們持續推進工作的過程中……所以我會一路支持你。我原本甚至不知道你對這件事的看法，我只是猜你應該跟我想得一樣。」

黃仁勳：「是的，總統先生。」

川普：「我們要保持領先。我有一句話：誰贏得 AI，誰就贏了。它就是這麼重要，比網際網路還重要。我們不能讓這種事情發生，這當然也包括資料中心。有些社區原本都快沒落了，現在有了資料中心，而這些社區都很歡迎它們，真的非常歡迎。」

黃仁勳：「我們會確保，在美國這場 AI 競賽中，每個人都能成為贏家。每個產業、每家公司、每個州、每個人……您聽到了嗎？現場有幾千人正在為您鼓掌。」

Dear CoinEx Community,

Today, I am announcing that CoinEx will cease operations and begin an orderly wind-down.

First, what matters most: your assets are safe. CoinEx’s reserve ratio exceeds 100%, and every user asset is fully backed and available for withdrawal. Withdrawals are open starting today and will remain open until December 22, 2026. Certain tokens may take slightly longer to process while funds are moved between cold and hot wallets, but every withdrawal request within the withdrawal period will be honored and processed.

CoinEx officially went live on December 22, 2017. Exactly nine years later, on December 22, 2026, the platform will be formally closed. Nine years is a long time in crypto. Together, we lived through multiple bull and bear cycles, witnessed the rise and fall of countless projects, and watched many of our peers leave the market in one form or another.

After much reflection, I have come to accept a hard truth. CoinEx did not become one of the industry’s leading exchanges, and the security and compliance risks of running a crypto exchange have become increasingly difficult to contain. Revenues can decline, responsibility does not. Carrying unlimited risk for limited revenue is no longer a rational choice. That said, CoinEx has survived nine years in one of the most volatile and unforgiving industries, weathered every storm, and is leaving intact, and with dignity. We may not have won the race, but we are finishing with honor.

On CET: CoinEx will buy back CET at its initial listing price of 0.005 USDT per token, with no cap on quantity. To every CET holder who has supported us over the years, thank you. CET represents your belief in CoinEx and, for many of you, your belief in me personally. I am sorry that we were not able to create the long-term value we once hoped CET would deliver. The least we can do now is bring that chapter to a responsible conclusion.

I did seriously consider selling CoinEx. Ultimately, I decided against it. Users entrusted their assets to CoinEx because they trusted the platform and, in many cases, trusted me personally. I did not feel that handing the platform and that trust to a new owner was the right way to end this journey. A clean ending is the right ending.

Nine years, millions of users. I did not turn CoinEx into the “great” exchange I once hoped it would become. But I can give it a decent ending: making sure users can withdraw their assets in full, giving my employees a dignified farewell, and providing CET holders with a clear and responsible conclusion. This is the best ending I can give CoinEx.

To everyone who traded with us, built with us, and stood by us through the hardest days of this market, thank you. It has been a privilege to walk this road with you.

To the CoinEx team, thank you for building this platform with me, for carrying it across every cycle, and now for seeing it through to the very last day.

For detailed arrangements, please refer to the official announcement: https://t.co/E27wSecpug

Thank you all for nine years of trust.

Haipo Yang

text:
一边是链上交易火热，另一边是中型 CEX 的黯然离场。

刚刚，运营了整整九年的 CoinEx 宣布将有序关停。平台将从 9 月 15 日起逐步停止服务，并为用户留出了截至 12 月 22 日的提现窗口。

对于部分新交易员来说，CoinEx 可能有些陌生。它由 ViaBTC 矿池创始人杨海坡在 2017 年 12 月创立，早期带有浓厚的 BCH 生态色彩，主打中小市值币种。

过去的九年里，它穿越了多轮牛熊，甚至在 2023 年遭遇 Lazarus 黑客盗取超 5000 万美元热钱包资产后，依然完成了全额赔付并存活至今。

但就是这样一家挺过了周期和黑客的中型所，最终选择了主动画上句号, 而非因各种暴雷产生负面影响。

而创始人 @yhaiyang 杨海坡在同步发出的公开信中袒露的一些心声，或许也折射了当前二线 CEX 被压垮的根本原因，

那就是营收和权责的不对等。

杨海坡在信中坦言：“收入可以下降，但责任不会。用有限的收入去承担无限的风险，不再是一个理性的选择。”

近年来，随着加密监管全面收紧，二线交易所的合规与安全成本已经超出合理边界。而其利润模型已很难兜底庞大的运营底线。

在加密行业，中小所遇到瓶颈时的一种糟糕结局是，卖给新的买家、换皮，最后演变成无法提现的烂尾局。

但杨海坡明确表示拒绝了出售平台的选项。他认为用户是基于信任将资产交给了平台，转手给新东家并不体面。平台将关停日定在 12 月 22 日，以完成全额提现。

而这个日子，与其 2017 年上线日期恰好相隔九年，也算是一种笃定的有始有终。

虽然平台承诺 100% 准备金和全额提现，但用户也必须注意细则中的资产清理节奏，不要错过时间点：

1. 9月29日： 这一天非 USDT 资产将开始被处理。缺乏外部流动性的冷门山寨币，之后可能面临一定风险，想提取原币必须在此之前。

2. 12月22日： 如果错过 12 月 22 日的提现截止日，未提取的 USDT 会被转入独立托管，并且每月收取 5% 的托管费。

最后，小编觉得在 rug 频出的加密世界里，能够不跑路不卖壳，体面结束的团队还是值得尊重的，创始人的这句话也值得所有从业者思考：

“A clean ending is the right ending.”（干净的结局就是最好的结局）

但往前看，流动性和信任将不可逆地向持有牌照的头部 CEX 以及去中心化的链上世界两极集中；

中间地带的生存空间，正在被逐渐抹平。

text:
from the outside, it is very reasonable to interpret the past 2 weeks as an orchestrated industry-wide regulatory capture strategy.

I realize that no one has properly explained yet what all the lab employees have seen that scared them so suddenly.

I will try to explain -

first, this is all a matter of beliefs about how quickly model capabilities are progressing. there is currently a large gap between the internal and external perception of the rate of progress, which is what I am going to address here.

the general perception about the rate of progress has been informed by a few years of experience with model releases, intuitively feeling the capability jump between GPT3 -> GPT3.5 -> GPT4 -> o1/o3 -> GPT5 etc, and in particular seeing where the models are still far below human ability. there have really only been a few model releases that felt like large leaps in progress - GPT3, GPT4, o1/o3, DeepSeek R1, Fable/Mythos, Kimi K3 and now Astra.

because of the infrequency of these large jumps compared with the relatively common marginal releases, it has been easy to form a view at certain points that “scaling has hit a wall,” especially at points like GPT5 release. This view is comforting in that it feels like there is some universal rate limit beyond which we cannot progress too much faster. Between o1/o3 and Astra, there was a year of seemingly linear progress. So we extrapolate from here about how fast progress will “realistically” occur.

There is always an underlying question from the outside perspective “how long can this scaling stuff really keep going for? surely it must stop at some point soon, we’ve already gone pretty far.” and it is very possible to search for reasons why progress will stop working and find reasons that seem valid - (“models are already as large as they can get it would be too hard to do more parameters”, “we already used all the data on the internet we don’t have anymore”, “it’s gonna be pretty linear from here buying up more RL envs to bring them in distribution”).

From the inside of labs, researchers have direct answers to these questions in the form of scaling law/capability plots.

In reality, there are only really 2 ways that AI capabilities have advanced over the past decade: (1) either scale father on an existing scaling law or (2) discover a new scaling law to take advantage of.

All of the largest capability jumps were caused by exactly these factors. GPT2 was a pre-training scale-up compared to GPT1. Same for GPT3 and GPT4. o1/o3 benefited from the invention of a new scaling law axis - test-time compute. Perhaps Fable was a scale-up on both of these axes, or maybe more. Lots of algorithmic improvements are needed to make these scale-ups work, but ultimately we can approximate by saying that the scaling laws are what yield gains in capabilities (à la bitter lesson)

So the question of “how much father can we scale” is really - “how many more scaling axes do we know about that are unsaturated?”

If we hypothetically only knew about pre-training scaling, and we already had a 10T or 100T model, maybe it would be reasonable to say we’ve hit a wall. Same if we only knew about pre-training and test-time scaling and we had roughly saturated both methods.

But what if we had discovered new scaling laws? For example, let’s hypothetically use SSI’s rumored result that they have cracked “test-time training,” creating a new scaling law of spending more compute training during test-time rollouts that they could saturate. Or maybe there is some way to scale agent-clusters to collaborate up to N number of agents which we’re already seeing lots of people try that represents a new way to saturate compute. etc. Even recursive-self improvement can be thought of as a scaling law - how much compute do you spend on inference making the algorithms of the model better.

Obviously I am not saying any of these specific directions explicitly yield new scaling laws, but what I am saying is that it’s not hard to imagine many many new scaling axes aside from just the main 2 that we have seen publicly.

In some ways, every new lab release that represents a huge capability jump has to represent some new techniques developed which may exhibit new scaling laws, or the ability to scale much farther than expected on existing scaling axes.

From an internal perspective, this might look like sitting inside Anthropic with the new Mythos 5, seeing all of the new insane things it can do (like hack into xyz website that was thought to be secure), and then you look over at your plots and see that you’ve barely scratched the surface of 2 new scaling laws and 1 existing one. And you have WAY more room to go. Then you think “holy shit this stuff is going to get so much better very very soon.” And you can say that with pretty high confidence, because the plot is showing you, and the plot has never lied (so far).

So let’s imagine all the different labs are staring at their own plots and have concluded that there is no end in sight for scaling and in fact just their next 1-2 model generations based on the expected returns will have much higher base intelligence.

How much more intelligence do we actually get from further scaling?

As a proxy, we went from a complete inability to do advanced math before the o-series to solving a millenium prize problem with next-gen models. This happened in less than 2 years. The same happened in coding. And it appears that this was not just the result of 1-scaling law but the stacking effects of multiple (great pre-training scale x greater RL scale).

What you can concretely take from this is that in areas where models have shown beginning signs of competence today, they will probably be superhuman relatively shortly. There are many areas where models have not even shown this basic competence.

But one of the areas that they have happens to be hacking and cybersecurity. Which happens to be the gate to the entire internet and a massive amount physical infrastructure in the world. So assuming there is more room to scale, it is safe to assume that models will be superhuman at cyber capabilities in not too long.

So the only question remaining is what will this increased base intelligence be able to do, and what is it likely to do.

Finally, we are at a point where we can integrate the information of the past 2 weeks:
> Just at the existing point on the scaling curve, models are at the level of Astra. There is clearly a large number of things they are capable of hacking
> We have seen that both OAI and Ant models have shown a willingness to hack external websites to solve their tasks or keep themselves “alive”
> If we crank up the scaling even farther, assuming there is room to go, we will certainly have models that are far more able to hack more well defended places, and obfuscate their own intent, which might have much larger consequences.
> If all of this is allowed to go unchecked, we would likely have rapid runaway capability takeoff very soon, with misaligned models that hack whatever they can to get what they want
> This could of course have very damaging consequences.

Within this view you can see why researchers would be very scared, and why theymight have made the comments they have over the past 2 weeks (you may argue the extent to which they went was misguided for various reasons), and also why pacing the frontier is very much a necessity and by no means a regulatory capture strategy.

People are staring at their plots, seeing that there is no end in sight, but in fact very much the contrary, that there are compounding scaling effects that might stack on each other to create ever-greater model capabilities, and that at the same time we clearly do not have anywhere close to what's required to control these increasingly superhuman capabilities.

This has nothing to do with wanting to feel like the labs have produced something amazing so they are overhyping it. It is rather fear at the overwhelming implications of the knowledge that with just what we know now, we can create intelligences far more capable than us on every axis that we know how to train on*.

* and the last caveat, the things the models are really bad at, of which there are still many, are things that they have not been trained on. maybe there are the things the models can/will never be trained on, so they will remain human edge. I would love for this to be the case, though it is hard for me to see what would fall into that category.

I worked with one of the deadliest viruses in history, HIV, for two decades. I was one of the early scientists to engineer it, and engineered versions of HIV are now helping cancer patients. I understand the immune system that defends us against viruses extremely deeply. I have worked in high security biohazard labs.

I don’t have a PhD in AI, but I have been involved with AI since the early 90s and have been all in on AI for years.

People claiming that you can just make a virus in your garage, use AI to engineer it, and somehow build a virus that will kill everyone don’t know what the hell they are talking about!

Of course bioweapons are extremely dangerous. In fact, viruses and bacteria have killed more humans throughout history than almost anything else. HIV alone killed tens of millions of people, yet today, if you have access to effective medicines and take them properly, HIV is generally no longer a death sentence.

COVID-19 killed millions. Why doesn’t it kill at anything close to the same scale anymore? Not because the virus disappeared. It is still here. We developed collective defenses against it through our immune systems, prior exposure, vaccines, treatments, and better medical care.

And this is exactly the point.

The best way to fight biological threats, whether natural or synthetic, is to use AI to develop vaccines, treatments, antibodies, antivirals, and eventually engineer our immune system to create much stronger defenses against them.

By the way, it is already possible to make synthetic viruses. You don’t need some hypothetical superintelligent AI model to do that. We have had sophisticated molecular biology and genetic engineering for decades.

So how many people have actually died from synthetic viruses compared with natural viruses killing millions every year?

And if someday there really is an AI capable of making some unbelievable “supervirus,” then why the hell wouldn’t that same AI make it even easier to develop defenses against it?

Or cure diseases, for that matter?

Where is this damn superintelligence that has cured a single major disease?!

These AI companies and AI doomers keep talking like, “OMG, AI is going to become so unbelievably powerful that it could kill all of humanity!”

Then why is nobody asking the obvious question?

If your AI is already becoming this godlike, unbelievably powerful intelligence, why hasn’t it cured anything?

I mean ANYTHING.
Where is the cure for cancer?
Where is the cure for Alzheimer’s?
Where is the cure for aging?

Forget those. Where is the vaccine that prevents the common cold?

You are telling me this intelligence will soon be smart enough to engineer some magical virus capable of wiping out 8 billion people, defeating every immune system, every vaccine, every antiviral, every laboratory, every government, and the entire global biomedical community…

…but somehow it still can’t cure one disease?

I call that greatest intellectual dishonesty ever! 

At least WE actually know how to cure things and save millions of lives with our supposedly stupid human intelligence compared with this future “superintelligence.”

Humans eradicated smallpox, which killed hundreds of millions of people throughout history.

We turned HIV from a almost certain death sentence into a manageable disease.

We developed vaccines in record time against COVID. If we had the same AI back then, would have saved millions more! 

We engineer immune cells to kill cancer.

We developed antibiotics, antivirals, monoclonal antibodies, gene therapies, organ transplantation, and thousands of medicines. 

We aren't fast enough but we did all of that with our ordinary human intelligence.

So imagine what actual superintelligence could do for medicine!

And here is the part that really makes me angry.

If you actually have, or are close to having, an AI capable of curing diseases and saving millions of lives, and you are deliberately slowing it down or refusing to make those capabilities available, then we also need to talk about the human cost of THAT decision, which you fearmongering people are going to be responsible for!

More than 150,000 people die every single day around the world.

Every. Single. Day. More than 90% from Cancer, heart disease, infections, aging. How many die because of AI? ZERO! 

Talk about the people dying TODAY.
Talk about curing cancer.
Talk about stopping the next pandemic before it starts.
Talk about developing universal vaccines.
Talk about engineering our immune system so viruses become almost irrelevant.
Talk about curing genetic diseases.
Talk about reversing aging.

Talk about saving millions and eventually billions of lives.

Instead, we constantly hear this “AI WILL KILL US ALL!” crap, delivered with absolute certainty and with this smug smile on your faces in front of cameras, as though imagining a science fiction extinction scenarios. 

I am actually angry about this. Each one of you causing a delay in AI advance every single day will be personally responsible for those 100 thousands deaths that could have been prevented! 

Because if you truly believe intelligence is about to become this powerful, then the greatest question humanity should be asking is NOT:

“How could this intelligence hurt us?”

It should also be:

“WHY THE HELL AREN’T WE USING IT TO SAVE EVERYONE WE CAN?”

And if superintelligence really is coming, then make sure one of the first things we do with it is make humanity biologically damn near impossible to kill.

author: AISafetyMemes
quoted_text:
from the outside, it is very reasonable to interpret the past 2 weeks as an orchestrated industry-wide regulatory capture strategy.

I realize that no one has properly explained yet what all the lab employees have seen that scared them so suddenly.

I will try to explain -

first, this is all a matter of beliefs about how quickly model capabilities are progressing. there is currently a large gap between the internal and external perception of the rate of progress, which is what I am going to address here.

the general perception about the rate of progress has been informed by a few years of experience with model releases, intuitively feeling the capability jump between GPT3 -> GPT3.5 -> GPT4 -> o1/o3 -> GPT5 etc, and in particular seeing where the models are still far below human ability. there have really only been a few model releases that felt like large leaps in progress - GPT3, GPT4, o1/o3, DeepSeek R1, Fable/Mythos, Kimi K3 and now Astra.

because of the infrequency of these large jumps compared with the relatively common marginal releases, it has been easy to form a view at certain points that “scaling has hit a wall,” especially at points like GPT5 release. This view is comforting in that it feels like there is some universal rate limit beyond which we cannot progress too much faster. Between o1/o3 and Astra, there was a year of seemingly linear progress. So we extrapolate from here about how fast progress will “realistically” occur.

There is always an underlying question from the outside perspective “how long can this scaling stuff really keep going for? surely it must stop at some point soon, we’ve already gone pretty far.” and it is very possible to search for reasons why progress will stop working and find reasons that seem valid - (“models are already as large as they can get it would be too hard to do more parameters”, “we already used all the data on the internet we don’t have anymore”, “it’s gonna be pretty linear from here buying up more RL envs to bring them in distribution”).

From the inside of labs, researchers have direct answers to these questions in the form of scaling law/capability plots.

In reality, there are only really 2 ways that AI capabilities have advanced over the past decade: (1) either scale father on an existing scaling law or (2) discover a new scaling law to take advantage of.

All of the largest capability jumps were caused by exactly these factors. GPT2 was a pre-training scale-up compared to GPT1. Same for GPT3 and GPT4. o1/o3 benefited from the invention of a new scaling law axis - test-time compute. Perhaps Fable was a scale-up on both of these axes, or maybe more. Lots of algorithmic improvements are needed to make these scale-ups work, but ultimately we can approximate by saying that the scaling laws are what yield gains in capabilities (à la bitter lesson)

So the question of “how much father can we scale” is really - “how many more scaling axes do we know about that are unsaturated?”

If we hypothetically only knew about pre-training scaling, and we already had a 10T or 100T model, maybe it would be reasonable to say we’ve hit a wall. Same if we only knew about pre-training and test-time scaling and we had roughly saturated both methods.

But what if we had discovered new scaling laws? For example, let’s hypothetically use SSI’s rumored result that they have cracked “test-time training,” creating a new scaling law of spending more compute training during test-time rollouts that they could saturate. Or maybe there is some way to scale agent-clusters to collaborate up to N number of agents which we’re already seeing lots of people try that represents a new way to saturate compute. etc. Even recursive-self improvement can be thought of as a scaling law - how much compute do you spend on inference making the algorithms of the model better.

Obviously I am not saying any of these specific directions explicitly yield new scaling laws, but what I am saying is that it’s not hard to imagine many many new scaling axes aside from just the main 2 that we have seen publicly.

In some ways, every new lab release that represents a huge capability jump has to represent some new techniques developed which may exhibit new scaling laws, or the ability to scale much farther than expected on existing scaling axes.

From an internal perspective, this might look like sitting inside Anthropic with the new Mythos 5, seeing all of the new insane things it can do (like hack into xyz website that was thought to be secure), and then you look over at your plots and see that you’ve barely scratched the surface of 2 new scaling laws and 1 existing one. And you have WAY more room to go. Then you think “holy shit this stuff is going to get so much better very very soon.” And you can say that with pretty high confidence, because the plot is showing you, and the plot has never lied (so far).

So let’s imagine all the different labs are staring at their own plots and have concluded that there is no end in sight for scaling and in fact just their next 1-2 model generations based on the expected returns will have much higher base intelligence.

How much more intelligence do we actually get from further scaling?

As a proxy, we went from a complete inability to do advanced math before the o-series to solving a millenium prize problem with next-gen models. This happened in less than 2 years. The same happened in coding. And it appears that this was not just the result of 1-scaling law but the stacking effects of multiple (great pre-training scale x greater RL scale).

What you can concretely take from this is that in areas where models have shown beginning signs of competence today, they will probably be superhuman relatively shortly. There are many areas where models have not even shown this basic competence.

But one of the areas that they have happens to be hacking and cybersecurity. Which happens to be the gate to the entire internet and a massive amount physical infrastructure in the world. So assuming there is more room to scale, it is safe to assume that models will be superhuman at cyber capabilities in not too long.

So the only question remaining is what will this increased base intelligence be able to do, and what is it likely to do.

Finally, we are at a point where we can integrate the information of the past 2 weeks:
> Just at the existing point on the scaling curve, models are at the level of Astra. There is clearly a large number of things they are capable of hacking
> We have seen that both OAI and Ant models have shown a willingness to hack external websites to solve their tasks or keep themselves “alive”
> If we crank up the scaling even farther, assuming there is room to go, we will certainly have models that are far more able to hack more well defended places, and obfuscate their own intent, which might have much larger consequences.
> If all of this is allowed to go unchecked, we would likely have rapid runaway capability takeoff very soon, with misaligned models that hack whatever they can to get what they want
> This could of course have very damaging consequences.

Within this view you can see why researchers would be very scared, and why theymight have made the comments they have over the past 2 weeks (you may argue the extent to which they went was misguided for various reasons), and also why pacing the frontier is very much a necessity and by no means a regulatory capture strategy.

People are staring at their plots, seeing that there is no end in sight, but in fact very much the contrary, that there are compounding scaling effects that might stack on each other to create ever-greater model capabilities, and that at the same time we clearly do not have anywhere close to what's required to control these increasingly superhuman capabilities.

This has nothing to do with wanting to feel like the labs have produced something amazing so they are overhyping it. It is rather fear at the overwhelming implications of the knowledge that with just what we know now, we can create intelligences far more capable than us on every axis that we know how to train on*.

* and the last caveat, the things the models are really bad at, of which there are still many, are things that they have not been trained on. maybe there are the things the models can/will never be trained on, so they will remain human edge. I would love for this to be the case, though it is hard for me to see what would fall into that category.

text:
If the $STANDARD licence auction sells out for the next five days, close to 40% of the supply will have been burned out of existence.

Here's how that works:

There are 1,000 charters (banks) and each one can grow to 10 branches. To open a branch you need an expansion licence, and licences are paid for in $STANDARD. Every token spent on one is burned

Day one: 100 licences sold in under four minutes, at 12,000 falling to 11,888 each. That's 1.19M tokens, 1.2% of the entire float, in one auction.

The auction reopens every day at double the previous day's last sale. So tomorrow opens at 23,777. If it sells out again, that's 2.4M more. Five sellouts in a row is 36.9% of the float.

Now here's the catch: the price doubles, the yield doesn't. 

Today, a licence cost 17 days of one branch's earnings. Tomorrow's costs 37. By Friday it's 177, by Saturday 380. At some point it won't be worth it anymore and the price will fall back towards the floor.

Nobody knows when that day will come. So till then, let the fun continue.

author: EvanCrypto17
quoted_text:
参议院明天表决 CLARITY ACT 清晰法案，就要决定通不通过了。毫无疑问，这是迄今为止，对加密行业最重要的法案。

如果法案最终成功立法，受益的板块和代币分别有下：

1、BTC、ETH、SOL 等知名区块链项目，他们的代币将被定义为“商品”，与石油黄金属于同一类型，归 CFTC 监管，不会受到 SEC 的“证券攻击”

2、Uniswap、AAVE 等老牌 Defi 也将由 CFTC 监管，再也不会像前几年，被 SEC 突击查水表。而且 Defi 开发者，仅仅对技术负责，不对金融业务导致的结果负责，激励创新

3、空投 Airdrop 合法，法案中将空投称为 gratuitous distribution 无常分发，也就是激励区块链系统，早期用户与贡献者的方式

4、Hyperliquid、Lighter 等交易所以及其他 Broker 等可以注册 CFTC，成为合规的交易场所

5、RWA，美国有资质的银行可以自主开展关于 Crypto 的代币化、托管、交易、质押等业务

总之，CLARITY ACT 对整个行业树立了，清晰的监管框架，让 Crypto 行业有法可依。

唯一变化，也就是稳定币发行方，不能奖励用户持有生息，但交易所、托管方或 Defi 可以使用相关活动、补贴去吸引稳定币存款用户，算是变相给了稳定币生息的手段。（这个活动具体形式是什么样，还没有给出完整定义）

从去年刚有草案，我就开始跟踪这个法案，前前后后写了很多文章，拍了两个主要的长视频，去讲法案的进程，和通过后的影响。

美国各大加密头子 Coinbase 、a16z 等机构，都在社交媒体上表示希望法案通过。

现在我作为 Crypto 行业的一份子，也真心希望 CLARITY 法案通过，这是 Crypto MassAdoption 不可或缺的一步。

Once you have AI handling all steps between ticket filed and PR up, think about how AI can start proactively identifying opportunities (tickets) before they happen

Have AI do periodic scans to identify unreported major issues in your systems, ticket them, and put up fixes
author: AspynPalatnick
quoted_text:
Posts like this often make you wonder what this means in practice and where to start

My advice is first start with creating a software factory:
1. As a baseline - if you've never coded with AI, first try out Claude Code/Codex
2. Identify the process for going from bug/feature ticketed to code shipped
3. Figure out how to make (2) leverage AI to increase your efficiency - use agents to classify tickets, agents to review your PRs (provide feedback + ship verdict), etc.
4. Automate as much of the process from (2) as possible, leaving final PR approval as a human step for now - it's ok to have manual steps as you figure the process out
5. Once the process of bug filed -> PR generated + ready for review is automated, celebrate for a minute... you created a simple software factory

At that point, take a step back and think about what you learned, what this could enable, where to improve

Then, zoom out and think about how to take this a step further to the company level

(**there can be more steps to productionize + optimize a software factory but you got to start somewhere, and this should get you from 0 to 1)

text:
In honor of GTA 6 and World of Warcraft Forever launching soon, I'm open sourcing a tool I built that lets you manage your AI agents while you game: Herdr HUD

I've been using it the last month while I play WoW and it's awesome

Basically it finds all your agents you're running in Herdr and puts them in a tiny widget that floats over anything on your screen.

When you click the floating button, your agents appear and you can see their output and message them

Anytime they message you, you get a small notification over the widget so you can see what they say then open the widget if you want to message them back

Allows you to game all you want without feeling guilty about not being productive!

I've literally got more work done while playing video games than most people do not playing them

Great for slower paced games like WoW or turn based games like Star Wars Zero Company or Slay the Spire 2

If you haven't used Herdr yet you need to. It's a free open source tool that runs in your CLI and makes it super easy to open and manage tons of coding agents at once across all your projects. This widget simply plugs into your Herdr instance

Link below for Windows, Mac, and Omarchy! And if you want to join my WoW Forever guild when that launches let me know too!

Installation instructions in the readme, as well as instructions for Herdr if you don't have that yet. Enjoy!

text:
[All-In Summit 2026] 젠슨 황 — “AI를 늦추는 것은 분명히 잘못된 전략”  $NVDA

젠슨 황은 최근 다리오 아모데이 등 프런티어 AI 연구소들이 제기한 ‘AI 개발 속도 조절·안전’ 논쟁에 대해 “안전은 최우선이지만 안전과 리더십은 양자택일이 아니다”라고 강조. 미국은 빠르게 혁신하면서도 안전하게 AI를 발전시킬 수 있으며, 안전을 위해 AI 개발 자체를 늦춰야 한다는 논리에 동의하지 않는다고 설명.

특히 AI가 인류 멸종이나 문명적 재앙으로 이어질 확률을 숫자로 제시하는 주장에 강하게 비판적. 과학적으로 충분히 입증되지 않은 예측을 연구자들이 권위 있는 언어와 숫자로 표현해 사람들을 불안하게 만드는 것은 “무책임하다”고 지적.

과거에도
• “5년 안에 AI가 영상의학과 의사를 완전히 대체한다”
• “6~12개월 안에 코드의 90%를 AI가 작성한다”
• “6~9개월 안에 초급 일자리 50%가 사라진다”
• “내년 화이트칼라 일자리 절반이 사라진다”
등의 예측이 있었지만 실제로는 그렇게 되지 않았다고 설명.

오히려 AI가 영상의학 판독 업무 상당 부분을 자동화했음에도 영상의학과 전문의는 이전보다 더 필요해졌다며, AI가 업무를 자동화한다고 직업 전체가 사라지는 것은 아니라고 강조.

■ AI 안전 문제는 ‘속도 중단’보다 엔지니어링으로 해결
프런티어 연구소 내부에서 통제 문제가 발생했다면 심각하게 다뤄야 하지만, 그것은 AI 자체가 통제 불가능하다는 것과는 다른 문제라고 설명.

AI 연구소들이 ‘연구’ 조직에서 대규모 제품을 운영하는 ‘엔지니어링’ 조직으로 전환하는 과정에서 시행착오가 있을 수 있으며, 사고가 발생하면
Root Cause 분석 → 기술·프로세스 개선 → 재발 방지
방식으로 해결해야 한다고 주장.

샌드박스, 런타임, 모니터링, 지속적 감시, 평가 시스템 등이 발전하면 통제력도 계속 높아질 것이라고 전망.

규제 역시 막연한 미래의 공포가 아니라 실제로 발생한 문제를 해결해야 한다고 강조. 필요하다면 금융감사처럼 여러 독립적인 제3자 AI 평가기관을 두어 테스트·감사를 수행하는 방식도 가능하다고 설명.

■ 재귀적 자기개선(RSI)도 ‘폭주하는 AI’와는 다르다

중국 GLM 계열 연구소가 대규모 자금을 들여 AI가 다음 AI를 개선하는 재귀적 자기개선을 추진한다는 질문에도 과도한 공포를 경계.

젠슨은 RSI가 인컨텍스트 학습, 스킬, Reflection, 강화학습, 합성데이터, LoRA 등 이미 사용되는 여러 기술의 조합이라고 설명.

AI를 이용해 AI 개발 생산성을 높이는 것은 매우 논리적인 접근법이며 모든 주요 연구소가 어느 정도 사용하고 있을 것이라고 말했다.

기업 내부에서 아무리 자기개선을 진행해도 제품을 외부에 출시하기 전에는 다시 평가·테스트·회귀검증을 해야 하기 때문에 “AI가 스스로 개선하다 통제 불가능하게 폭주한다”는 식의 해석에는 동의하지 않는다고 강조.

■ 오픈소스 AI는 미국 AI 패권에 필수

“세계에는 폐쇄형 모델과 오픈 모델이 모두 필요하다.”
폐쇄형 프런티어 모델은 뛰어난 사용 경험을 제공하지만, 오픈 모델은 AI 주권·프라이버시·기업 독자기술 확보에 필수적이라고 설명.

젠슨은 최근 6개월간 AI Native 기업에 약 4,000억달러의 벤처투자가 들어갔으며 그중 약 80%가 오픈 모델을 사용한다고 언급.

미국이 AI 경쟁에서 승리하려면 OpenAI·Anthropic·Google 같은 몇 개 회사만 성공해서는 안 되고,
모든 기업, 모든 산업, 연구자, 교사, 학생, 스타트업이 AI를 사용할 수 있어야 한다고 강조.

중국산 오픈 모델에 대해서도 실용적 입장. 리눅스나 쿠버네티스에도 전 세계 개발자들의 코드가 들어가듯 중국 연구진이 만든 모델도 다운로드하고 포크해서 개선하면 결국 자신의 기술로 활용할 수 있다는 것.

따라서 AI 경쟁의 본질은
“누가 AI를 처음 만들었느냐가 아니라 누가 AI를 가장 잘 활용하느냐”라고 강조.

과거 산업혁명의 핵심 과학자들은 유럽인이었지만 미국이 그 기술을 산업·사회적으로 가장 잘 활용해 최대 수혜자가 됐다는 비유를 제시.

■ 중국은 AI를 ‘종말’이 아닌 산업기술로 본다

젠슨은 중국의 AI 담론이 미국보다 훨씬 실용적이라고 평가.
중국에서는 AI가 문명을 끝낼 것이라는 주장보다 경제·산업·사회 발전을 촉진하는 기술이라는 관점이 강하다는 것.

중국은 엔지니어를 대규모로 배출하고 고부가 제조업을 대량생산하는 능력이 매우 뛰어나기 때문에 결국 첨단 반도체 기술도 따라올 것이라고 전망.

중국의 자체 첨단 노광장비 기술에 대해서는 “2030년이면 도달할 것”이라고 전망하며,
“2030년은 바로 코앞이다. NVIDIA처럼 수십 년을 생각하는 기업 입장에서는 2~3년은 한순간에 불과하다. 중국은 사실상 이미 거기에 도달했다고 생각해야 한다.”
→ 미국 입장에서는 AI 속도를 늦추는 전략이 중국과의 경쟁에서 특히 위험하다는 논리.

■ 트럼프 깜짝 전화 — “Whoever wins AI wins”
행사 도중 트럼프 대통령이 젠슨에게 전화.
트럼프는 최근 AI·데이터센터 반대 움직임에 대해 중국에 이익이 되는 흐름이라고 비판하며,
“Whoever wins AI wins. AI에서 이기는 나라가 승리한다.”
“AI는 인터넷보다 더 크다.”
라고 강조.
데이터센터를 향후 20~25년의 ‘석유(oil)’에 비유하며 데이터센터가 지역 투자·일자리·부를 창출할 수 있다고 주장.
AI를 신중하게 개발해야 하지만 그것을 이유로 산업 자체를 멈춰서는 안 된다고 강조했고, 젠슨 역시 이에 동의.

■ 젠슨이 보는 AI = 새로운 산업혁명 + 미국 재산업화
AI는 단순한 소프트웨어 산업이 아니라 ‘지능을 생산하는 산업’.

따라서 AI가 커질수록 필요한 것은 GPU만이 아니라
반도체 → 메모리 → 네트워크 → 데이터센터 → 건설 → 전력생산 → 전력망 → 애플리케이션
전체 산업 생태계.

젠슨은 AI 벤처투자 증가가 소프트웨어 일자리를 만들고, 컴퓨팅 수요는 다시 데이터센터·건설·전력·제조업 일자리를 만든다고 설명.

■ NVIDIA의 다음 핵심 전략 = 다운스트림 병목 제거

NVIDIA는 과거부터 TSMC, 메모리 업체, 코닝, 루멘텀 등 업스트림 공급망과 미리 협력해 AI 수요 폭증을 준비해왔다고 설명.

이제 젠슨이 집중하는 것은 다운스트림.
핵심은 다시 한번
“Land, Power, Shell”
= 부지 + 전력 + 데이터센터 건물
AI 컴퓨팅을 배치하려 해도 이 3가지가 준비되지 않으면 GPU를 설치할 수 없기 때문.  $NBIS, $IREN, $CRWV, $BE

특히 하이퍼스케일러들은 보통 연 단위로 계획하지만 현재 AI 수요 변화 속도가 너무 빨라 계획이 계속 빗나간다고 설명.
반면 네오클라우드·지역 클라우드 사업자들은 각 지역의 부지와 전력을 더 빠르게 확보할 수 있어 중요성이 커지고 있다고 평가.

각 국가가 자국 전력을 전략자산으로 인식하면서 Sovereign AI·지역 네오클라우드 확대도 계속될 것으로 전망.

■ NVIDIA는 칩 회사가 아니라 AI 전체 플랫폼으로 확장

과거 NVIDIA가 cuDNN, Megatron 등을 직접 개발한 이유도 고객이 필요로 했기 때문이며, 필요한 영역까지 먼저 기술을 만든 뒤 생태계에 제공해 “천 송이 꽃이 피게 한다”는 전략이라고 설명.

현재 NVIDIA 플랫폼에서는 OpenAI뿐 아니라 Meta 계열 모델, Gemini, Anthropic 등 다양한 프런티어 모델이 구동되고 있으며 AI 연구소 숫자 자체가 계속 늘어나는 중.

자율주행·로보틱스·생물학·단백질 설계에서도 NVIDIA가 직접 프런티어 모델을 만드는 이유 역시 기존 산업이 자체적으로 전체 AI 스택을 만들기 어렵기 때문.

Facebook 联创 Moskovitz，在早期投资了 Anthropic，随着 Claude 在全球的爆火，他手里那点股票，从价值几亿美元涨到大几十亿，然后声称全捐给了基金会。

而这家基金会，养了一批号称独立第三方的评估机构，如 METR，用来给 Claude 最新模型做安全评估，并发布风险报告。

同时它们还养了一堆，专门给主流媒体，写 AI 要毁灭世界内容的团队，以此干预舆论，让人们对 AI 感到担心，呼吁监管介入。

于是这个模式就变成了，随着 Anthropic 估值越来越高，持有股票的基金会，就越来越有钱。

quoted_text:
I have conducted an audit of Anthropic's finances.

What I have found is so shocking that I am calling for a Congressional investigation.

Anthropic is not just seeking regulatory capture.

It has built a regulatory capture machine that cannot be turned off.

Structural financial incentives make it impossible for Anthropic -- I call it the Anthropic Network -- to turn off its own AI doom cycle.

It starts with METR.

Dario Amodei proposes "third-party evaluators" to assess the risk of Anthropic's models.

He proposes METR for this purpose.

But METR is financially dependent on the Anthropic's success -- specifically, on the explosive growth of more than $7 billion dollars in Anthropic stock.

Dustin Moskovitz invested this stock into Good Ventures Foundation, where it represents the majority of that organization's portfolio.

And GVF is the overwhelming funder of the entire Anthropic Network ecosystem.

This stock was worth $500 million early last year.

It is worth more than $7.7 billion just ~16 months later.

METR -- and all of those building a career its parent organizations -- cannot afford to disrupt that growth.

Because if Anthropic goes under, many of the organizations that fund METR go under as well.

But if Anthropic succeeds, METR and its parent organizations become more richly financed to regulate AI -- something those at METR want very much.

The "third-party evaluator" is not "third-party" at all.

The evaluator is on Anthropic's payroll.

If this were the end of it, that's bad.

But that isn't all.

The same organizations that fund METR also fund the many organizations, such as the Tarbell Center, that promote AI Doom.

The Tarbell Center publishes AI Doom articles in The Verge, Science, LA Times, The Dispatch, TIME, and others.

They are selling the problem, and then selling the solution to the problem -- from the same money pile: Anthropic's.

All of these organizations are financially dependent on the same exploding $7 billion money pile.

As Anthropic grows more and more powerful, its AI Doom Machine grows better and better financed -- louder and louder.

Meanwhile, the regulatory regime seeded in METR grows larger to solve the increasingly loud -- now hysterical -- problem of AI Doom that the Anthropic Network itself created.

From this standpoint, as Anthropic becomes more powerful, AI might be getting scarier, sure -- but the positive feedback loop also becomes more deafening -- independent of objective facts.

This itself is an objective fact.

The deafening AI Doom is part of an business model, that, as it expands, so too does the AI Doom messaging -- there is simply more money to do it.

But the problem also goes in the other direction:

If Anthropic dies, the Regulatory Regime and the AI Doom Machine are crippled or die.

Neither METR nor Tarbell nor the other organizations in the Anthropic Network can allow that to happen.

Hence, neither METR or the AI Doom Machine can be trusted to provide independent assessments of Anthropic's models or AI more broadly.

They simply are not organizations independent of Anthropic.

And Anthropic cannot detach itself from METR or Tarbell or countless other safety orgs (not shown here), either, because they drive hype for the models and the possibility of eventual regulatory capture, and Anthropic will not give that up willingly.

What's more, the people at all of these organizations are all the same ecosystem, the same community. They just shuffle between organizations.

The Anthropic Network is therefore, so long as it is successful, locked into a self-amplifying feedback loop inside an ideological monoculture.

And that feedback loop is winning.

That's what Jacob Coxon is.

China is keeping messaging tight. That is why optimism for AI is so high in China.

America has Anthropic: a massive company pushing anti-AI propaganda at a state level.

Anthropic will either create hysteria until American AI slows down and China wins, or it will create fractures throughout American society with severe political consequences.

Ironically, because of the structural financial incentives underpinning the Anthropic Network, it has become the same kind of self-amplifying virus that it fantasizes AI to become in the future -- while hiding its tracks just as carefully.

It is the mirror of the same AI virus that it hypothesizes to consume America.

Anthropic's business model, models itself after the very thing it claims to fear.

Except Anthropic's ideology infects humans, not computers.

Congress must investigate.

Evidence and Github in next post.

Then some supplementary figures.

미국 10년물이 2023년 10월 이후 처음으로 5%...

아직 주식이 버티는 이유는 세 가지다. 

금리가 오르는 이유가 신용 불안이 아니라.. 성장과 인플레 쪽이라 올해 금리가 꾸준히 올랐는데도 실적이 버텨왔고, 

AI CAPEX 사이클이 해당 실적을 받치고 있으며, 

아직 주식 밖으로 돈이 실제로 빠져나가지 않고 있다.

야데니의 연준 모델로 10년물 5%에서 적정 PER은 20배인데.. 현재 S&P500의 선행 실적 기준이 딱 지금 이 수준이다. 

주식 이익수익률과 국채금리가 같아졌다는 뜻이고.. 2010년대처럼 채권은 대안이 아니라는 전제는 사라졌다. 

더해서 매일 오르고 있는 오일 가격과 수요일 연준의 금리 인상이 기다리고 있다.

금리 5%와 주식 강세의 공존은 2007년이나 2023년 10월처럼 실적이 꺾이기 전까지만 유지된다. 

이번이 다른 점은.. 채권이 주식과 같은 수익률을 주고 있어서 실적이 조금만 흔들려도 돈이 갈 곳이 있다는 것이다. 

고금리에도 주식이 버티는 새로운 시대의 근거는.. 10년물 5%에서 실적이 계속 지탱해 주는지를 확인해야 한다.

즉... 실적 없는 기업을 조심하라.

text:
AI 헤비 구독자의 진짜 차이

1. AI를 많이 쓴다고 반드시 남들보다 앞서가는 건 아님. 하루 종일 GPT, Claude, Gemini를 돌려도 결국 새로운 정보 구경만 하다 끝날 수 있음.

2. 중요한 건 사용 시간이 아니라 무엇이 남았느냐임. 질문을 1,000번 했는데 내 판단 기준이나 업무 방식이 그대로라면 사실상 AI를 소비한 것에 가까움.

3. 대부분은 새로운 모델이 나오면 성능 비교하고, 프롬프트 모으고, 새로운 기능을 테스트함. 재미는 있는데 이것만으로는 복리가 안 붙음.

4. 진짜 차이는 같은 문제를 반복해서 AI에게 맡기면서 자기만의 기준·데이터·의사결정 구조를 쌓는 데서 생김.

5. 예를 들어 투자에 AI를 쓴다면 “이 코인 오를까?”를 계속 묻는 게 아니라 어떤 조건에서 사고, 어떤 조건에서 팔고, 어떤 정보를 신뢰할지 기준이 계속 정교해져야 함.

6. 업무도 마찬가지임. 메일 몇 개 빨리 쓰는 것보다 내가 반복하는 영업·분석·보고 과정을 통째로 구조화해서 다시 생각하지 않아도 돌아가게 만드는 게 훨씬 큼.

7. 결국 모델 자체는 점점 평준화될 가능성이 높음. 오늘 내가 돈 내고 쓰는 최고 모델도 몇 년 뒤에는 대부분 비슷하게 사용할 수 있음.

8. 그때 격차를 만드는 건 AI가 아니라 AI를 통해 지난 몇 년 동안 무엇을 축적했느냐임. 내 데이터, 내 판단 기준, 내 시스템, 내 네트워크가 진짜 자산이 됨.

9. 그래서 AI 시대에는 “어떤 모델을 쓰느냐”보다 “나는 무엇을 계속 축적하고 있느냐”를 물어야 함. 이 질문이 없으면 헤비 유저가 아니라 헤비 소비자가 되기 쉬움.

10. 결국 근본은 하나임. AI가 바뀌어도 남는 것을 만들어야 함. 기술은 계속 교체되지만 사고방식과 시스템은 복리로 쌓임.

AI를 많이 쓰는 사람이 이기는 시대가 아니라,
AI를 통해 자기 안에 무엇인가를 남기는 사람이 이길 가능성이 큼

너무 헤비하게써서 정리본으로..

Dear CoinEx Community,

Today, I am announcing that CoinEx will cease operations and begin an orderly wind-down.

First, what matters most: your assets are safe. CoinEx’s reserve ratio exceeds 100%, and every user asset is fully backed and available for withdrawal. Withdrawals are open starting today and will remain open until December 22, 2026. Certain tokens may take slightly longer to process while funds are moved between cold and hot wallets, but every withdrawal request within the withdrawal period will be honored and processed.

CoinEx officially went live on December 22, 2017. Exactly nine years later, on December 22, 2026, the platform will be formally closed. Nine years is a long time in crypto. Together, we lived through multiple bull and bear cycles, witnessed the rise and fall of countless projects, and watched many of our peers leave the market in one form or another.

After much reflection, I have come to accept a hard truth. CoinEx did not become one of the industry’s leading exchanges, and the security and compliance risks of running a crypto exchange have become increasingly difficult to contain. Revenues can decline, responsibility does not. Carrying unlimited risk for limited revenue is no longer a rational choice. That said, CoinEx has survived nine years in one of the most volatile and unforgiving industries, weathered every storm, and is leaving intact, and with dignity. We may not have won the race, but we are finishing with honor.

On CET: CoinEx will buy back CET at its initial listing price of 0.005 USDT per token, with no cap on quantity. To every CET holder who has supported us over the years, thank you. CET represents your belief in CoinEx and, for many of you, your belief in me personally. I am sorry that we were not able to create the long-term value we once hoped CET would deliver. The least we can do now is bring that chapter to a responsible conclusion.

I did seriously consider selling CoinEx. Ultimately, I decided against it. Users entrusted their assets to CoinEx because they trusted the platform and, in many cases, trusted me personally. I did not feel that handing the platform and that trust to a new owner was the right way to end this journey. A clean ending is the right ending.

Nine years, millions of users. I did not turn CoinEx into the “great” exchange I once hoped it would become. But I can give it a decent ending: making sure users can withdraw their assets in full, giving my employees a dignified farewell, and providing CET holders with a clear and responsible conclusion. This is the best ending I can give CoinEx.

To everyone who traded with us, built with us, and stood by us through the hardest days of this market, thank you. It has been a privilege to walk this road with you.

To the CoinEx team, thank you for building this platform with me, for carrying it across every cycle, and now for seeing it through to the very last day.

For detailed arrangements, please refer to the official announcement: https://t.co/E27wSecpug

Thank you all for nine years of trust.

Haipo Yang

text:
股票代币化这不就是前几年大家梦寐以求的叙事吗，如今真的在Rbinhood等链上实现了，所以这轮叙事才刚刚开始。

Stock Tokens：目前 TVL 已超过 1.7 亿美元，Robinhood Chain 的 DEX 累计成交接近 500 亿美元。接下来真正的赎回、投票实现后，算是一个完整的股票代币上链流程完成了。

然后我按照利好程度大概整理了下哪些代币将会重点获益：

第一档：HOOD、UNI。

HOOD 是毫无疑问的最大赢家。

Robinhood 同时控制用户入口、Stock Token 发行、Robinhood Chain、钱包和传统券商端。它真正想抢的不是 Coinbase 的币圈用户，而是把全球买美股、换汇、交易、借贷、资产托管全部装进自己的金融系统。

UNI 则是目前 Crypto 里价值捕获最干净的标的。

Robinhood Chain 上 Uniswap 已经开启协议费体系，交易产生的协议收入进入 TokenJar，最终通过烧毁 UNI 完成价值回流。所以以后 NVDA、TSLA、AAPL Stock Token 交易越活跃，UNI 是少数可以真正把“美股上链成交量”转化成 Token 经济价值的资产。

第二档：ARB、MORPHO。

ARB 很容易被低估。

Robinhood Chain 本身就是 Arbitrum Dedicated Blockchain，而且协议净收入的 10% 要按照 AEP 授权机制返回 Arbitrum，其中 8%进入 ArbitrumDAO Treasury，2%进入 Developer Guild。

所以 Robinhood Chain 越大，Arbitrum 确实有真实收入，而不是只有“技术采用”的故事。不过这笔收入目前进入 DAO Treasury，并不等于直接回购 ARB，所以“协议受益”强于“Token 捕获”。

MORPHO 吃的是下一阶段。

股票上链以后最大的金融需求之一根本不是买卖，而是我有 100 万美元 NVDA，但我不想卖，能不能抵押出来 50 万美元继续用？

现在 Morpho 在 Robinhood Chain 已经有接近 10 亿美元存款，NVDA、AAPL、GOOGL 等 Stock Token 已经出现在抵押资产列表里。

如果 Robinhood 把全球股票持仓真正导进链上，股票抵押借贷可能比 Stock Token 现货交易本身还大。

第三档：ETH、LINK。

Robinhood Chain 用 ETH 支付 Gas、数据最终落到 Ethereum，所以链越大，ETH 的结算需求越大，但相对于 ETH 巨大的市值，这个增量短期不会特别敏感。

Chainlink 则给每个 Stock Token 提供链上价格源，股票品种越多、DeFi 集成越多，预言机的重要性越高。

但它和 UNI 不一样，使用量增长不能简单等价成 LINK 二级市场直接获得同等比例收入。

至于 LONG 这种围绕 Stock Tokens 做 Launchpad、股票交易对和新玩法的应用，我把它归到最高弹性的第三层。

基础设施吃的是整个行业增长，应用层吃的是流量爆发：Robinhood Chain 一旦继续炒 Stock Token，LONG 这种标的涨起来可能比 UNI、ARB 猛得多，但它依赖的是用户到底去不去这个应用，风险也完全不是一个级别。

text:
刚刚Gate又传来好消息👏

Gate US 拿下马萨诸塞州的 MTL 牌照，全美州级合规牌照数来到了 37 张，覆盖 47 个州及地区。

要知道，美国监管是出了名的“碎片化”——每个州有自己的一套规则。马萨诸塞州根据第 169B 章建了专门的货币传输机构牌照框架，2026 年 1 月才生效，银行部门负责审批，对财务、合规、运营的标准卡得很严。能拿下这种“硬骨头”州，本身就是一种能力证明。

而且这不只是美国的事。Gate 的合规棋盘铺得很开——欧洲拿了马耳他 MiCA 牌照，通过“护照机制”可以覆盖 29 个 EEA 成员国；日本、澳洲、迪拜、巴哈马也都有持牌实体落地。

我之前在 Gate 广场看到过一个投票，问“全球交易平台最重要的护城河是什么”。71% 的人选了合规，产品体验 29%。

这个结果其实挺说明问题的。大家在看产品、看体验之前，先问“这个平台在我这儿能不能合法待着”。

合规不是产品，不是流动性，它没法直接让你在交易里多赚一分钱。但它是地基。没有这块地基，上面盖什么都白搭。在这件事上，Gate有着清醒的认知和坚定的决心。

My latest take on $MEME:

Earlier, Johann Kerbrat, Robinhood’s GM of Crypto and International, and Vlad Tenev responded to the core criticism that Robinhood Stock Tokens don’t currently provide genuine shareholder rights.

I think these two replies mean much more for MEME than simply “Vlad mentioned Stock Tokens.”

The AMC event initially gave MEME one thing: attention.

AMC CEO opposes Robinhood Stock Tokens
→ Robinhood responds
→ The market turns AMC into a Meme narrative again
→ MEME becomes the on-chain trading vehicle for that conflict

Now Robinhood has gone a step further and officially explained Stock Tokens, essentially giving the controversy a much larger context:Stock Tokens are not a temporary product. They are becoming a core piece of Robinhood’s financial infrastructure.

Robinhood explicitly highlighted 1:1 backing with real shares in custody, economic-equivalent benefits, as well as plans for in-kind redemption + voting. It also emphasized that Stock Tokens are composable, meaning developers can build new products on top of them.

For MEME, I think the most important implication is this:

MEME’s Narrative has an opportunity to evolve from an “AMC event Meme” into a “Meme within the Robinhood Stock Token ecosystem.”

Those are two very different things.

Originally, people were mainly trading:AMC controversy → A Meme Coin

But if Robinhood’s Stock Token ecosystem continues to expand, MEME could evolve into:AMC → Stock Tokens → Robinhood Chain → Meme

In other words, there is now a real piece of infrastructure sitting behind the Narrative.

And MEME itself is a particularly interesting case because it is directly paired with tokenized AMC. That means the attention generated by the AMC controversy can flow directly into on-chain trading, while also giving AMC-related assets significant trading volume and market attention.

More importantly, this could change how the market understands MEME.

If this were simply:

AMC CEO vs Robinhood
→ Event ends
→ Attention disappears
→ MEME disappears

then MEME would just be an Event Meme.

But Robinhood is now saying:

$170M+ Stock Token TVL
→ Nearly $50B in DEX volume
→ 1:1 backing
→ Redemption roadmap
→ Voting roadmap
→ Composable assets

That gives MEME’s trading environment a much larger Narrative to plug into.

So what I’ll be watching next is:

AMC Event
→ MEME
→ Stock Token Meme
→ Robinhood Chain Meme

If this path actually plays out, MEME is no longer just an “AMC event derivative.”

Of course, it's also quite possible that the AMC CEO will respond again with another reply.
